I needed a better way to monitor my symptoms and spot trends over time, so I downloaded Fibromyalgia Tracker. I liked how well-organized everything was, and the app was simple to set up. Having information about sleep and medication in one location was also convenient for me.

This fibromyalgia tracker finally made sense of my bad days. Logging pain, sleep, and triggers takes 30 seconds and the charts show real patterns my doctor actually used. I feel more in control now instead of guessing. The flare warnings help me plan ahead. Simple, accurate, and genuinely useful for daily management.

title: Useful, but recent updates make it worse
body:
I’ve used and appreciated this app for over a year and it has really made a difference. However, I became very used to its system of numbering focus sessions. I track how many I’ve done on a white board, and the numbering system on the app allowed me to double check that I was in the right place with it. 

In an update maybe a month ago, they changed how these numbers worked, so that they no longer reset after two tomatoes, with no setting option to keep it with the old numbering. This wasn’t the end of the world, as I could just reset it myself every two hours. However, the most recent update removes the numbers completely, and I can find no way to get them back. It replaces them with little visual tomatoes instead, which I can’t tell if they indicate halves at all or not. Either way, I and others would really appreciate a toggleable option to use the legacy numbering system. 

I know this is a small thing, but I think it’s the kind of thing that can have a big impact on specifically the groups of people who find this app most useful. I hope this is seen and I want to add that I’m very appreciative the app has as much functionality as it does even on the free tier!!

title: Subscription Model
body: Paid for the app some time ago as a one time purchase. The recent update switched to a subscription model. I understand the developers need to make money for the updates they make, but a subscription model is not the way to go if there are no substantial reoccurring costs beyond the time cost of development. If huge improvements are made and new features are added, I’d rather make another one time purchase. If instead, you had released a v2 separately as a one time purchase (even a much steeper price would have been ok), I would have been more than happy to have bought the new app. I want to make it very clear that subscriptions for apps that run almost entirely locally is not a trend I’m willing to get behind. I don’t blame the developer(s), since this is a common trend, but I also want to make clear to them the loss of a potential sale and the reason why.

My favourite feature is that you can run it in the background so you can still put on a podcast etc while Endel is in the background. 

When I do self care I always have a choice of soundscapes to help me feel more centred and relaxed, and I feel I am more in the moment. 

It’s also great on speakers as background noise, it creates the atmosphere you want and I have found no issues with the current version. 

The ongoing ADHD support has been wonderful as I have been diagnosed with the condition, and I have not used the vast array of tools as much as I have for the more downtime oriented sounds but this app continues to keep giving.

title: Top-quality audio, brilliantly designed
body:
This app is *OUTSTANDING*. It’s clear that a LOT of development has gone into it from the high quality audio to the clear design and user-friendliness. I have naturally gravitated towards using it just about every day for work, relaxation, activity or sleep. It seems to subtly regulate my mood while giving my brain something to keep it occupied and focused.  
I like that the soundscapes can easily be tuned according to user preferences. For example, gentle drumbeats are helpful and sometimes they are irritating, so you can change this. There are also nature sounds, cello and piano tracks in some of the soundscapes. There are some cool modes like “wiggly wisdom” which has sonic landscapes with spoken inspirational messages. If you are playing the app fullscreen (which I have tested, works seamlessly across Mac computer, iPhone and iPad), different modes have very cool, mesmerising black-and-white line animations. The coloured noise mode has little motes of coloured dots floating around on the screen, accompanied by a tunable coloured noise soundscape. 

I love the gentle way that the sounds match my movement when I’m going out for a walk. It always feels like they are following and matching my movement rather than pushing me, which leads to a greater sense of relaxation. There is some very clever programming behind this. Even if you think you don’t like ambient music, I would recommend trying this, because the soundscapes are designed based on research that demonstrates their effectiveness – even if you’re not conscious of it. Do I *love* this app? YES I DO! 😍

As for the content provided, the routines could use more variety. A more upbeat focus option would be great. Think a dance/techno kind of vibe.

title: Shows promise but not quite there yet
body: I’m a current paying subscriber, and I don’t regret that. The sleep soundscape is perfect for me and is the kind of thing I’ve been trying to find in other apps with no meaningful success. But the interface needs some rethinking. It’s *pretty*, but it’s not immediately clear what anything is or how to navigate out of it once you realize the feature you tapped isn’t what you wanted. You can’t tune the sound on every soundscape, and that’s frustrating. I don’t know what Autoplay does, and I can’t find anything about it in the user guide. I mean, it seems like it just replays the last thing I listened to, but I’m honestly not sure. I wish I had a way to create my own sleep soundscape with a combination of sounds already in the app and to assign those sounds to specific phases (activation, onset, etc) from a menu of sounds Endel recommends for those phases. The ui within each soundscape almost makes it look like you should be able to do that, but it turns out those icons are just yet another menu for the overall app. There’s good stuff here, but it’s fairly limited even for subscribers, and it looks complicated for what little it offers, even if what it offers is actually pretty good.

title: Helps me
body:
After falling prey to an ad, I signed up for the free trial. After discontinuing the subscription before I was charged, I felt myself wishing I had kept it. I tried substituting with other music options…YouTube Music, Apple Music, Spotify, Pandora…I ended up going back to this and reinstating my subscription. 
When I have to focus in spite of constant interruptions, this is perfect. Washing dishes, working in my office job, and doing laundry are examples where it has proven most useful. The beats get a bit louder when I’m in the midst of loud things-like when pots and pans make a racket or when there is a ruckus at work. I can still easily hear around me when I need to, but it really does help calm my anxiety and also acts like rails on a go-cart track keeping me focused on my work. 
I primarily have used the sleep, focus, and…recovery? When I wear my sleep headphones (flat cheap things that are in a headband,) the automatic alarm wakes me up and suggests something…but I don’t recall what it is at the moment…but it is really nice…it may be recovery, but it’s definitely nice to wake up to. 
So…five stars. Would recommend.

title: Kaleidoscope of sounds
body:
A beautiful app to aurally tailor your daily activities. There is no lack of selection as they’ve been steadily introducing new soundscapes alongside a few knobs and dials for customization since its inception.

It’s definitely heavy on the pricing, perhaps too much so, but others like I have found value in Endel’s vision of a well-integrated audio relief companion and reaped its benefits profoundly.

---
To that, I’m hoping the devs can:

1. Improve the automation & scheduling functions of Endel, as the current “Routines” only serve as a glorified notification

2. Bring the desktop app to feature parity (for those who want to stay disengaged with their phones during work) and more accessibility to the timer and soundscapes with keyboard shortcuts

There is so much more room to grow, and I’m excited to see what the team has in store next!

title: My favorite app
body: Endel has quietly become an essential part of my daily routine. The sleep soundscapes are incredibly calming, helping me unwind almost instantly. I especially appreciate the subtle tuning—it feels personalized, like the sounds are in sync with my own rhythms. The study mode keeps evolving, too. It strikes that rare balance: not distracting, yet never dull. There’s real craft here. It’s not just background noise—it’s an ambient engine for focus and rest.

title: Soundtrack Your Sanity
body:
Imagine it’s 2:17 AM. The dog’s chasing ghosts, the fridge is humming like it’s possessed, and you’re just trying to exist. You think, “Music might help,” but every playlist either wants to party, cry, or preach. That’s when I learned: sometimes, music is not the vibe. Sometimes, you need Endel.

Endel doesn’t blast bangers—it reads the room, your body, and maybe your soul, and gives you a soundscape that feels like your brain got hugged. Studying? Cooking? Existential spiral while folding laundry? Endel says, “Say less,” and tailors a sonic backdrop that just fits. No lyrics, no decisions, no DJ anxiety.

It’s now my go-to when I want to feel something without feeling too much. Like sonic incense for your mood. Endel doesn’t just play sounds—it calibrates your chaos.

The app itself works fine but has left a bad taste in my mouth regarding the poor customer service. I tried requesting a refund through Apple, was denied, then tried through Paypal. I have been denied both times, saying “product delivered” but I never even wanted to buy it in the first place. If you download this, be sure to set reminders and timers to cancel it because Endel will not do that for you. Feels like they’re a predatory app, but 🤷🏻‍♀️

title: A Helpful Balance during the Healing Process
body: I have been struggling with my mental health for awhile now. I meditate often and it seems to be one of the only things to help me. I have a hard time finishing things, staying present in the moment, and maintaining a higher vibration. I open the app when I’m losing focus, or my energy is off and I’m no longer finding/or I’m losing my mental peace. I can only share my experience as it pertains to me; this app has helped me in ways that only a spiritual and therapeutic approach have worked. I open the app when I’m doing dishes, working out, while at work, etc. and it always pulls me back to the present. I accomplish the things that I start, and I do it gracefully(rather than rushing). To think a simple melody can change the trajectory or my moments is pretty crazy- but I’ve notice the world is a pretty crazy place... I’ve been using the apps free trial, and I’m not one to have many subscriptions-but I will be subscribing to this app monthly. I’m grateful for this app. I’m grateful for the peace in which it brings me and then energy within myself that it can help me to redirect. If you’re reading this, I hope you give it a genuine chance and I hope you gain something from within yourself by using it- above all, I hope we all heal.

title: I was skeptical
body:
As someone who struggles with their ADHD and can become easily overstimulated I was initially looking for a white noise generator and found this app. 

I was surprised to find that I had a variety of white noise, brown noise, beats other settings to help you focus depending on the task at hand. 

I have now found myself using this daily. I usually focus timer to break up work that requires me to be focused for a long period of time or to break up tasks that I don't really want to do.

For example if I need to do laundry, clean my bathroom, Vacuum, or other chores I set the timer for seven minutes with three minute breaks over 6 cycles (1hr). The soundscape keeps me on pace and then it almost becomes a game to see if I can complete the task within seven minutes. Then I rest for the three minutes by watching TikTok videos or answering text messages etc.  

I use the sleep timer every night, and I've noticed that I am asleep within five minutes, I use the timer feature and have it automatically turn off after one hour to save battery.  

I had no expectations with this app, and it has been surprisingly useful. I only gave four stars because I can't save custom "sound blends".  the app lets you customize the intensity and beat of each soundscape, which is awesome. I wish that I could save it  for certain tasks.

title: Price Gouging
body:
Screen 1 prompts you to pay $10/mo. Doesn’t even tell you what you’re getting. Just “7x Productivity.” Great thanks. Cancel. 

Screen 2 says “wow you unlocked a crazy low price of $3/mo!”

So $3 is the real price, $10 is just the fake anchor that some poor souls are paying.

And even at the $3 “deal,” the purchase screen says nothing about what you get. Why??? This feels so antagonistic for an onboarding experience.

Also, the design is pretty, but distracting. I’m sitting here on the “Start Focus” screen and some full-screen animation is twitching all over the place. It’s meaningless lines, and screams the opposite of “focus.” 

Takes multiple taps to change a sound. Why can’t I just play the Rest soundtrack instead of selecting an untitled button to see what soundtrack it is, read a full-screen popup, then choose to “Start Rest?” That first meaningless line icon could have a label. 

Idk, it must just not be for me.

The soundscapes help focus my mind, or provide a pleasant backdrop despite living in a very busy city.  @WORK I use the ADHD Pomodoro-style timer in the app.  It works great, and is much more pleasant than just a timer.  There are many options for sounds.  A new feature (they are constantly updating) is distraction blocking which links with the iPhone’s focus/screen time modes, highly customizable but you can set it to auto stop notifications during focus periods for example.  @SLEEP Every night I have Endel’s “Wind Down” scheduled to autoplay on my Amazon Echos near the bed.  (Part of that same routine also dims & turns off lighting).  When I’m ready the sleep soundscape is initiated and it’s time to sleep.  If I do wake up at night, the sounds transition to a low warm hum (like a monk vocalizing) that indicates it’s still sleepy time, go back to sleep.  @READING/RELAXING the sounds are great and provide a good backdrop.  I also play Endel when taking a bath, rejuvenating both body & mind.  @MOVE is an interesting soundscape and it is great for a walk or even driving.  If you didn’t know, all of this automatically syncs to your Apple Watch’s Health data, so it knows when you wake up / fall asleep and what your heart rate is (if you choose to share all of that).  It modifies the soundscape to be *in tune with each step you take* as you walk.  If nothing else, this entire app is a genius-stroke of design and integration.  It works on almost every platform, Amazon Echo, Apple Everything, PC, etc etc.  It absolutely deserves to be on every recommendation list.

title: Lack of Focus AND Sleep  👎🏼
body:
Don’t get sucked into paying $120 for this dumb, creepy app. I bought it, thinking it would be a way to cope with ADHD. It was not.  😵‍💫

The focus sounds are like a horror film’s heartbeat soundtrack. They did NOT—in any vague sense of the words—“relax” or help me “focus.” It was like being in an Edgar Allen Poe tale with a giant heartbeat pounding in my ears. Adderall calms me down, but whoever or whatever “Endel” is, it ain’t my Chamomile cup of tea. No offense to Estonians—as apparently the name Endel has its origins there—but this app was a complete and total failure for me. 

The sleep sounds are so busy/buzzy they’re like caffeine. As I lay staring at the ceiling, bloodshot Tex Avery looking eyes wide open, I could only wonder how Endel was getting these unknown app awards decorated with palms. Palms always make things look official, I thought to myself at 3am.

So I gave up. I returned to playing ocean sounds at night on the HomePod and Baroque classical music during the day to help me focus.

But the worst part?

There was no way to get a refund from Apple! 

I still had 9-10 months on my one-year subscription and thought I’d at least get a prorated refund. But Apple said “No way,” and the supervisor I rose through the ranks to speak to only offered to send me the Apple Terms and Conditions. I politely said, “No way. Nobody reads those, man, and that’s a mean thing to say.”  He sent them anyway. 

I love Apple products and have been a believer for a long time, long before Apple became cool or the biggest publicly traded company in the world. I’ve spent many tens of thousands of dollars on hardware and software for myself and my family. This was an extremely disapointing experience and I’m bummed Apple couldn’t have my back. 

In the meantime, don’t waste your time or a single dime on this unkind app that will not help you unwind at bedtime or find focus in the daytime. 

👎🏼

title: Incredibly helpful
body:
I tried Endel in the hope that it would help me concentrate a little better. There are a lot of sound apps out there, and I honestly expected this app to be similar to one of those. Helpful, but really just a convenient way to play focus music. 

Instead, I’ve found that Endel has not only helped me focus but the new exercises are helping me to be more calm and relaxed too.

The design of the app is really nice and I appreciate that it adapts to my day.

The only thing I think could be improved is that I find that it’d not really adapting to my activity (walking, working etc), more to just the time of day. If I don’t have to manually switch away from auto play throughout the day, that would make it even better.

However recent changes to the sleep sound are making it harder for me to get to sleep (perhaps too many random wailing noises, ambient noise only is too quiet), so an option to revert to the old sound would be appreciated. Even if it is a particular tuning setting. As things stand I probably need to stop using it.

Edit: Updated rating while feedback is being worked on

My only suggestion:

title: The Only App that has worked for me
body: As a university student, I’ve noticed significant improvements in my mood and productivity since using this app. The Relax and Focus modes have helped me stay on track with my studies while also giving me the ability to unwind. I’m using the free version, and while it’s effective, I have to give it four stars because of the 10-minute time limit per channel for free users. It’s disappointing since it used to be unlimited, but overall, this app truly delivers on its promise.

title: Flawed app spoils promising concept
body: I’ll keep this brief. The soundscapes are generally well designed but the app has serious  flaws which will probably not become apparent during the short 7 day free trial period. At then end of that period you will be pushed towards an annual subscription. I would recommend against taking it. I did not follow my own advice and since then have been let down on several occasions. Examples include being woken up an hour and a quarter before my scheduled alarm, sleep mode failing to kick in at bedtime and the watch app failing to accurately show the energy levels determined by the phone app.

title: Huge help in calming and focusing
body: I’ve loved Binnaural Beats and sounds aligned with energy frequencies for a long time. However, there’s something Endel has that’s different. I don’t know what it is but I do know it works. I am rapidly able to focus, feel a lift, or a down shift whenever I tune in to my experience and select a sound track. Not having changes every few minutes is soothing. A friend with ADHD recommended it, and I’ve since recommended it too. Well worth the money.

body: Be very careful when you opt for the free trial. I am sure I selected the free trial for 7 days and was then prompted by the £59.99 charge. title: Big time fan… no longer :(
body: Been using Endel and recommending to all my friends and family for years now. I’ve loved using it nightly and I literally do not go to sleep until I’ve put my sleep mask on and turned the sleep music on. I will be reverting back to my old Spotify sleep playlist unfortunately due to the new ten minute timer and forced subscription service. I have also used Endel for the focus mode in the past when studying, and found it helpful; I have also tried the free trial of the previous premium level service, however did not find enough extra features to warrant the price. Over the years I have been using Endel, I have not noticed a huge amount of change or development. For this reason I think it is maybe not by choice that the company behind this app have chosen to remove almost every feature that I have been loyal to for the past however many years I’ve used it for (in the app it actually says I’ve been with Endel for 966 days, and according to my last weeks “insight”, spent 2,937 mins using the app, “putting me in the top 3% of users). title: Pomodoro Productivity

I like the apps simple design and layout, unintrusive. I haven't used all its features yet, for example the Activity audio, but the sleep and focus audio is really effective.

However, a few features that would improve things for me:
- Can the IOS version of the app please support chromecast, not all of us are tied into the apple eco system, other audio based apps for IOS support both options. Have tried using the bluetooth with chromecast speakers but often find this disconnects randomly, possible bug with nest speakers.
- Can the 'focus timer' be added to the the mac desktop app, there is a timer but you have to reset it for each session, for the pomodoro time its good to commit to a number of rounds up front, otherwise its an extra distraction to restart.
- I'm on the student pricing currently which is generous for £16, feel like £60 a year would be a little too much otherwise, there are many apps that compete at this price point that are likely to be needed over this one if I was to make cuts. For £36 a year / £5 a month it would be a no brainer.

title: More of a computer app than anything else
body:
The app name tells you you should be able to do two things: use a timer and keep track of tasks. The first one is ironically hard to do on the Apple Watch, and the second one is hard to do on either AW or iPhone...

On the phone, it tries to do too much, or is at least not intuitive at what it does. Basically there's no home screen outside of the timer, and different functions are hidden in a menu that looks like a sidebar but works like a website with hyperlinks. The timer settings hidden under your profile, the graphs are hidden behind an icon on the top right, and the calendars you have to switch between by going back and forth to the menu. And really it's not a menu because your projects or for some reason listed there too.
The timer works, but the live activity widget seems to use a lot of battery and cannot be paused/resumed without unlocking your phone.

On the AW, it doesn't do enough. You can't start a task if you didn't already set it on another device, and it takes some time to sync those. You could start an unlabeled pomodoro, but you'd later have to label your sessions on another device. You can also only see the today menu so can only look at and do those tasks.

All that said, I think the biggest con is that the actual timer itself doesn't give you an alert on your watch (!!!) I don't know if Apple is making this difficult for developers but for some reason there is not AW app that does pomodoro well, which you'd think would be the perfect device for it!

title: Cannot use without two-way sync with Reminders
body:
I love the Moleskine productivity suite. I LOVE it passionately; it’s beautiful, intuitive, and dynamic, but I cannot use this set of apps for exactly one reason: I need a two-way sync with Apple Reminders. It is non-negotiable. I canceled my last subscription because of it and was very disappointed to see it has still not been implemented. I love this set of apps, but it is literally completely unusable to me because of this one flaw. 

Without this two-way sync, I cannot assign tasks to other people or share tasks/lists with other people, nor can I track other people’s progress on tasks. I can’t use Apple Reminder triggers that aren’t available in Moleskine. I can’t easily move a task from one platform to another. It’s such a shame. I love this set of apps, and it’s amazing to me that despite the consistent and unrelenting feedback from end users about the need for this two-way sync, Moleskine chooses to continue biting the hands that feed.

title: Decent overall
body:
Pros
1. Pretty easy to organize with how the app allows you to structure tasks into different lists
2. Good ability to manipulate the ordering of tasks with dragging to position.

2. Display is simple and easy to understand. 

Cons - just some extra steps that could be eliminated for increasing the simplicity of using the app. The cons are not bad enough to not buy the app. 
1. When adding new tasks the order is displayed as last task created to first. So if you wanted to add tasks in order of completion, it will display them backwards. This requires additional steps of dragging tasks to their proper place in the sequence. 
2. If you want a task to have a time written before the name of the task (4pm Dr. appointment), the app will automatically assign the time to the reminder part and remove it from the name. So you will have to create the task, save it, go out, open it, and then type in the time in the name, and then save.

If you hit the Trashcan icon your item/changes disappear. Makes sense. (No Are you sure? though)

If you hit the button that makes your iPad keyboard go down your changes disappear.

You can also set up a bedtime schedule where it blocks all apps and websites. It provides an informative dashboard detailing approximately how much time you saved. However, I really can’t get behind the modern era of subscription based apps. Especially for the lifetime license costing a whopping FIFTY dollars, and SEVENTY for a “family plan”. I don’t have any problem supporting independent developers and paying for software, but I personally feel like this is overpriced for what it does. Most of it is just relying on the iOS shortcuts functionality anyway, and all the app is doing is showing a pretty GUI and recording the time. You could replicate something similar in shortcuts (although not entirely, like website blocking for instance.) If you don’t mind the cost, go for it, but I would probably pay $15 maximum for a lifetime license, not $50. Especially considering many people using this are likely college students.

But I would still recommend this app for shorter breaks.

I also want to mention that the settings are complicated and hard to set up. I have a PhD, but this app made me feel intellectually limited because of how tricky the settings were. I have adhd, maybe it’s just not compatible with my brain. That said, the app creator very graciously walked me thru the settings and they clearly do want to help people figure it out (there are tutorials etc).

title: A must-have
body:
I can't remember the last time I felt so strongly compelled to write a positive review.
I don't consider myself to have a problem with doom scrolling or screentime for the most part, but I have one digital vice - YouTube. I have premium and it's probably my favourite entertainment platform.
I noticed that my Screentime was creeping up over time into numbers that I wasn't comfortable with.
With all other apps I was wasting time with and knew they werent bringing me any value, I simply deleted them, cold turkey, about a year ago and have no regrets. But YouTube felt different, I do get genuine value from it whether that be entertainment, educational or practical. The problem was the volume and lack of intentionality.
Although it's early days I can whole heartedly say that one-sec has completely changed the dynamic and feels like the perfect solution I was missing all this time. In just one week my Screentime reduced by 45% while feeling like I wasn't even trying. Through a combination of blocking schedules and interventions, the frequency and duration I spend on YT has dropped dramatically and I can feel better habits forming already.
Often you really do only need the intervention, but I do like having the scheduled block features to stop me from checking work apps when I'm off the clock.
As others point out, the setup is a bit unconventional and less straightforward than some of the alternatives. But it is absolutely worth it, and the instructions are still clear enough.
More than happy to pay the modest annual fee for such a high-impact and well thought out experience.

title: My second time reviewing - milestone achieved
body:
This app has changed my life, and got me my most valuable asset back: 

My time.

Since May 2023, I have saved 4.3 weeks of SCREEN TIME on Instagram, and another couple weeks across multiple different social media’s.

Across the board, I have saved 1.4 MONTHS of screen time. Just think about that for onesec (excuse the pun) 

Overall ‘app opening’ preventions currently sit at 19,701. 

In fact, my milestone has now been achieved:

The blockers were genuinely so annoying to bypass, I started to get frustrated and it clearly conditioned my brain to resent the app in question that was being blocked, in this case, Instagram. I have now uninstalled Instagram, and I can say confidently that I am much happier without it. 

You actually realise after you don’t have some of these apps that their presence in your life is meaningless, and they literally give you zero value.

The only social media app I could justify using is “X”, which I still have yet to even use, but it’s a platform of free speech and uncensored content so that you can make your own informed decisions about the world without being reliant on mainstream media. Again, just make sure you have the blockers in place & re-interventions (stops you from doomscrolling / getting you into rabbit holes for hours) 

Nevertheless, it’s actually quite scary to think that some of us can’t live without social media. It used to be me. 

The truth is, whether or not you have social media on your phone, the world keeps spinning. It’s up to you to decide what you do with your time as it spins. 

I trust you’ll make the smart decision that I did back in May last year. Install the app and get your time back. 
 
Massive thank you to the developers, hopefully one day I’ll meet you and treat you all to a drink. 

Alex
United Kingdom 
24/09/2024

title: IS THE TEAM AI NOW? 1 star because I can’t give 0!!!!
body:
I have been a loyal subscriber since 2021. But since they destroyed their UI in Nov 2021, and after my experience communicating with the team, my subscription will end today. This app is a complete waste of time and money, and the team have not fixed errors that I have been requesting for 6 months. When I initially was in contact with the team at breathwrk regarding the issues with the new version of the app, they were responsive and engaged with my feedback, but nothing that they said they would do have they followed through on 6 months later. The post workout session has been broken for 6 months and I have emailed them 3-4 times about it. But recently, the replies have seemed to be automated responses, when I emailed about the post workout session still not working (4 months after notifying the team of it not working, which they said they would fix within a week) I received a reply saying that I was having difficulty logging in and telling me how to log in??? I emailed them back to say that is not what I was asking about and they have not at all replied since. This series of events leads me to believe that they have replaced at least some of their team with AI, while continuing to charge the same price of $15/month, all while the app is a shell of what it once was. 
In communicating with the team  earlier this year, I spent several hours of my time giving feedback. They had asked me to provide this feedback and as I hoped that I would be able to continue to use the app, I spent enough hours on it that the work would be worth 6 months of subscription when measured against my country’s minimum wage. I did not expect compensation, but as I told them much about my loyalty to the app despite my financial struggles due to chronic illness, I would have appreciated some acknowledgment or gratitude or in the very least that they do what they said that they would.
They have not implemented anything that they said they would. This used to be my favourite app. I have been a subscriber for 4 years. I will now be ending my subscription as I cannot justify the continued $15/month for an app that doesn’t work, a dev team that doesnt fix or do anything, and comms that I can’t even trust to be a person that I’m talking to. At this point for the price you pay they are thieving their customers hard earned money for less than 10% of the services and benefits that the previous UI offered. Shame on the owners of this app.

title: The Newest Update Ruined the App
body: I’ve been using Breathwrk for years. It has been one of my favorite apps. Some updates have been better than others, but it was always my go to app if I was feeling overly stressed, for a midday reset, or if I wanted to skip my nightly meditation for something a bit quicker. However, this newest update has completely changed the app and has rendered it virtually unusable. Now it seems like a grift that wants to ask you a million questions and run breathing diagnostics to curate a specific experience. This would be great except that now the sound and visual aspects are often out of sync, the timer glitches so what should be a 6 second inhale becomes a 12 second or 3 second inhale, and now the app won’t even let you get passed the setup section without signing up for a payment plan. In the past it was always free for the basics, and you could pay for more advanced breathing techniques. The first time I dealt with the paywall I was able to circumvent it somehow, but as I said the app itself is now awful and it looks cheap and barebones. I have never written a review for an app before, but I feel pretty frustrated that an app that I’ve using for years to help manage anxiety has greatly diminished its functionality while simultaneously requiring payment for the first time. Try any other breath work app, and don’t waste your time with this.

All your records (sorry, they have a breath number) and interactions are gone. There’s no logic, no cohesiveness, just a complete amateur of an app.   They have saving buttons for specific exercises but nothing saves once you close the app. Nothing works anymore just complete GARBAGE! How in the world can someone, go from a perfect tool - literally and with not an ounce of exaggeration - to such a useless and horrible app? Live and learn!

title: Time to find a new app
body: Really bummed wit he the update? I really like the optima for the breathing symbols. Like the wave or animal. App looks modern and lacks character now... I'm sure it will stop having free features and limits on daily free usage. Super bug bummer and I use this like 25 times a day to help my tachycardia.

title: Worst update i’ve ever seen in my life
body: ugly ui, no preset timer options, no finish sound, this might be the worst update in all of app store history

title: preferred the old style
body: idk much else to say other than i preferred the old way the app was, everything about it is just more abrasive with the updates, more emphasis on payments, less choices, and customizing - i miss the app that just had different breathing exercises  based what im feeling without having to pay $50 a year

title: NOT WORTH IT
body: Deceptive messages to charge you more. They offer free trail but they don't respect it and charge you the full year. And the app doesn't even work well. Be careful! I’ve sent 3 mails already and got 0 responses. Terrible!

title: Disappointing Update
body: This app used to be my go-to for relaxation, but the update ruined it. The peaceful design is now a cold, cluttered mess, and the black theme is awful, it’s the opposite of calming. Even the sounds aren’t soothing anymore. Really disappointed. Time to find a better app.

title: Terrible New Update
body: This used to be my go-to app for breathing exercises. The animations were simple and the sounds were very soothing. I opened it for the first time in a couple weeks and it looks and sounds totally different. The sounds are terrible now. Not relaxing at all. The look of the app went from simple and cute to cold and tech-y with splashes of unnecessary motivational quotes. Why does every health app need quotes? I really miss the well-designed simplicity of their previous rendition. It was perfect and it felt happier. Even their new logo is overly conceptualized. Very disappointing and unfortunate update. Time to look for a new app 😒

title: New Update Ruined It
body: I LOVED this app. It helped me sleep and with calming.  But, unfortunately, they just released an update that turned it into a robotic app. The audio guides only say “In, Out, Hold” period. They used to say things like “relax into a sense of peace” and they actually sounded like real people instead of computer-generated voices. And the options for the blue waves are gone - they changed it to circular animations that don’t even match the in, hold, and out breaths in like a brownish gold/yellow, but they took away the options to choose those. So disappointing. Canceling :(

title: Never gained full access - zero support!
body: I contacted Breathwrk (through ‘contact us’ in app) twice asking for help because my app only let me use the initial screen.  I was excited to explore meditations and would’ve strongly considered a year paid membership but I never received a response from Customer Service after either attempt.

title: Beware Bait-and-Switch Scam
body: Shocked this is on the appstore.  Bait-and-Switch Scam.  You must pay for a subscription to test the app.  After I paid, I noticed that the app was hardly working.  When contacted for a refund, customer service noted its policy to not refund post payment.

title: Beware of being charged twice
body: I got this app and as usual you can try it out for 7 days. Before my 7 days was up, I received a message indicating that I can purchase the app for $29.99 instead of $49.99 and I went ahead with the lower price. I didn’t cancel after the 7 days. I then noticed that I was charged twice once at $49.99 and another at $29.99. When I called the Apple support they indicated that I am paying for the pro version of the app at $49.99 and the regular at $29.99. I have yet to find the difference between the two. This is unethical! In addition, how can an app that I purchased to help me reduce stress cause more stress! I now need this app to help calm me down with their breathing exercises. What a ripoff to have to pay over $70 annually for an app!

title: One more thing we now have to pay for
body: This app was great and you could still access a few free features and not have to pay for everything but of course capitalism rules and now we have to pay to access the app. Everything’s about money.

title: Pay or this?😂😂😂😂😂😂😂. It's a joke!
body: Paying for a clock is really irresponsible when you have 5 of them one you're holding right now. This app doesn't relax you. It's a cash grab for people who don't understand pranayama. It's counter intuitive. And then they guilt trip you for telling the truth.

title: Loads blurry
body: After I created an account the app went blurry. Couldn’t swipe or proceed. Forced closed it. Delete and reinstalled app. Restarted phone. Completely unusable.

title: HORRRRRIBLE Customer Service
body: Needed to update my Credit Card, but forgot my password to login on their website. It’s 2025 and they have to be the ONLY service that doesn’t offer resetting your password on their site. Ridiculous. So I have sent THREE email to them and it’s been almost 3 weeks and ZERO response. Nice way to treat subscribers who have been with you for a few years. No need to contact me you lost a loyal subscriber. And your update had made the App a complete joke.

title: Hate the changes
body: Where are all the shorter exercises? That’s what kept me going! Where is the cute monkey? Longtime fan, but I dunno if I’ll stick with the new version.

title: Poor Customer Service
body:
I tried to sign up for a free 3-month trial with a program I bought through Bodi.  I wasn’t able to do that and emailed Breathwrk customer service on February 18, 2025 after I purchased the app without the 3-month trial.  I also sent them a message through their app the next day.  As of today, I have yet to receive any response.  

I will say I do like the Breathwrk exercises.  I haven’t explored much beyond that, but the breathing exercises do calm and balance me.

title: Update ruined app
body: I’m sad i paid for another year of the app especially because they upped the price for worse performance. It’s buggy.. it doesn’t sync with Apple Health anymore and the actual guidance and education components are missing! I can’t read descriptions of what each exercise is meant to do, some have it some don’t. The visuals that say whether to breathe through your nose or mouth disappear after 1 breath. They keep getting this feedback and say they want to improve but nothing changes. Went from my favorite app to one I barely open. Will cancel subscription for next year.

title: Subscription
body:
Looks to be a good app, however it requires a very expensive subscription.

There is no reason this needs a subscription. Look for any other app.

title: Great, until….
body:
The previous app was pretty great! Loads of info and great ways to streak your way to a healthier lifestyle. The only flaw in my opinion was, if you forgot your phone at home, but did your breathing exercises anyway, there was no way to keep a streak going by adjusting it manually. Sad. The updated app not only lost all my data, streaks and preferences, it’s so obtuse it’s almost useless. I accidentally signed out after day 4, it started me all over again. Where are the holding your breath and exhale exercises? Plus, I don’t think I understand some of what the info is telling me: at the top it says 116 Streak. But the opening splash page says I’m on a 44 day streak?  Lastly, the calendar is, well, 
 just a calendar. It doesn’t show any information. 
I’ve since been using Breathing Zone. It’s simple, but I can at least see my history.

title: Sigh
body: I used to really love this app but with the new update the breathing doesn’t sync up :(

title: Update made it worse
body: It’s strange to call yourself the number one breathing app and then release an update that limits functionality, introduces more noticeable bugs, and makes it harder to find and save exercises. The new layout feels less organized—almost like a knockoff of apps that were already worse than Breathwrk. As a paying user, I don’t necessarily need the old UI back, but an update should improve the experience, not make it worse.

title: Update messed it up
body: This was an excellent app before the update with more flexibility and options.  The update messed it up. Barely usable now. Wish they would go back. Will likely cancel my subscription after it expires.  Support never replied to comments and questions.

title: Used to love this app
body:
I don’t know why y’all changed the features of this app so much but sadly they don’t make it better. In fact when I downloaded it after not using Breathwrk for a while, I wasn’t even sure it was the same app. The colors feel depressing in my opinion and the whole interface is completely different. I cannot track my goals the way I used to and the lung capacity tests seem to be completely gone. Plus the sounds you have to accompany the breath patterns are glitchy and I don’t enjoy as much as the former ones. 
This still is the easiest and streamlined app I have tried for breath exercises. That is why I am sticking with it in hopes that you will be updating it soon and potentially bringing back some of the wonderful aspects the older version had.

title: Don’t pay for this
body: I thought paying for it would give me more options for the breath types or more on what they’re for - nope! It basically just unlocks classes. DO NOT PAY FOR THIS. It’s totally not worth it

title: Broken
body: Doesn’t seem to work properly since update.

title: Beautiful UI isn’t Enough
body: I've had Breathwrk for many years, with the subscription and free plans. In versions from two years ago or more to now - the app has been loved by me for it's minimalistic aesthetic, ease of use, and it's focus on the beloved namesake. With those details, I equally have full disdain for the über lack of keeping streaks. I wrote a review to Breathwrk before but to see the problem on Premium still, years later, is wild. I also wish there was an option to receive 2-3 free streak days in Premium and then we'd have to deduct points or pay to keep the streak without doing the work. Also, why was the favorites tab removed? Who wants to always see your suggested options and not their own saved ones? Scrolling through them all is cumbersome unless I'm missing where to find favorites...The app having these issues and me losing streaks makes me not want to use it even though it's great for mental health. Regardless, thank you to the developers & code writers.

title: Miss the monkey
body:
I liked this app a lot when it had the monkey and those cute visuals for timing breath hold and doing the exercises.

The new UI feels dated and not as inviting.  Still like having an app to help count breaths, but wish it felt more playful again or brighter instead of the dark look.  Also can you no longer do the breath hold timers?

title: Best yet but buggy
body: This is by far the best breathing app I’ve used. I wanna start off by first saying that. However, I have two issues with it. The first is that the visualizations become out of sync with the breathing cycle on longer exercises. You’ll see the visualization constricting as you’re supposed to be exhaling sometimes it only halfway before contracting. There’s no good reason for an issue like this on an app that cost this much. The second thing is much less of an issue and more of a request. I’d like to see integration with Apple health meditations.

title: Stability issues
body: Hangs quite a bit at the end of the session.

title: Poor Changes
body: This app really was a nice part of my routine and daily habits, as I used it to start my day refreshed and to end it calmly. Unfortunately, the funnel toward the subscription payment in the redesign has been quite annoying.

title: Buggy and bad customer service
body: The app itself is good and I liked the simplicity of the exercises and functionality. The calendar tracking failed to switch over to 2025 in January. After purchasing a full plan during my trial, my account never updated to show the purchase. I emailed my receipt and screenshot of my account to customer service who told me I was using the wrong email to log in. I wasn’t and when I told them that they (again) said to make sure I was logging in correctly. When I asked for a refund they ghosted me. I had to reach out again a few days later and was then issued a refund.

title: Downhill
body: I have been a regular user for the last 4 years. I was in touch with Max and felt very supported with the growth of the app. Something has changed, the interfaces is wack. The streaks just reset on their own. I am going to look elsewhere. Sad to see something lose it’s functionality. Wish you the best on your journey, breathwrk. The ads are fire, the app is just too busy now and glitchy

title: Not as good anymore
body: I used to love this app it had helped me with my panic attacks, all nighters, you name it. What made me love it was the music they chose for you to breathe in and out to. The music helped me know where I was in the session and it was just pleasant enough where it actively helped me not focusing on my thoughts since I had to follow the music to synch up with the breath. That helped so much with my overthinking. Now they give you choices on the background music but the problem is that it’s not synching with the breath and is basically just background music. Please fix this if you can this used to be my favorite app.

title: App constantly freezing
body: I can’t even explore the app because every time I try something it instantly freezes .

title: No free option
body: No free option. False advertising on App Store.

title: Disappointed in new UI
body:
I loved this app. It had so many different breathing exercises all which were organized by what you wanted: focus, sleep, energy, anxiety, etc.

They got rid of all that for a new interface that took all that away.

Then they took away the different visuals for breathing. Now it’s just this annoying circle. What happened to the line you could follow?!

The new UI is weird, looks like the app made a regress back to 2010, really doesn’t make any sense.

So disappointed since this app helped me with so much. Now I never use it cause of the cruddy interface.

Why fix it if it’s not broken?

title: Faulty App
body: I downloaded this app and found it valuable the first week when it worked, but it freezes/crashes at the end of most sessions, does not track my sessions, and won’t even show me the 2025 calendar. I did contact the team about the glitches/issues but nothing has been resolved and they have stopped responding to me. I got several months free with a fitness program I’m doing. I won’t be staying once the promotion is done. It makes no sense to pay for an app that doesn’t work. Lots of potential but until the bugs are worked out, definitely not worth it!

title: Great potential but terrible update
body: Not sure what happened but recent updates made the app bad . I see breath score but no way to take test and influence it . Phone heats up a lot when I do the exercise and some exercises have a mismatch between what descriptions says and how the exercises executes. Other than these issues great app . Removing 2 stars because of these critical issues . Would love to see future updates take care of these issues

title: Slow to respond
body: Got the app and paid for the yearly subscription, just to find out the explore section freezes when I try to use anything on it. On the 6th of January I sent an email detailing the issue. Someone from the team responded on the 8th telling me to uninstall and reinstall the app and if that didn’t fix anything to screen record the problem and get back to them. I did as instructed but the app kept freezing. On the 10th I sent a follow up email with the screen recording saying that the issue was still happening. I’m writing this review on the 20th and they still haven’t gotten back to me. Figured I waited long enough. Before getting a subscription with this company it’d be best to make sure everything is working as it should.

title: Well done
body: Hi guys ，I also created an app BreatheLab with rich breathing ，any advise is welcome!!

title: Great exercises buggy app
body: I have had this app for over a year.  I have found all the exercises (when the work right) really wonderful and helpful.  The app has had two  iterations since I got it.  Both have been buggy.  The first was bad enough that I stopped using it.  When they did a big update I was excited, but it’s annoying too.  If you try to add or subtract time the app seizes up and you have to restart it.  This is a VERY expensive app to be so clunky and hard to use.

title: The App glitches every time now- and other devolvements
body: The actual breathing exercises are great- but they changed the graphics- and the new graphics are terrible.  There is only one version of graphics for all the exercises - so it’s also extremely monotonous- in addition to being ugly.  The new user interface is also very clunky.  You can’t easily navigate and customize your view to readily get to your favorites, etc.  The app was so much better before- please fix your unfortunate “improvements.”

title: App keeps crashing
body: Update: it’s been over a month and the dev still hasn’t fixed the app freezing at the end of the exercise — how difficult could it be that it takes so long?? App keeps crashing towards the end of each exercise

title: Can’t get past payscreen
body: An app that doesn’t let you try before forcing commitment to trial gets instantly deleted. It also asks for a review before even leaving the setup… devs need better customer experience skills.

title: Glitches
body: I would enjoy the app much more, but it literally glitches at the end of my 5 minutes and I have to shut the app down.  I haven’t had updated stats due to this.

title: Freezes up
body: App freezes up during sessions.

title: Good Concept, Bad App
body: Like the breathing exercises and the science behind them but the UI is poor and the explanation of what you get for the app, premium and pro is unclear. Contacted developer as the app keeps freezing with no response.

title: Disappointing
body: I have loved this app until about a month ago when it began to freeze up mid exercise.  I had hoped the update would fix this, but it did not.  I contacted customer service but didn't hear back.  I'm wishing there was a way to get my $49 refunded.

title: Doesn’t Work and Won’t Take Me Off Email Lisr
body: Over the course of my trial the app NEVER worked. I thought “surely they’ll update and fix it” nope. It’s unusable so I cancelled after my trial. Well now I’m stuck getting emails for life. When you try to unsubscribe it also says you CAN’T. Which is ***illegal***. I told them to manually remove me, they said no, and now they’re still sending me their stupid emails. Basically this company is the worst and add 0 value. Parasites. Get out of my inbox. Do literally anything of value. Leave me alone.

title: Zero response from customer support
body: App is pricey for what it is.  I was supposed to get 3 months for free through Belle Vitale, with an offer for $29 for a year.  Instead I was charged $49 for the year, with no months free.  I’ve emailed a few times with no response at all.  Kind of a bummer for an easily solvable problem.

title: Latest updates
body: Long time user of this app, but latest versions really clunky. Distracting in a way that diminishes the intended effect of breath work. Unless user interface bugs cleaned up, will likely cancel subscription

title: Not a fan
body: I downloaded this app as part of a program, it was part of the purchase from another company.  The app has consistently stopped in the breathing portion and doesn’t show it through to completion. I contacted customer support with screen grabs and was asked to delete and reinstall. I was hesitant because I didn’t have my promo code for the three month program.  When I replied with the concern I had no reply. I decided to delete the app and reinstall and after I did and nothing changed I replied to the email and days later I still have no reply. The customer service is 1 star at best, the app is decent but has issues I feel no one is willing or capable of addressing.

title: App freezes frequently
body: Thought the app was decent at first, but have become very disappointed and wish I had cancelled the trial before accepting subscription.

title: Worst Update
body:
They need to change up how long the breath is and if you hold the breath or not. This new update is just laziness. I want variety when I do breath work exercises. 
There should continue to be a free version.

title: Was a Great App ! Now Almost Useless !
body:
It was a great app , stable and a lot of features. 

 Now the apps is missing a lot of the previous features. It is very buggy, it freezes often , if loses or missing counts. 

The interface is very confusing and not on sync. Many time the ring is expanding (meaning INHALE ) but the message says EXHALE. 

It is almost useless to me after it was an integral part of my daily routines.

Update 1:
I reached out to Apple to get a refund for the app and pointed them to the latest reviews. 

I am now looking for an app to use instead of Breathwrk , BrrathWrk was the only Breathing app I ever used and I feel like starting from scratch.

Update 2:
I received a refund from Apple and purchased another breathing app. 

I made a note in my calendar to check this app in a year from now  to see if they fixed it and brought back the previous functionality

title: I loved this app
body:
I’ve been using this app for a week, it’s been helping, however tonight I did my daily 5 minute breath work session just for it to freeze four times. 

I uninstalled, then reinstalled the app, and restarted my phone, to no avail. 

This is not worth the $50 I was just charged.

title: Good until it stops working
body: It was working for the first week and now it freezes and won’t allow me to complete. Has done it on multiple phones.

title: Design Update Broke The App
body: In an attempt to update the design language of the app, the developers broke most of the embedded functionality within the app and it has been reverted back to a “beta”state, which is a shame because this app was amazing before the design change.

title: Inconsistent!
body: Why is it not working correctly?? No way to report it!

title: Cancelling
body: It says “cancel at anytime.” It does allow you to do this, but you are still on the hook for the annual cost, without a refund.

title: The source to energy
body: This app is AMAZING. Whether you read using its free features or purchasing annual subs. I use this app to start my day and to clear my mind. I think if more people were to use this, people will unlock a hidden potential. A MUST TRY.

title: Disappointed in the changes
body: Used to love this app. I have anxiety issues and they always hit in the middle of the night. A few of the Calm and Wind Down ‘group’ exercises and I’d feel better. But the changes they made recently don’t allow you to change graphics anymore, there’s constant background ‘white noise’ that makes it hard to hear the cues, the visual cue I do have isn’t timed correctly, and if I try to change the length of time it just bombs out after 30 sec or so. I’ve deleted and reinstalled several times and still have same issues. My husband’s version is still the old version so that’s also frustrating. And the ‘Contact Support’ option just gives you an email and a ridiculously long incident number that you have to manually copy to be able to go to your email app and send a message. With no response.   Seeking another option.

title: Worked for a few days…
body: After a week the app freezes at the end of a session on “exhale” and the screen won’t change unless you close the app. When you reopen it did not track the session you completed when it froze.

title: Great customer service
body: I had an issue getting started with the app and their customer service was fantastic. Responsive and helpful! Exceeded my expectations.

title: Used to be good
body: I’m pretty sure the new design update was made by AI. It’s clunky and all over the place and makes me more stressed 😅 the page that lists my subscription has a bunch of premium “features” that I don’t think are supposed to be public facing. To list a few: free bgv, free tone, free bgm. I can’t help but think this was all AI and the design team is long gone. Sad.

title: I love this app. Please bring back the old sounds.
body: I really love this app. I started using it before you guys did the big redesign. I like everything about it except a couple things. 1.) I really miss the old sound effects that came along with inhales and exhales for different breathing patterns. It helped a lot being able to close my eyes, follow along and focus on my breath. The audible cues now are so quiet it basically forces me to use the app eyes open the whole time. 2.) There’s a breathing pattern that is a quick double inhale and then an exhale; the time between double inhales is skippy and not clear. Every time I get it I cut out of the app, or reset to something else. But this sort of defeats the whole purpose of the big breathe now button. Thought I’d say something in case a developer hears it.Thank you for making an incredible app!

title: Glitchy App And I wasted 30 dollars
body: Bought the year subscription. With the promise of all the features in the app. And then none of them worked. The app would glitch and then shut down. I guess time to keep searching.

title: Nonexistent customer service
body: Have a 3 month free trial and can not get app to work. Have reached out to Breathworks twice with no response. If you use this hope that you don’t have any issues.

title: Great, but broken..
body: I downloaded this and was loving it. It’s a great app this is easy to use, and with a lot of great content BUT I had just upgraded to the paid version when it started having technical issues and freezing during every session. I tried deleting and reinstalling the app, but no luck. I’m glad I was able to cancel during my free trial version, because until the bugs are fixed I can’t say it is worth paying for. I may try it again in the future, but I’m going to move on to a different app for now.

title: App crashes all the time
body: I really enjoyed this app. It was very different than other apps but now the app crashes all the time. It loses your streak counts because you can’t finish a session due to it crashing.

title: Not as good as it was. Too many issues.
body: I’ve had this app for a long time and it was always great. Then I got a new phone and the app was updated. Now the app is constantly freezing up. Also, when I choose to do “High altitude simulation” breathing it goes in to the “sniff” breathing which is the wrong breathing technique. I wish they would have left the app as it was. I will be looking for another breathwork app and not renewing this one.

title: Impossible to use
body: I couldn't log into the practice, the application stops at the login stage. Nothing happens next, neither verification via Google, nor via Apple, and you can't skip the stage. The trial is on.

title: update 👎
body:
where can i see how long each breath is for? i’m not going to pick something to play without seeing what the breaths will be? i needed to calm down and came to the app to do those inhale 5, exhale/hum 15 breaths and i have no idea how to find it :/ my subscription ends in december and unless there are some big changes to resemble the previous features i will not be renewing

update: they added more info but i still miss how i could browse by color on the old UI and ride the line with my breath. still missing the old app.

title: Freezes all the time!
body: App has lots of potential, but it’s hard to enjoy when it freezes or crashes during every exercise. It’s especially uncool when you’re holding an exhale for an excessively long time because you think you’re following an exercise and not realizing it’s just stuck on that part.

title: Miss the old version
body:
I love this app because of the access to breathing strategies it offers. I miss a lot about the old version. Here are a few of the things:

1. I can’t seem to find access to the times breath hold. I was able to see my improvement as well as hope my lung health was by using this. 

2. The suggested breathing activities do not have visual instructions like the previous version did. I like seeing what I will be doing in advance.

title: Almost great
body: I love the app, but it freezes fairly often. Otherwise I would give it 4 out of 5 if they fixed the bugs.

title: Update is horrible
body: This was my go to app until you completely changed it.  The new app does not allow you to create your own schedule, when you try to add mins to patterned breathing, such as Brain Fog, it does not save and you have to go back and start over every 4 min.  The breathing patterns have changed, no pause between changing in Brain Fog, and the layout and sounds are not as good, something that was relaxing is now giving me frustration and anxiety.  I have already turned off my automatic renewal.  After 2 yrs what a disappointment.  Wish you would go back to some of the original app’s functionality.

title: Limited Customizations
body: The breathing exercises are varied & helpful. I see 72 exercise options & 59 classes (56 of which are in 4 groups). However, the customizations are limited. The background is an unpleasant dark/dirty green. There are only 3 options for the background soundscape (1 of which I find stressful) & 3 options for the tone notifying you when to start/hold/stop your inhale & exhale (1 of which I find annoying) . Overall, I find the breath exercises helpful, but the aesthetic experience of using the app to be unpleasant & even stressful, which is counterproductive. Pretty background images, & more color & sound options would go a long way toward making this app more user-friendly.

title: Avoid at all costs
body: This app was a total waste of time and money. It’s buggy, confusing and the automatic modes are the opposite of relaxing. It froze multiple times at the “hold” stage of breathing, which is frankly dangerous if you’re trying to get into a meditative state. I cannot recommend that you do NOT buy or download this app strongly enough!!!!

title: App keeps crashing
body: App keeps crashing, please fix

title: Buggy
body:
I would love this app, given the fact that I am working my way out of long covid, and deep breathing is instrumental in down-regulating my sympathetic nervous system. I paid for the app about six weeks ago. After a week of use it stops working properly: it freezes after each use of a breathing exercise and I have to close the app and reopen to get it to work. Uninstalled and reinstalled and it worked flawlessly for one week then the same issue if freezing reappeared. Changing the times for a given breathing exercise is also broken. Always. 
Best,
Tiffany

title: Good App - impossible to cancel subscription
body:
I subscribed briefly to Breathwrk, and then decided that I wasn’t using it enough to justify the expense. I have never
had so much trouble canceling a subscription - I spent way too much time, trying to figure out how to do it, and they are still sending me renewal notices and billing me. I haven’t been able to figure out how to remove my credit card from my old profile - it seems like they force you to re-download the app and sign up again in order to do so. 

I use other breathing and meditation apps on a daily basis, but I will never use or recommend this one - I don’t know what is happening on their end, but I have to breathe deeply every time I get another charge from Breathwrk!

title: App not allowing me to use subscription and no response

title: Underwhelming, lackluster, boring, no wow factor…
body: One word to describe this app: underwhelming. I actually can’t believe that this app requires a paid subscription, that’s how underwhelming it is. It makes me wonder if the creators of this app actually use it or not… because if so, surely they’d know that it’s lackluster (from a user standpoint), right? No widget and can’t add it to Lock Screen. The exercises finish abruptly, like midway through the final exhale. Breathing exercises (on the “explore” screen) aren’t organized or categorized at all so you have scroll through them. Doesn’t make sense to me that the “daily classes” are on the “explore” screen and not the main “breath” screen. Do you want me to do them daily? Maybe it’s just on my phone but I couldn’t tell that there were multiple “guided classes” because the “calming body and mind” class fills that entire section of my screen (with no other indication that you can swipe to the side for more). I’m personally not a big fan of the calendars being on both the main “breath” screen and the “activity” screen. In my opinion, if you’re going to dedicate such a large space (on the “activity” screen) to the “sessions” calendar, at least give us the option to click on any day to see what sessions/classes were completed on that specific day. Something! Some data! Anything! And what’s up with the levels and breath score (on the “activity” screen)? Will my breath score change over time? Why is my level relevant and what does it refer to? I can’t see any information about these metrics on the app. This just seems like an app (subscription) that you’re meant to forget about…

title: Promising App, But Persistent Glitches and Poor Support
body:
I’ve been using this app for two months and paid for the full subscription. Initially, during the first week, everything worked wonderfully—my streak was accurate, the app ran smoothly without freezing, and I could easily access my favourite exercises.

However, after that first week, the app’s performance declined significantly. It began freezing frequently, especially during the last minute of breathing exercises. All my favourited exercises disappeared, and my streak has remained at 0 despite daily use. I’ve updated the app three times as new updates were released, but these issues persist.

I reached out to the Breathwrk team via the contact email provided, requesting an explanation and a refund, but I haven’t received any response. It’s been four weeks since my initial message, and I even sent a follow-up email in between.

I waited this long before leaving a review to give the team a fair chance to address the issues, but I feel quite disappointed. While the app is well-rated and has great potential, the recent glitches and lack of basic functionality have made it frustrating to use. I feel like I’ve wasted my money on a subscription that doesn’t meet expectations.

Back in the day the only flaw this app had was its lack of widgets. Now that it’s had a ‘makeover’ it’s gained a lot more flaws. title: Unstable and glitchy
body:
The idea for this app is amazing, but the glitches, instability, and poor user experience are getting very frustrating. I want to love this app, but I’m only waiting for a competitor to make a better one so I can leave. 
- Older versions of routines have suddenly reappeared to override existing routines 
- Developers aren’t fluent in English, so it’s hard to communicate issues to them 
- When adding a habit to a routine, it doesn’t appear straight away; you have to go back to the routines list and then in again to see it appear 
- Dragging a habit in a routine only works to the top of the screen, then you have to scroll up and move it up in stages  
- Same for reordering a routine in the list of routines 
- Changes to routines sometimes aren’t saved at all 
- Apple Watch app frequently doesn’t sync well, and routines won’t run, skipping straight to the ‘Awesome!’ final message 
- Despite being in silent mode, a habit finishing will play a sound through AirPods and stop—not just pause, stop—whatever you’re listening to  
- Obvious features, like having the projected end time on the Apple Watch, are missing 
- Finishing a routine often isn’t logged by the app, so it doesn’t record streaks well; I have to use a separate app for that

This needs some feature updates for users who aren’t teenagers or young adults. More statistics—mood (not just mood on how do you feel about completing your routine), percentages of routine completed, correlation between mood and percentage of routine completed. 

This could be amazing if they focused less on incorporating things like the community aspect of the app and nonsense like celebrities’ routines and more on actual science and data. If, for example, users could see a positive correlation between completing at least 85% of their routines with an improvement in mood, many would certainly find routines—and this product—to be vital rather than something they downloaded on a whim and won’t renew next year. 

Developers need to consider they’re neglecting an entire pool of serious adult users who are also inclined to have deeper pockets than the teenage and college crowd do.

title: Mental Clarity
body:
I am the mother of a child with severe disabilities.  We have a lot of routine care tasks to track. Routinery has really helped me with mental clarity, and I feel much better since I started using it. i can’t say enough how helpful this app has been for me. 

I do have a wishlist. All of my routines are manual because I don’t start them at the same time each day. I wish there were a way to hide my usual evening tasks (like a bedtime routine) until later in the day because my entire list of daily routines has become too cluttered. I also wish there were seasonal, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual routine options. I also wish there were a way to make certain tasks show up only on certain days. For example, I water my houseplants on each Sunday, but I fertilize them once a month. It would be nice to be able to have it all as part of the same Sunday plant care routine with the fertilizer showing up only once per month.  I know I could duplicate the routine and set them for different Sundays, but any future changes to the routine would require the change to be made to each of those routines. I hope this makes sense.

UPDATE: I love this app, but I have so many routines that I am having difficulty finding and organizing them when I filter by activated routines. I wish there were some way to categorize the routines by day, frequency, and topic (like fitness, household, plants, etc. ) so I could pull them up to make any changes.

title: absolute game changer
body:
This is one of the best apps i’ve ever used. I’ve tried so many routine apps, timers, but this one has been the most helpful so far. the constantly updating reminders of when the next task will start and when it will all end are IMMENSELY HELPFUL for actually keeping me on track/getting back on it after becoming distracted, which is generally my biggest routine struggle. The push notifications that can’t be dismissed are also absolutely crucial. The ability to rearrange tasks and choose to update only today or for all days is also pretty great. I also really enjoy the little in-app encouragements, I didn’t think much about them at first but they add up and are nice to see on bad days. I’ve spent money on premiums for apps before and have mostly been disappointed or frustrated after losing interest- i can honestly say that the paid version of this is absolutely worth it. Unlike most paywalled apps, the free version of this is perfectly good if you only have one or two routines. With no limit, my routines help me get ready for work, decompress at home, take my medication on time, and do my chores.

A feature I think I’d like to see one day would be the ability to add conditions to individual tasks (it only shows up on a Monday, it only shows up after a certain time of day, etc) in a single routine. This way, if my daily routine is the same every day but I have an extra chore to take care of on Mondays and another on Friday, I can have one daily routine that adapts. Currently you can do this by adding the task and simply skipping, but this makes the timers and “all ends” time slightly inaccurate.

Overall, this app has been life changing in taking some weight off my shoulders every day. I hope one day I can develop an app or tool like this that can benefit someone the way this app has benefitted me.

title: Load time and constant reminders already clicked on will make you ADD if you weren’t already
body:
Update 6-4-25: Every update downloaded just makes the app more prone to glitches, freezing and deletion of data. I’ve given the app many months and heard many promises of improvement from the developers. Unfortunately, the function just gets worse. If you have an older iPhone, don’t download this app. It’s poor and inconsistent performance will not ease ADD symptoms but make them worse. 

My original Routinery app review submitted 8-29-24: 
The app gets four stars mostly because of the size of the problem it is trying to solve. However, the biggest reason it gets four stars instead of fewer is that they’re really don’t seem to be any other options for people whose mind works the way mine does. The app is worth the annual fee charged no question. However, a handful of improvements could make it worth two or three times the price and simultaneously still be a five star value! number one decrease the battery usage, especially during longer tasks and with respect to notifications, for example I have an older model iPhone there are two apps on my iPhone that use up one percent of battery almost every minute that I am using that app: Google Maps is one and Routinery is the other. I can sort of understand why Google maps requires so much battery considering the sheer computational power of providing real time traffic information and navigation at such granular detail With street level video. On the other hand, why exactly does Routinery require so much battery? I think it must be a flaw in the design or some non-essential portion of the application that is not being regularly used by the customer are draining the customers device battery. Fix that and I’ll actually be able to use the routines that I created for Routinery currently I cannot— because within an hour and a half Routinery has drained a 100% battery. What about the other 17 hours of my working day I have routines set for those two and they aren’t things that can be run while my phone is plugged in just to conserve the battery required to use the app which reminds me what I’m supposed to be doing? I have very detailed twenty and thirty step routines over the course of two or three hours that I created— and mostly cannot even run on the app. Fix That and it’s a five star product. Improvement number two and this could just be nitpicky but the app for me glitches at least a half dozen times over the course of every day that I use— freezes the screen. I have to close the app and reopen it which takes half a minute sometimes. Actually a lot of times it takes me 30 seconds of trying to tap on the screen before I realize ‘oh it’s probably completely frozen and I need to shut it off and open it back up’. In a day we have 1440 minutes. I really dislike wasting five of them every day because of this smartphone glitch! it’s small annoyance but if you fix that and simultaneously double the price I would pay it and I suspect a lot of other people who are annoyed at the freezing Would happily do the same. Thirdly, there’s a setting somewhere in the apps software that is sending me a notification at 6 AM that says end of rest and another that says bedtime reminder at 11 PM. Neither of these is part of any of my routines that are currently activated. At least once per month I get so frustrated by this issue that I turn off all notifications for Routinery, just to stop those two notifications from waking me up when I am asleep. Please please make it easy to find inside the app where this can be turned off or tell me where it can be turned off if that setting already exists and my exhaustive search of the application has failed to find the setting!
