title: Great app - frustrating sometimes though
body:
This is only way I’m able to start my day quickly. It’s a lifesaver! 

I’m struggling with it a bit lately though. I started a routine on my watch. I skipped some things, hoping they’d be added to the end—the watch doesn’t offer a choice of what to do when you skip like the phone does. 

After completing a couple of tasks, I needed to do the skipped tasks before moving on, but I couldn’t rearrange or do anything at all. Pretty normal for the watch app. I went to the phone app, and it says I have to end the watch routine and start it on the phone. I feel like they used to both run at the same time, which was really helpful. 

After ending the watch routine, I can’t unskip the skipped tasks on the phone. I can’t check them off either. They’re just.. crossed off for the day? I’m so confused as to why this is the way it’s working. If I don’t have full functionality on the watch, I should be able to switch to the phone quickly and easily and make whatever adjustment I need to, and then switch back to the watch. 

I used to start a routine on my watch and when I realized I needed to skip a task, I’d open up my phone and do it because I get to choose how to handle the skipped task as I’m skipping it. Then I’d just continue on the watch, no ending and restarting necessary. Now that the watch and phone app have been separated, I have to end the routine to make adjustments and that seems to be causing problems on top of being really inconvenient.

title: Best routine app on the apps store
body:
Pros:

It’s really amazing all around, it allows you to save routines, then set alarms and shortcuts to start them. The countdown for each step is really nice for someone with ADHD and keeps me on task. The UX is cute and clean. There is a huge list of cool icons to use to represent each step and the routine as a whole (though those icons are seemingly randomly assigned as you create each step and you need to go back and correct them)

Missing features:

Missing a few features that could make things a little easier. You can’t easily add routines by copying and pasting them from outside the app. I have many routines saved in my notes app and I need to retype each step into Routinery to add them. Not too big an issue but still frustrating (especially since I have ADHD). Also, I’d love to be able to quick edit routines when I’m done with them in order to tweak and adjust them for further use. (Like adjusting the time for each step, adding steps I forgot, etc.)

I’ve also seen other apps use AI to quickly generate steps of a routine for you as a starting point. This could be a good “pro” feature addition down the line.

Overall, this is an incredible app that has been making my life much easier. Seriously, thank you so much for making this 😊✅

Initiating tasks, maintaining focus, and being aware of time passing are all things I struggle with a lot. And this app helps me with that. One of my routines is called “quick morning” for when I need to leave the house early, like for an 8am meeting. Watching the time tick down keeps me aware of how much time is passing, and how much time things are taking. Watching it tick down challenges me to be on time by racing the clock. I don’t need to panic trying to remember what to do because I’m following all of the necessary steps in order. And I’m less stressed about being late knowing that I’ll be ready at the end time of the routine. If you struggle with ADHD or any other time management or motivation issues, this is one of the few apps I’ve actually found helpful for more than like 3 days.

body:
I tested out five different calendar apps, and I like Apple’s main calendar app best, because others lack features that come with Apple’s. Some apps don’t allow you to create new calendars, not manage them (without upgrading), not delete calendars, and some come with ads.

This one, on the other hand, can do everything that the others cannot. I love Apple’s main calendar app, but it’s not too polished. Planner Pro has a recognizable icon, the UI looks really nice, and it is very easy to use. You get most of the features you need, and it is designed for users to be organized and productive. And the free plan offers a lot that the other apps do not.

My only criticism is that it has minimal notification options. Day of, one day, two days, or a week before. That’s it. I don’t know if you get more options in the premium version, but you already have it in the main Calendar app, which is not premium. So it doesn’t make sense for me to upgrade when I can already do what I need in another application. But I will say that this app came very close, and feels more user friendly.

title: Feature Request: Integrate Deadlines, Task Sorting, and Reliability Enhancements Across Google Calen
body:
Hi Google Calendar and Tasks Teams,

I’m writing to suggest a few key enhancements that would significantly improve my ability to plan, prioritize, and execute tasks using your tools. I rely heavily on both Google Calendar and Tasks to manage time-sensitive responsibilities, and a few key limitations are creating friction in my workflow:

⸻

1. Add Support for Distinct “Due Dates” and “Work Dates”

Right now, when I add a task, I can assign a date (and optionally a time), but I can’t distinguish between when I plan to work on the task and when it’s actually due. This causes confusion when priorities shift. For example:
	•	I may plan to work on a task Wednesday because it’s due Friday.
	•	If my Wednesday fills up unexpectedly, I need to know if I can push it—or if it’s a critical, non-negotiable deadline.

Feature request:
	•	Let me assign a due date and a scheduled work date to each task.
	•	Let me sort tasks by due date so I can instantly see what’s flexible vs. urgent.
	•	Ideally, provide reminders or visibility when a task’s due date is approaching, even if it’s scheduled for earlier.

⸻

2. Support Grouping and Filtering Tasks by Priority and Deadline

I use a variation of the Eisenhower Matrix to triage tasks:
	•	Important/Urgent
	•	Important/Not Urgent
	•	Urgent/Not Important
	•	Not Important/Not Urgent (these are often joy-giving but deprioritized)

To manage these buckets:
	•	I’d like to assign and filter by these labels or groupings.
	•	I should be able to toggle which task lists I’m viewing, similar to how you might show/hide series in an Excel chart.
	•	Whether this happens in Calendar or Tasks doesn’t matter—I just need one central, reliable location to group and interact with my priorities.

⸻

3. Address Calendar Task Input Errors

Lately, I’ve been experiencing a high failure rate when trying to input tasks directly in Google Calendar. The entries sometimes don’t save properly or disappear after entry. These errors are causing significant disruption, particularly when tasks are high-stakes or tied to hard deadlines.

Request:
	•	Please investigate and improve the reliability of task entry via Google Calendar.
	•	Consider offering confirmation messages or undo options when a task is created.

⸻

Summary of Needs:
	•	Distinction between due date and scheduled work date
	•	Sorting and filtering by deadline and custom groupings (e.g., Eisenhower Matrix)
	•	Toggle views for task lists
	•	Stability and reliability in Calendar task entry
	•	Integration and usability across both apps (Calendar and Tasks)

Thanks for all the work you do. These changes would be a game-changer for managing meaningful, time-sensitive, and joyful tasks alike.

title: Nice app for getting things done
body:
Solid integration with iCal. Can edit in iCal. Tight cross-device syncing. Easily worth the Pro price. Would be 5 stars if quadrants could be re-titled and all tasks automatically progressed to the next quadrant as time nears and the tasks become important and urgent. (That feature is already there for the top row). All tasks quadrants should move tasks beginning at right lower "Z"" to upper left in the pattern. I disagree that non-tasks (things that should not be worked) should be listed in a task matrix, unless the lower right quadrant can be re titled "Inbox" and things toggled as tasks that advance to "Do it now" or remain non-tasks that just sit there in the lower right as triaged reminders of non-tasks. 

If one could re-title the quads, I'd title upper left "Important-Do Now", upper right "Important-Workup", bottom left, "Important-Someday", lower right, "Inbox" with actionable tasks moving automatically toward "Do Now" in the Z pattern.  Such an arrangement would be a progressive 4-quadrant task manager. Right now, app sticks strictly with the Eisenhower matrix that combines a two-step task manager (top row) with an attention manager: i.e., lower row is used to ID attention or time drains that are not actionable tasks belonging on top row.  That concept is important for recognizing what is draining time, but it is not useful for managing tiered tasks. 

Things that should not be worked are by definition not tasks but merely diversions that one should recognize are sucking time regardless of "urgency".  Matrix is good tool for recognizing those, but that also is the purpose of a triaged "In Box".  Things that are not actionable tasks just do not belong in progressive task quadrants.  

Anyway, good job done. I'd pay triple for functionality like I've described. One can do some of this with "Priority Matrix", but their pricing is insane and still does not automatically move tasks to higher quadrants. Automatic quadrant progressing of tasks on the top row is one of the best features of this app.

Filter is great for limiting views.

body: I like that the Outlook App exposes the email address of the sender so I can quickly identify spoofed business/government emails. It is a shame this feature is only available in the Junk folder. I think the naming of folders should be more transparent - “focused”, “other”, and “junk” are misleading. The “other” folder is really the junk mail folder and the “junk” folder is the folder for potentially harmful scam/phishing/malware  emails, and should be renamed to reflect that danger to protect users. It should also be possible to report phishing emails without opening them in the App to prevent the sender being notified the account is active.

title: Massive Improvements from 2020 and Before
body: As the years have passed, outlook has consistently improved to a point that I am recommending its use to all my friends and family. While nothing is ever perfect and can always be improved I think it’s important note the quality, service, and features that have been implemented as of late. As one of the largest tech companies, Microsoft is poised to shape the industry and oh boy has it ever. I am in love with the ability of end user to finally report phishing attempts and other emails for different categories on mobile and desktop finally! I wish we could setup and manage rules from mobile but perhaps that’s something coming in the future. Outlook still, despite the lack of a few minor things, sits atop the rest in my opinion, ease of use and operation is highly scoring for me and I believe this is something that should be advertised to the populous. It’s very effective with its protections and sometimes maybe too over zealous with junk classification but that’s okay because it’s simply resolved through marking as not junk which will ad them to safe senders. I love the unsubscribe feature and many others that I can’t remember right now. The only thing I’m really missing and haven’t quite figured it out yet is how to install extensions to the new outlook, such as my antivirus from BitDefender/NETGEAR which should scan inbound and outbound emails and be an add-in.  Over all the product itself is great!!! Highly recommended

title: Still not a pro tool, but improving.
body: Email service itself has improved a lot, however, the GUI is far from ideal. I have a big 13-inch tablet, and still the screen always feels cramped and not optimized. For example, the left bar is a huge waste of useful space, and customization options is almost null, such as being able to resize the email list vs the email-reading section. And good luck using outlook as as non-full-screen app. Also attaching files is as awkward as ever, always prompting to attach only those files that were recently viewed. It’s a painful process to share files that you know you have in your drive, but you haven’t used recently. In general, tablets such as the iPad have the potential to equal the Windows experience, but it still feels like a mobile version of a compatible app, complementing the actual professional tool. Also, email tagging lacks so many options that you have on a desktop version. And the list goes on.

title: “Undo Send” option needed for iOS app
body:
“Undo send” (actually, just the option to automatically delay an email being sent via an “undo” option) is not possible via Outlook iOS (though I swore it used to be possible). This is an ESSENTIAL feature for functionality on Outlook iOS, as there is the very real possibility of accidental sends on a mobile phone. Please make it available right away, so we can have functional email service through the Outlook iOS app. Without it, this app is unusable.
UPDATE: There is a new version of the app, however, still no addition of an “undo send” feature. The web version makes clear that this is purely a 10 second (or 5 second) “delay” before an email is actually sent…that would suffice, and until then, how can professionals be expected to use this app with the possibility of accidentally pressing send (let alone, last second edits). Please submit feedback to Microsoft to help make this possible, so we can all use the app consistently. Thank you.

Highlight words or sentences

Italics 
Change font size
Change font 
Underline

title: Repetitive, Annoying, and Stupid
body:
Every time I need to use this app, sometimes several times in an hour each day I have to go through the most mindnumbingly repetitive steps, and that’s when it actually works!

First, of course, unlock my phone. Not a problem.
Then, unlock the app, because I’m apparently not the one who unlocked my phone…
Then, enter the code if the place to enter it actually shows up. Sometimes it doesn’t and I need to have another one made to put in. In that case it’ll usually end up asking for both codes one after the other.
Codes entered, it’s time to move on with my day right? WRONG! Now I have to confirm with the app that I’m the one who entered the codes! You know, me, the one who unlocked the phone just so I could unlock the app just so it could pretend there wasn’t a login attempt until the second try!

Quick question, if someone else managed to unlock my phone, could they not also be expected to be able to use the very same method to unlock the app, and then confirm once again that they unlocked the phone, just to unlock the app, just to enter a code they probably don’t need if they were good enough to crack the security on my phone in the first place?

title: Microsoft Authentiception
body: My college recently, and suddenly, required every student to use this authenticator app to sign into their school emails and school website portals. Despite the team behind the creation of this app having numerous reference points for designing an authentication system like Google for example, they somehow managed to make  authenticating more of a nuisance than it already was on other apps. And not by a small margin either. The BIGGEST problem that I instantly noticed with this app is that the process of authenticating a Microsoft app or website is EXTREMELY unintuitive, and is highly prone to bugs due to its poor design. In fact, just today I experienced a bug with this app that completely locked me out of Outlook. How you might ask? Because instead of email-based logins not being authenticated through proper, non-randomized codes like regular apps, authentications through emails require you to memorize a two digit code on the login page, receive a NOTIFICATION popup that would take you out of the app you were currently in, enter the code in app, and then you can finally go past your login screen… all of which never happened to me because the app NEVER SENDS NOTIFICATIONS. Don’t get me wrong, I appreciate the high levels that were put into making the authentication process safe and secure, but the utilization of this in-app PIN system is extremely anti user-friendly. I think the app would be a lot better if instead of using its current notification system that repeatedly asks for the user to authenticate every time they want to use Microsoft Word, there would be an option that, upon a successful login and authentication, trust the currently used device for a fixed amount of days, like 30 for example. In its current state, this app feels more like a giant Google Authenticator advertisement for companies instead of being a proper alternative to Google.

title: Awful Company
body:
I signed up for an Adobe trial while exploring options for my church’s business plan, but I never ended up using the product. I missed the cancellation window by about two weeks (around day 45 instead of day 30), and Adobe is now demanding $150 to close the account.

Even worse, they refuse to let me cancel unless I pay the fee—so I’m locked into an account I don’t want, for a product I never used. To make matters worse, this isn’t just any business they’re targeting—it’s a church. For Adobe to treat a faith-based organization this way feels especially harsh and exploitative.

Plenty of modern companies offer prorated refunds or grace periods when a customer clearly hasn’t used the product. Adobe’s rigid approach feels predatory, not customer-focused. It leaves a bad taste and makes me question whether they value people at all, or just profit.

I sincerely hope Adobe rethinks these policies and starts treating customers—and community organizations like churches—with basic fairness.

Excel has been nothing short of a revolution for my business. As an entrepreneur handling inventory management, file organization, and countless data-driven tasks, I can't imagine a day without it. From dynamic pivot tables to custom formulas, Excel adapts to my needs like no other tool. Its ability to seamlessly manage massive datasets has been a lifesaver, and its compatibility across devices ensures that I can access my work anytime, anywhere. 

What truly sets Excel apart is its user-friendly interface coupled with its robust functionality. Whether you're a novice or an advanced user, there's always something to discover and master. For me, Excel has been the bridge between chaos and clarity, transforming complex tasks into manageable processes.

Thank you, Microsoft, for creating a tool that's not just software—it's a partner in success. I wholeheartedly recommend Excel to anyone looking to elevate their productivity and take control of their business. 💼✨

title: Excel is very good!
body:
Excel is a powerful spreadsheet application that has become a staple in both personal and professional environments. Its versatility allows users to perform a wide range of tasks, from simple calculations to complex data analysis. One of the standout features of Excel is its user-friendly interface, which makes it accessible for beginners while still offering advanced functionalities for experienced users.

One of the key strengths of Excel is its ability to handle large datasets efficiently. Users can easily input, organize, and manipulate data using various functions and formulas. The built-in functions, such as SUM, AVERAGE, and VLOOKUP, enable users to perform calculations quickly and accurately. Additionally, the ability to create pivot tables allows for dynamic data analysis, making it easier to summarize and visualize information.

Excel also excels in its charting capabilities. Users can create a variety of charts and graphs to represent data visually, which is essential for presentations and reports. The customization options available for charts allow users to tailor their visuals to fit their specific needs, enhancing the overall presentation of data.

However, Excel does have a learning curve, especially for those who want to use its more advanced features. While basic functions are straightforward, mastering formulas and data analysis tools can take time and practice. Nonetheless, there are numerous resources available, including tutorials and online courses, to help users improve their skills.

In conclusion, Excel is an invaluable tool for anyone who works with data. Its combination of user-friendliness, powerful functions, and versatile visualization options makes it a top choice for both personal and professional use. Whether you're managing a budget, analyzing sales data, or creating reports, Excel provides the tools necessary to get the job done efficiently and effectively.

Google Voice is a complete joke. I tried to set up a simple business number for my new company and it turned into a multi-hour nightmare. I switched accounts, devices, WiFi, and even tried it through mobile data — same broken loop. Meanwhile, this is the same company that floods my inbox with spam 4x a day. They want your data, not your success.

If you’re a small business owner or freelancer, stay far away. Google clearly doesn’t care if their platform works — and if they screw you over, there’s no way to appeal. You’re better off with literally any other service.

title: Usually great
body:
I’ve been using Google Voice to send text messages with students without giving everyone my permanent cell phone number. 

Pros: 
- you can easily send and respond to text messages from either the app or the website 
- for me, it’s easier to copy and paste the same message to several people on my computer than my phone 
- it’s a free alternate phone number for anytime you hesitate to share your primary number

Cons: 
-My primary complaint after using this for a few years is that the app is now discriminating against 1 specific number. Calls and text messages won’t go through. My phone says “message not sent”. Messages sent from my computer just disappear
- it’s difficult to get support in odd situations where it’s not working 
- it requires either cell data or a WiFi connection, so it can be easy to miss calls 
- it can be hard to tell whether an incoming call is coming to my Google number or my regular number

title: Shaping the future the right way.
body:
Having come from one of the more traditional backgrounds in industry, construction, before moving into the technology space, this was one of the very first tools I had the pleasure of using. It was by far the smoothest, most enjoyable experience I have ever had adopting new technology. Seven years later, I still use it every day, and my respect for the product has only grown.

It does not matter if your business has 35, 100, or 1,000 people, this is one of the most powerful solutions you could ever put in place. It does not just support culture, it shapes it. It creates opportunities, drives openness, fosters collaboration, and connects to virtually everything you could hope for.

There are very few products I am genuinely happy to pay for, and this is one I simply refuse to operate without. In fact, it is now part of my interview process. I ask whether an organization uses it. If the answer is no, my follow-up is simple: Why not? Because life is just too short to work without a tool that makes such a fundamental difference.

title: Texting but more complicated
body: I used this app for several years at a past job. I would say it is like texting with a few small additions like the ability to tag people and notify them of something specific via an accompanying notification. That sounds useful until you actually use it and get tagged dozens of times an hour. Really this is basically just a messaging app with one problem. If you get a message from someone, or multiple people in group message, and you read it and think I will come back to this later and minimize the app when you come back later it is gone. It’s not really gone but it’s not still displayed as it would be if you minimize your texting app or WhatsApp. Instead you have to search for it. If it’s a message from one person you just have to search for that one person and sift through every message they have ever sent. If it has multiple people and you can only remember one you just have to search through every message that one person has ever sent anyone in your organization. If this were free I would say it is maybe useful as an alternative to using direct text messaging. If it costs anything I would say it needs some work. I could see it being good with some tweaks but it isn’t as of my last use which was in May of 2025.

A built-in translation function would be a game-changer. It could auto-detect and translate emails into users’ preferred languages, supporting multiple tongues. This would save time, boost communication efficiency, and strengthen international collaboration.

Thank you for considering this idea. I look forward to seeing such a practical update.

title: Need more artists work
body:
I really enjoy using this app — it’s smooth, useful, and well-designed. I do have a few suggestions that I think could make it even better:
	1.	Add More Fun Visuals: It would be awesome to have more playful or creative features, like uploading our own emojis or using fun reactions. It adds personality and engagement!
	2.	Organize Tasks by Categories/Files: I’d love a way to group tasks by themes or goals — like separate folders for work, study, travel, etc., each with different color codes (similar to Apple Calendar). Maybe this exists already, but I didn’t notice it.
	3.	Include a Habit Tracker + Insights: Adding a basic habit tracker would make the app feel more holistic — great for managing both tasks and personal growth. A simple stat dashboard showing completed tasks, overdue ones, and trends over time would be a helpful bonus. It would give users insight into their productivity and behavior.

Overall, this app is great — and with these improvements, it could easily become a one-stop productivity hub!

title: Most helpful
body:
As an older man who has suffered with ADHD most of my life, I am always searching for a program or app to help me get my mind organized. Ticktick is the first one that has helped. It allows me to do a brain dump from my mind into a list in the app. I can then put a date, priority, recurring, etc., and keep track of them all on a calendar.  That way I’m looking at tasks to do gradually instead of just looking at one giant list and getting overwhelmed.Best of all, it syncs everywhere, so I never have to wait to add a task. I even have it on my Windows desktop.

Tick tick has been a lifesaver. Now, instead of looking at paper lists everywhere, I can quickly add a task to a list and schedule it. I even have a separate list for household items where I keep track of bills to pay. There has been a bit of a learning curve (an online manual would be great.) but once you learn it, you find how easy it is to use. There’s so many other things that this program does; I can’t recommend it enough.

title: Brilliant app - wish I could pay a one-off fee for life.
body:
I just started using it and it’s honestly brilliant. It’s incredibly feature-rich, giving you plenty in free mode, while also offering substantial extras for premium mode. For me, the game changer is the Eisenhower Matrix. I’m really bad for doing things that aren’t a priority at the expense of other things even though I keep a bullet journal for my tasks. When my days are hectic I’m usually pretty good, but on the less hectic days, this is where I go astray. Having an editable EM is a revelation for me and elevates the app above all others, and it will work perfectly with my bullet journal.

I tried a few other big name apps, which all give free versions, but they’re so limited that they’re simply not workable in the free version. They all provide trials, like TickTick, but I uninstalled them without using the free trial. A free workable version, that still keeps some goodies for premium, and is really good will make me want to buy it, simply because it’s so good and because the developers are so generous with what they provide. However, none of them provide the EM. 

I have one single gripe and it’s a wider gripe for most services these days, but there’s no lifetime fee. I’m fed up with subscriptions because they all add up every month.  Tick Tick is actually a tiny subscription, especially compared to others, so it’s definitely worth paying for but it’d be nice to have the option to buy it outright too, offering the developer team some security as well. Otherwise, I can’t praise this app highly enough.

title: So good I came back after my annual subscription ended
body:
TL;DR

	•	User Experience: The app is immersive and intuitive, enhancing productivity and relaxation.
	•	Platform Consistency: The app’s user experience is inconsistent across different platforms (Mac vs. iPad).
	•	Future Development: The user suggests adding motion art as new environments and clarifying if lifetime access includes future updates.

Full review:
The Portal app has seamlessly integrated itself into my daily routine, becoming an indispensable tool for both relaxation and productivity. During my year of study, it provided a tranquil environment enhanced by its soundtrack pad, creating an immersive experience when paired with noise-canceling headphones. The sensory engagement offered by Portal is unparalleled, making each virtual environment profoundly immersive.

What stands out is the app's ability to associate different environments with specific tasks. For instance, I found myself writing one story to the calming ambiance of a river and another to the mysterious allure of a purple forest. Much like curating playlists for particular moods, Portal helps me achieve the ideal mental state for various creative projects. Its intuitive and clean user interface is commendable, with easy access from the menu bar, allowing seamless activation and deactivation as needed.

However, using Portal on an iPad didn't quite match the intuitive experience I had on a Mac. This inconsistency was a bit disappointing, and I hope future updates address this.

Interestingly, the app features textured oil paintings as thumbnails for certain articles, making me wish that Portal adds motion art as new environments in addition to natural environments.

Despite these minor drawbacks, the Portal app has proven its worth, prompting me to resubscribe after a brief hiatus. It undeniably contributes to my productivity. One pressing question remains: if the developers happen to read this review, I am curious if a lifetime access purchase includes future updates with new environments, or if it's limited to the existing content at the time of purchase?

Overall, Portal is a well-designed app that enriches my daily routines and creative endeavors.

title: A Breath of Color in a Black-and-White World
body: Portal is an app that should be studied. It carefully and thoughtfully builds a captivating experience in the name of wellbeing. Upon running the app for the first time, being greeted with a stunning 8K-resolution environment was not only visually surprising, but was accompanied and held the hands of an auditory catharsis of 7.1 Dynamic Spatial Audio originating from the scene you’re placed in. In my home I have several smart lights, and you can imagine my surprise to see that by linking them to Portal, the colors instantly matched the setting, creating a depth of immersion. Instead of the push towards stress and pressure from other productivity apps, Portal encourages clarity and balance. From a circadian-based evolution of a day and night cycle, grants an environment that accompanies you throughout your day, or takes you to the rainforests of St. Lucia, or to Scottish castle walls on a breathtaking loch. All with the purpose of relaxation, sleep, or everyday focus. In an age of data harvesting and spying, Portal is transparent about their removal of analytics, data collection, and ad-trackers. And highlights the processes behind their making of a passion-project that doesn’t have to spell out that lthe team is in it for the long term. From the compassion and sincerity that the small independent team of friends and brothers, it suggests that focus grows gently, like nature itself. It reminded me that true productivity comes from steadiness, not rush. It’s rare to find an application, that feels both practical and nourishing, and this is the only app in which I was truly reminded that clarity, balance, and progress, are rooted in nature.

title: Good but destinations not updated enough
body:
I quickly bought an annual subscription after trying this. Since then, I’ve used it almost everyday for many hours at a time. It is one of my favorite apps on the Mac. It helps block noise and keep me focused. 

That said, I recently canceled my renewal. In the past year and a half, there have only been two additional destinations: Costa Rica and the volcano. Neither one are interesting to me. The developers have repeatedly said much more is coming (nearly doubling portals according to one comment over a year ago), but nothing has come of it (look through the reviews). I wonder if they’ve lost interest. As of this review, the last update was many months ago and it was UI fixes. Their social media pages and blog have been quiet. I do wonder if this is still being developed.

I’ve also found that I really only use a handful of the portals over time. I’d use more, but so many of them feature birds, which is hard to listen to for long periods of time. If the birds could be turned off, it would be better. I also wish there were much more ocean/beach portals. 

I hate to give a critical review of an app I use so often. If the developers end up adding more destinations on a regular basis, I may resubscribe. Until then, I may just go back to YouTube.

If you try it and like it, it’s still probably worth an annual subscription. But, like me, I think you’ll find that the destinations need to be updated to justify annual renewals.

title: Not bad - I just need a little more to justify it.
body:
Pros: 
-This is great for people who don’t like it completely quiet or use it to sleep and work. 
- the interfaces are gorgeous and there is good variety. All Beaches, mountains, woods, greenery, and 1 fire. 
- I love that I can use it on most of the Apple ecosystem - more on that below.
-there’s a built in timer and alarm which is great for workers
- I loved that I could play the interfaces in the background while moving on to another app like my kindle app or shopping apps.
-my family liked having access to it on their devices too 

Cons:
- there are some people who like a “soft city” setting which is pretty common in the ambient world. A little surprised that one is not included for this app. 
-a majority of the interfaces are for places like Switzerland and Iceland which is great, but I was hoping they’d add a few more from different places throughout the year I had it - like more from Hawaii, Africa, Canada, South America, etc…and of course, a city one or something of that nature.
-some of the interfaces move more beautifully than others. As in, some of the interfaces don’t seem to move at all. They are standstills with the ambient noise in the background. Obviously, I enjoy the ones that I can see moving for an immersive feel.
-I see that there’s information about the price being different depending on which geographical app store you are using. However, I bought the annual subscription last year for $49.99 from my I-Phone. And it says it’s $69.99 now from my IPad. I’m seeing two different prices from two different devices. I don’t really like that…So you could potentially be charged differently depending on the device you use. I have not moved locations or have any different settings on my devices that could cause that. So look at the pricing from different devices if you consider purchasing the subscription, because that is strange. I would think it would be the same across all platforms if my location and settings haven’t changed….
-nevertheless, let’s say the “true” new price is now $70 for someone in my location for the year a - I just don’t see how it would be worth it at this time. In the past year, nothing has changed on the app for users except the inclusion of one new portal. I saw the developers response to someone bringing up the subscription model, but with the price increase based on your device and geography, I definitely think there could be more interfaces dropped throughout the year to justify a price increase too. Again, for the year I had it, I can only think of one new interface released and I believe it was for an Iceland volcano - which we have quite a few of already. 
-My biggest ire is that given this work on your phone computer or iPad, I really wish or hope to see them develop a Portal app for Apple TV. All my family and friends play ambience on their TVs. Even some teachers I know use it on their school TVs, but we all have to rely on ambience interfaces from YouTube because there is not a robust app that can offer these interfaces otherwise through a TV.  It would be amazing to see portal migrate to that. Then I think that lifetime membership of $299.99 would be well worth it regardless of if they update with yearly portals or not! I play ambience on my Tele daily but something like that would mean I never have to use YouTube again. For now, I just can’t really justify the subscription or price increase until I see what else they do with the app. 

Side note: while I understand that practically every business is about that subscription life to essentially “help them grow”, you do not have to pay for a sub to enjoy this app. There’s 6 free ones available unless they decide to make them all subscribe to play and those particular portals are actually really good ones.

title: Love it but still hope it could be better
body:
I absolutely love this App. I've always wanted to find excellent dynamic wallpapers of nature in 4K+ resolution for my MAC system, but the results were generally mediocre until I discovered Portal. I immediately became a subscriber and now use Portal as a startup application and dynamic wallpaper on all my Mac computers. Choosing my favorite Portal scene has become a habit right after starting up my computer.

However, I think there are two areas where Portal could improve for me personally:

1. The price-to-content ratio. Yes, I think the price is a bit high. I understand the importance of subscription fees, especially for sustaining a small development team's operations. However, to be honest, I feel the number of available Portals is too limited relative to the subscription cost. While all the videos are premium quality, for a user like me who subscribes annually and habitually sets Portal as wallpaper immediately after startup every day, the current quantity and update frequency are indeed insufficient. I hope the update frequency could be increased.

2. The subscription model. For users who want to use Portal long-term, I wish there was a lifetime subscription option with an appropriate price point that motivates people to purchase. I haven't found this option on Mac OS.

Overall, I love Portal and hope it continues to improve, providing high-quality videos and experiences to users more frequently and in greater numbers.

I can’t even remember where I saw this app recommended but I had it downloaded for some time before ever even opening it. 

When I did I was presented with 4 or 5 free soundscapes through stunning visual portals, no nagging, no strings attached - just chill calming soundscapes. 

So I started using them at night and couldn’t help notice how when I closed my eyes they just sounded so real, like I was authentically laying in a thunderstorming rainforest - it’s hard to really describe I just recommend trying it on a new iPhone and seeing if you agree. 

Then I found that the feature to continue playing these soundscapes in the background even over YouTube videos or music was available - and not a feature  locked behind any paywall, just free to use as well. 

The only thing I wanted that I could not do was try out the hundreds of other portals on the library, I was stuck with 4 - I considered paying to support them for the great app but I wanted to buy access outright and £250 was just more than I could justify. But then like magic the next day I was presented with a personal offer in the app for £20 to access the premium app for a year. Normally I’d never go for this stuff but I’m so impressed by the design of the product & I already wanted to support them, so even though it’s only a year access I subscribed there and then and am over the moon to have access to all these soundscapes all year! 


Thanks for the excellent work!

From tranquil rainforests to calming ocean waves, the attention to detail is unmatched.

The only thing missing? An Apple TV version. Being able to enjoy these incredible scenes and sounds on a big screen with surround sound would be a game-changer. Hopefully that’s coming soon (that’s what I keep telling myself since using this app).

Still, this is a must-have app for anyone looking to bring more peace and presence into their life.

This app offers excellent value with its affordable lifetime subscription and delivers on its promise to help users manage screen time effectively. Features like app blocking during specific periods and precise usage tracking have made a noticeable impact on productivity and mindfulness. It's especially useful for those looking to reduce phone dependency without external controls.

However, the app's limitations in customization—such as the inability to set unconventional bedtime goals—make it less suitable for users with non-standard schedules. Additionally, counting passive activities like FaceTime as screen time affects the accuracy of usage reports. Multi-device integration would also enhance its functionality.

Overall, the app has great potential and is a solid choice for anyone looking to build healthier phone habits, but addressing these issues would make it even better.

body: I use this timer for all my workouts, whether it’s HIIT training or a standard routine, and it’s been a game-changer. Programming it is super easy, and it even displays the total workout duration and actual training time, so I don’t have to track it manually. Unlike other interval timer apps, this one doesn’t interfere with your music. The sounds are distinct, and the on-screen colors make it easy to follow along at a glance. The only downside is the occasionally long commercials, especially when you first open the app. They can be a bit annoying, but considering all the features and how well the app performs, it’s a small trade-off. body:
This is a pretty good app for what I need it to do and for it to cost nothing. I’m satisfied.

Update: 
If you want a timer app you can use without paying for, I highly recommend Interval Timer - Tabatha Timer. It’s customizable. It does have ads, but they scroll through them at the bottom of the screen while the timer is running and doesn’t interrupt your workout at all. It even runs while the app is minimized, so you can still listen for the sounds of when each interval ends, so highly useful. You can even control your music from the app. :) It does not interrupt my music playing in the background on my iOS device. 

The one criticism that I’ve run across is that the app has become more glitchy as of late. I had to remove the app and add it back to my device b/c it would freeze up once I opened it. Unfortunately, doing this wiped all my saved interval timers, so I’ll have to recreate them - boo! But not a huge deal b/c they’re relatively easy to recreate. Also, after reinstalling it, I noticed that the timer occasionally freezes up or get stuck even though the timer isn’t paused, e.g., sits on 4sec left in an interval for more than 4sec. :/ I haven’t seen this happen too much yet, I only reinstalled it a week ago, but will be something I keep an eye out for, and may cause me to update my review further by dropping more stars -  a timer that can’t keep time is a deal breaker.

Imagine buying a watch and then being told the second hand costs extra. That’s where Zero is now.

If you’re serious about fasting, skip this nonsense and move on to apps that actually respect their users. Alternatives that give you timers and better features without a shakedown:
	•	LIFE Fasting Tracker
	•	Fastic

All of these let you track extended fasts without nickel-and-diming you for a function as basic as letting a counter run to 96 hours.

Zero built its reputation on simplicity and community. Now it’s just another subscription trap. Uninstalled.

However, upon regular use, I encountered issues with inconsistent integration—particularly with my Apple Watch. Despite the app recording my sleep data, it often failed to reflect correctly on the circle graph, making progress tracking frustratingly unpredictable. Additionally, the home dashboard prominently displays activities I never engage with, creating unnecessary clutter and an inconvenient scrolling experience. I would have appreciated better integration with calorie tracking from external apps, a feature that remains noticeably absent. Unfortunately, due to these limitations, I’ve decided to uninstall Zero in search of a simpler, more reliable solution.

title: Awesome tracker/motivator app

Having always been a thinner person, I decided to make some serious changes to my life and thought that having a tracker would be very helpful. I downloaded Zero to assist with this. I purchased the yearly service as I found it to be very helpful in my trial time. 
Between Jan 25th and May 20th, I lost 48lbs, ending up at a low of 165lb using a combination of Zero tracked fasting and exercise. I have now maintained a healthy weight range between 165 and 172lb since, coming off the blood pressure medication I was on last January and improving my health immensely. I’m in the best shape I’ve been in since I was probably 25 (I’m now 46). I deleted the app today…not because it didn’t work, but because it worked so well, I’ve made the fasting a regular part of my routine and had not opened the app in a couple of months now. 
Very thankful to the developers of this app, as it really is a cool way to track your fitness and fasting. 
Well worth the $

title: Ads are obnoxious, not worth using this app for
body: I want to say that the app works fine, I’ve used it before with my first child for contractions, but the ads are very annoying and make the app more of a hassle than a help. Having to close out the app after marking literally only 4 contractions because an ad for a game I do not intend to play is popping up really feels like a slap in the face. They know people are going to use the contraction app, they know the point of the app is to tap a button on the screen to track your contractions (which is obviously purposely designed to be right above the ads running at the bottom of the screen) and I have accidentally tapped the ad instead of marking a contraction far too often. I understand wanting to make money and even running those ads at the bottom of the screen, but the pop-up ads are very annoying and literally happen every 4 or 5 contractions, I highly doubt they are going to do anything about it because it makes them money. Makes me feel like I was too harsh on Count the Kicks’ contraction timer as they didn’t have any ads but rather some in-app pop-ups. Yes, I can just close the app and reopen it once the ad pops up but I’ve had it to where a couple times now the ad has played its audio despite me having my sound off, which is very obnoxious especially in a public space. Not to mention it deletes the intensity of the last contraction marked, and most people having a contraction are probably in a great deal of discomfort and having to deal with something popping up in your face on the app that is supposed to be helping you can make people feel more fed up with the situation than helped. Honestly I’m just going to use the Count the Kicks app because it has dual-functionality and feels like it’s actually intended to help rather than benefit from knowing so many people use the app. In fact the only reason I really started using this app again is because it runs the contraction in the background which actually can be a problem if you forget it’s running because it will completely destroy your whole session and you’ll have to delete all the contractions you’ve marked if you want it to actually be accurate. It doesn’t even offer a “delete last contraction” option. It’s a very simple app that has far too many ads to accommodate for something other apps do just fine if not better.

title: conflicted - lengthy/nit-picky
body:
TLDR: the app as a basic alarm and hourly sleep tracker is a 5/5 ⭐️ rating. it’s got a highly customisable wake up routine along with sleep-aid sounds and other things. the app as a whole, with the premium plan being a yearly subscription only, only offering the more expensive version in-app, and missing some quality of life features, brings it down 2 stars from me. 

i’ve been using the free version of this app for 4 & a half years and, while it’s easily the best sleep tracker and alarm i’ve come across, the premium set up really bothers me. 

there doesn’t seem to be an option in the actual app (or if there is, i could not find it easily) to pay for the $39.99 AUD version. you’re only offered the $49.99 AUD plan - which gives you the ability to share it with 2 other people. it’s a nice idea but i didn’t even know about the cheaper solo plan until coming to write this review, which is why it’s gone from 4/5 ⭐️ to 3. 

another issue i have is that there is ONLY a yearly plan available. if there were monthly or 6 month plans i would be more inclined to try premium. i already used my week free trial back in 2020 if i recall correctly, when there were less features then there are now. i think longtime users should be offered a week of premium simply for loyalty. perhaps every year? or 3 days every 6-8 months? i’m not too hung up on the numbers. plus it’d be a great advertisement for the premium as i’ve honestly forgotten the perks and have the mentality of “well i’ve gone this long without it, who cares?” - discord has a set up where they’ll offer users free premium every so often so you’ll get used to its features and want to buy it after yours runs out. good for business!

there’s also no way to edit a night (to change the hour you fall asleep since the app only goes based on movement and not phone usage), or to delete a nap that has taken priority over the proper sleep. 

one last thing is that i’d like the sounds to be stored forever BY DEFAULT - and have the data settings to be shown on the journal page. it slipped my mind back when i had the trial and it was funny listening to my sleep talk (which also hosted my cats who’ve passed away being silly). but i lost those due to the default discard being only 20 days. this is the most nit-picky suggestion i have.
