I can list a bunch of features but that’s the most important one, what’s the purpose of using a sleep tracking app that doesn’t allow you to see the data unless you pay a monthly subscription?

title: I really like SleepCycle . . . .
body: . . . Been using it for years. The sleep staging is interesting, but it underestimates my light sleep. It’s really frustrating as with the low estimate it shows too little sleep. Some days, the amount of sleep it  reports would place me at a non-functioning level, if it were accurate.

title: Does not take into account getting up and going back to sleep
body: I understand it con not compensate for naps but it should be able to compensate for brief trips to the bathroom or tiring off a light and going back to sleep. So if you get up at 2:00am and fall back asleep at 2:15 it registers you awake at 2:15am

title: The app works great but it bugs me to subscribe to features I don't want
body:
Update: I've been using this app for years and it works well. But I paid for the app years ago before they started the subscription-based features. I do not want those new bonus features so I'm not going to start a subscription. But since I haven't started a subscription the app bugs me to do that, sometimes blatantly and sometimes by telling me - in the middle of the day when the app isn't being used - that people in my area are coughing more than usual, it advises me that to get more info about it please get a subscription. Really, in the middle of the day it's bugging me!? 

I'm done, I switched to the "White Noise" app for the brown noise I like and will just use the built-in iOS alarm app with it.

/\/\/\

Wow, this is great! I didn't think it would work nearly as well as it does. 

Thanks!!

title: It’ll make you late for work
body: I have had this up for years. I loved it in the beginning. It was easy to understand, easy to use. I absolutely hate all the updates. Now I am late to work all the time. When I push the snooze. It doesn’t have sound the next time It goes off. So I had to start using another alarm. It’s not accurate saying I’m up all night or fell asleep two hours later when I know I immediately went to sleep. I am a premium member. Now I have to go get another app because they couldn’t leave a good thing alone.

title: Loading / Freezing
body: On the journal tab of the app, my app will have a loading icon pop up that never ends. This will freeze the app and I need to close out to make it go away. This consistently happens when clicking on that part of the app, within seconds. Hoping this gets fixed.

title: Early Adopter Features Gone
body: Used to absolutely love this app. So much so that I paid for the premium version when it was a fixed rate. Now they’ve converted to a subscription and have gradually whittled down the features that I used to have.

title: Been using it for years.
body: I’ve been using this app for years and it’s great. I love having a long-term log of my sleep. Only, as of late, when using my phone to turn off the alarm in the morning, the app will bug out and completely forget the whole night sleep that it just recorded. It needs to periodically save or something because it’s been getting frustrating. Unfortunately, if this isn’t fixed in a reasonable time, I’ll be switching apps. Also the watch connectivity is finicky. I would like a more seamless connection between the two and to actually know that the watch is tracking. When you only analyze sleep and don’t set a time to wake up, connecting the watch will show an alarm and it seems you can’t only analyze sleep with the watch. Aside from these issues, the app has been pretty good.

title: Once Useful App Ruined By Greed
body: I have a paid copy of the app, from before they went to a subscription model. The company indicated that they would add new features that I could subscribe to at a discount, but that they would not remove any features. They lied. I used to be able to see a sleep graph that showed depth of sleep. No more. Now all I get is a binary graph that shows sleep or awake, with a blurred out graph imposed underneath. Without the sleep graph, this app is useless. I wrote a previous review with the same title and two star rating. The developer responded “Hi there! Thank you so much for your feedback, we really appreciate it!" Talk about adding insult to injury. Since I was offered the opportunity to update my review I reduced it to one star, the minimum I can give. I hope the developers appreciate this review as well. I will be using a different sleep app.

title: Loved it
body: Similar to another review, I have used this app for years and love it, but have recently noticed it has me as “awake” for an hour or longer when I go to bed, despite the fact that I’m really good at falling asleep quickly. Switching to another app for awhile and hoping this one improves because I love the wake up window functionally, as well as other functionality.

title: Too many metrics
body:
I have been using this app for many years and made the mistake of updating it recently. There are now far too many metrics for my neurodivergent mind and I hate the pop ups and options. I don’t need to or want to hyper focus on my sleep. I just like a simple sleep tracker with a smart alarm clock and snooze option. Let me turn off the tips that pop up when I open the app. I’m ready to collapse in bed and go to sleep and the last thing my nearly-impossible-to-quiet brain needs is new information. It keeps me from falling asleep! Let me choose the sleep dashboard and info I want to see. And stop trying to push the premium
subscription on me. I have had it with this app.

title: Using for years… Meh.
body:
I’ve been using it nearly every night for years now (>7!), and I’m still not very sure of its accuracy. If you use the “wake in the light stage of sleep“ function… well… sometimes it does, sometimes it doesn’t. There are so many other functions hidden behind the pay wall, that most of the features that are promoted here or not accessible, unless you throw down a chunk of change.
Why do I keep using it? I guess it is a little bit more information than just the Apple health sleep tracker, and it does tell me how much I’ve been storing because it uses the microphone. However, it also inaccurately shows me as being awake, sometimes for as much as two hours a night, when in reality was maybe just 10-15 minutes. For example, many nights it shows me as being awake at some time, while also showing that I am snoring at that same time – huh???
All in all, I’m basically just using it out of habit at this point.

title: Responsive customer service
body:
I’ve been using this app since 2014. I paid for it and was told that would be enough to continue using its features. They have now turned off Sleep Stages unless you go with the Premium subscription.  Sorry, that’s a basic feature that has always been included. 

Update: After emailing support with this issue they offered me a coupon code for a free month of Premium and said Sleep Stages would be restored for long time app owners.

title: Removed accelerometer from free version
body: I have used the free version for years and was satisfied with the number of hours I slept and the acceleration graph. However, with the latest updates they removed the acceleration graph and I no longer have use for the app. The free version does nothing for you now.

title: Very Disappointed
body:
I didn’t even get a chance to really use the app. I used it for one night and reviewed everything in the morning. In the evening I went to review again and it acts like I don’t have a premium subscription anymore. I went to restore purchase which asked for my Apple ID password and after entering it I got a message that said “We could not verify eligibility for free premium features”. I checked my subscriptions and it was there but the app apparently has no recollection of me having premium. I tried logging out and back in. I tried deleting and the-downloading. Nothing worked. So, I cancelled my trial, deleted my account and data, and uninstalled the app. Not sure what the problem was but it’s pretty bad when the app that you’ve subscribed to can’t even decipher that you have an active subscription.

Edit: Changed to 3 stars because support was able to get it resolved  a day before my trial ended but they gave me a new 7 day trial. If all goes well, I will edit the review again.

title: Functionality downgrade
body: I’ve had this app for 10 years and loved it. Recently though they’ve started turning off basic functionalities and putting them behind paywalls even though that’s what I paid for when I bought the app. Really disappointed that I’ve stuck with this app and recommended it to people for a decade and now they’re turning things off.

title: Love This App!!
body: I recommend Sleep Cycle to anyone that will listen lol. Apparently I talk in my sleep and it’s great to hear what I said. The cough radar shows if any funk is brewing. The stories and meditations could be better - interesting selections but I also am big on meditation and these aren’t my style. Still highly recommend trying this way of an alarm. It gently wakes you up with this soft tune once it hears you moving it stops then gives you a few minutes before playing again. It knows how deep in sleep you are and adjusts itself. I love it!

title: Pure fiction
body: No relationship to my actual sleep. Last night shows a pretty typical night but it wasn’t. I was awake from 1:50 am to 5 am, playing games on my phone. The app should have picked up on the fact that my phone was in my hand being used while the app was running and showed I was asleep.

title: Used to be great
body: I have used this app for almost 10 years and at first, it was amazing. It would wake me up during my lightest sleep in the 30 minute window I picked and I woke up feeling refreshed. Now, the app wakes me up right at the beginning of my wake window when I’m still in deep sleep and I am waking up groggy because of it. I tried to make adjustments to fix it but after months of this issue, I’m looking into alternative apps. Bummer!

title: Ruined By Greed!
body:
Same as others, the basic set of features was plenty for me. Now, everything is locked behind subscriptions.

Many years of using it, will be looking for something new. I don’t need any of the paid resources.

title: Super helpful
body: Great calm alarms, clarity on sleep patterns. I thought I was the one keeping me and my fiancé up at night. The recordings helped us to realize my partner is coughing at night in her sleep.

title: Definitely not worth it compared to Apple watch sleep info.
body: Sleep cycle data was quite a bit different from Some watch, mainly in terms of time spent in each stage. From what I've read, Apple watch sleep data is more accurate than sleep cycle. Also the sleep cycle statistics section never populated with data. I missed canceling the free trial by one day so now I've wasted $39.95 on something that I'll never use.

title: Too Much Premium
body: We’ve reached the point in the lifetime of this app where every single feature of the app is locked behind premium except the alarm. If I wanted just an alarm I wouldn’t have used this app for eight years now. I’ve even recommended it to multiple people who’ve downloaded it based on that recommendation. I no longer would do that though because of how little it has to offer; which is sad to see. If I wanted to just use an alarm I would use the one that comes baked into the phone. They even have a bedtime feature similar to this now. I’m sorry to say I think I’m giving up on this app.

title: Disappointed
body: I was an early adopter and paid the asking price for lifetime membership 7+ years ago. The sleep graph is helpful in tracking patterns. When they switched to a subscription model to increase revenue to continue to build the program the “early adopters” that help them get going got thrown aside. I’m sure that people who pay the subscription will find this app useful as it is loaded with a great variety of trackers. As for me the only part that I was concerned with and the reason I paid for the app to begin with has now been locked away when I was promised it would not be. I wish the company the best in all of its endeavors. I will be looking for a different app now, the promises made have not been kept.

title: decent
body: Been using Sleep Cycle for years. Recently and without any sort of pattern, it’s been “deleting” the morning alarm. Last night I had it set to go off between 6:30 and 7, and I made sure it said that before I went to sleep. This morning I woke up and the alarm was just gone. Luckily I woke up during that window, but i would have certainly been in trouble with work if I had not.

title: Sleep quality
body: Not a bad app. I’ve struggled with sleep my whole life and the alarm slowly waking you up is very helpful, also along with the ai chat to give you tips and address more specific problems. The only thing is, I don’t think the actual tracking of your sleep cycles are very accurate, I’ll get a “sleep quality” of 100% and still feel tired throughout the next day.

title: Now worthless without paying
body: After years of using this app they have finally ruined it.  It’s basically useless without paying for a subscription. It’s honestly pretty sad, at one point it was a pretty good app, with great extra features for subscribers.  Now it’s completely unless.

title: Great app turned into another AI subscription cash grab
body: I’ve purchased this app many years ago probably close to when it first came out and have been using it consistently for many nights. The features were great and it was nice seeing the sleep graph when I woke up. They slowly started introducing “new” features that would require a subscription but kept certain things available to those who originally purchased the app. Now they’ve pretty much gotten rid of everything except for the part of the app that tells you when you went to sleep and when you woke up. Not really something another app can’t do. Im also constantly bombarded with popups that tell me to upgrade to the paid tier. Why can’t I just press no and not have it pop up again. I can always figure out where to go if I do want to go that path but you don’t have to keep bugging me about it. I’m pretty disappointed with the route these devs have taken for the app. They could’ve just left things as it was and made a new app that included all the AI and enhancements to not piss off those who originally purchased and supported them from the beginning. I even recommended this app to many friends over the years talking about how great it was but it looks like this has turned into another one of those “junk” apps where nothing is functional unless you pay a monthly subscription. If you’re going to pay for it then you’ll get some use out of it. But knowing how they changed the app years later doesn’t give me a warm and fuzzy that they won’t do it again and screw over their customers. Sigh we had a good run over these years but looks like it’s time to try something else that isn’t full of AI bloatware and monthly subscriptions for useless add ons. If you’re looking at this app and got through this review, I would highly recommend you pass and try out another app. Very disappointed with the devs and their choices over these last couple years.

title: Once  Useful App Ruined by Greed
body: I have been using this app for a long time and found it useful and recommended it to others. I will no longer recommend it and find it to be of marginal utility. Why? Features which were once free have become premium. The sleep graph recently changed from depth of sleep to binary (asleep or awake) and all the sleep stage data is blurred out. The sleep depth graph was an original feature and is now gone. I recommend looking for a different sleep tracker.

title: Disappointed longtime user
body:
This was a great app for many years. They were adding new features only for premium subscribers, which is fine. Now, they are taking away features that have been part of the app since the beginning…even when you paid for the app. 

There is not much functionality left unless you agree to pay $39.99 for 12 month periods for the rest of your life.

title: Love the app! Just one request…
body:
First off, I love Sleep Cycle. I’ve been using the app for years and years, and seeing my sleep habits laid out in front of me is super helpful. The new features added in the past years have been really great too - all around fantastic. 

On thing I’d like to request is this: a dream journal! There are so many times I wake up after having exciting, interesting, or downright bizarre dreams, and I wish I had a place to record them very shortly after waking up. I know I already have this 5/5 stars, but I’d give it 6/5 if there was a dream journal. Not sure what else is on the drawing board for this app, but I sure hope a dream journal is one of them.

title: User of 8 years
body: This used to be a good app until they’ve started locking more and more features behind the subscription. Now it’s basically useless if you don’t pay so after 8 long years, so I’m uninstalling it for good.

title: Scam - do not buy
body: I was an early buyer of this app @ $2.99 and was promised lifetime usage.  As sleep cycle grew and added features I enjoyed this functions.  THEN the BIG SCAM!  They switched to a subscription based service and I started loosing functionality even though they said I would not.  Now in the latest update I can no longer see my sleep graph showing sleep stages unless I upgrade and pay for premium features (again) What a scam!!!

title: Getting tired of the ad spam.
body:
I've been using this app for around a decade now, bought it before it was turned into a subscription. The app has always been great which is why I keep using it. I decided the features I paid for years ago that were honored when the subscription was introduced are enough for me and I hoped the app would respect that. Instead I feel the app slowly devolving into adware slop where now I cannot go to bed without the app reminding me how much I'm missing out on perpetually parting with my money every month including getting full screen splash ads. If I want to change my sound, I have to skip a gracious 3 month offer every night, silly me I guess.

I understand the need to add additional revenue streams or whatnot but I already get enough ads during my waking hours, I don't need more at bedtime too, especially when I already gave you money.


Late June 2025 edit: While the ad spam has decreased, now something as basic as the sleep stage graph an integral part of the experience (that one would think was included in the original purchase) has now also been hidden/paywalled as the predatory encroachment on early adopters continues.

title: Basic free features removed.
body: If I could rate zero stars I would but just the one star will have to do. New update removed the basic free features that have been useful for so long. The sleep stages feature is gone. Will be deleting app and search for a better one

title: Disappointed
body: I have been using the app for years. Maybe not the most accurate, but it was nice to have an idea of my sleep cycles. With the latest update, the sleep tracking is now a “premium” feature, the free app is now pretty much just an alarm clock. Also happened without any warning. Very disappointed. Will be finding a different app.

title: Was great, now almost all premium
body: I’ve been using this app for years now and overnight, they’ve turned everything but the alarm clock into premium features - even the sleep graphs I could see yesterday are blurred out now. Time to hunt a new app!

title: Works for me!
body: This app helps me understand how I slept, so if I feel tired I know why. It starts my day off well when I can see that I had a good nights sleep. I like seeing the quality, how much was dreaming or deep sleep or how many times I woke up. It’s also really helpful showing coughing and snoring. I can see now that I have a CPAP that I am not snoring and feel more rested. The times of what sleep it was, dream, deep etc is a little different from using an Apple Watch and the health app, so I check both. lol

title: Recent decline
body: Used the premium app for maybe a decade, in the past 6-12 months the tracking has become very poor related to time asleep and therefore quality.  From falling asleep times to time awake.  I came to the review section to see if others were having issues as well and was able to find instances that ask to reach out to support, which can’t be done through the app as I looked there first.  I hope maybe it’s something wrong with my phone or the app needs to be reinstalled but all settings look correct and the quality of reporting I would rate embarrassing on some nights.

title: Hasn’t seemed accurate lately
body: I’m not sure what is happening, but the app hasn’t been able to access the microphone quite a few times this past month. Is there a bug in the system now?

title: The way of the world…
body: I have loved this app for quite some time. I love the wake-up window that helps me ease out of sleep at just the right time, instead of a regular alarm going off in the deepest part of my sleep and leaving me groggy. There is a traditional alarm function and a “no alarm” function as well, which is nice. I also loved the insights about my stages of sleep throughout the night, and being able to look at how my sleep quality affected the way I felt in the morning. Sadly, this is now a premium feature. The first feature to go from free to premium was recordings of sleep sounds. That one I didn’t miss so much, though it was interesting to hear my sleep talking. Not being able to see my sleep stages is a significantly bigger hit. It seems that all good things ultimately get monetized, but I wish there had been some notice that a major feature like that was being taken away. For now, I will not be subscribing to a paid version, and will just have to enjoy the remaining features I love until those too are gone. Tracking my sleep regularity and overall sleep quality is still available - for now.

title: Another &$);@% subscription app
body:
Used to be good. Every update more and more features are moved behind the subscription. 
The updates aren’t worth paying for. And the app is almost useless now

It’s a shame to see it happen to a good app. Bye.

title: Love the app - wish it seperated naps
body: Love this app and am coming back after a time away because the ability for it to predict the best time to wake during a window is fantastic. The downside is, I nap a lot. I have narcolepsy, and take a nap almost every day. There is no real way to track naps separately from sleep, so it adds the total amount of naps hours to my daily total which is not ideal for me. I like to be able to see where my split is happening. But I’m not sure with the integrated apple health stuff it has a way to do that. Would be nice to see.

title: What used to be free is now locked under subscription
body:
This app used to be my daily driver in sleep tracking for several years.  However, recent updates/changes to the app locked previously free features under their premium subscription. This was most clear when you were previously able to see the graph of sleep stages (prominently shown after each sleep analysis) but is now blurred out or simplified to just sleep/awake stages unless you pay for the detailed analysis, when other free apps on this store still offer this.  I can no longer recommend this app for use as a result of these changes, and would suggest others to look elsewhere for now. I do hope that the devs reverse this decision in future updates. 

If you use an Apple Watch for sleep tracking and do not mind a one-time purchase for the app, I currently recommend using AutoSleep for its ease of use and accurate tracking even when I forget to start sleep analysis.

title: Features being taken away
body: I’ve been using this app since 2018, about 7 years. I paid the one time fee to download at the time. When I started using it, it literally changed my life. I went from waking up so angry most days to never having that happen again. I’ve been disappointed to notice that recently, features that used to come for free are now paid features. For example, I woke up today to find out that you know have to pay to access the full sleep stages breakdown, which used to be included for free. I used that section just mere weeks ago to help provide data to my sleep specialist about the quality of my sleep. It isn’t in my budget to pay for premium, and I’m worried the app will soon require premium to function at all.

title: All useful free features removed
body: Wow, way to go, guys. Removing the most basic feature from the free version of the app, being able to see your sleep stages in the nightly journal, a feature that has been free literally for several years at least. Times must be tough over there at Sleep Cycle Inc.

title: Developer became far too greedy.
body: Bought this app back in 2018 before they introduced subscription model. They kept their word for a few years afterwards only locking new features until today when they took away features I originally paid for. Have lost all respect for them and switched to a different app.

title: Gotten worse
body: I used to love this app, but in the past year or two it’s now just terrible. Im a premium paying member and I use the accelerometer because I sleep with a noise machine, and there are so many problems and features that I hate. First, the snooze is triggered by me moving my phone. WHAT? that’s the dumbest thing to design in - basically if I roll over my alarm snoozes. The only option is to turn off snooze entirely, which is stupid. Second, sometimes the alarm doesn’t go off at all. This has happened consistently with upgrades. Third, when it does go off, the alarm is way too low even though my volume is all the way up. It tracks my sleep but this app is totally useless as an alarm now, so I am looking for a different app now as this one does me no good anymore. Not sure who is leading this product, but you need to make smarter decision.

title: It used to be good
body: I used to love this app. We had premium back in the day and then they changed the app and it somehow nullified our premium account? It also used to sync with your partner’s app and could differentiate between your sleep and your partner’s. Now, the accuracy seems way off, the interface is ugly (they changed it a few months ago), and they keep adding features only to make them part of the paid version a couple of months later. It has been a part of our bedtime routine for years now, but it just doesn’t seem like it’s worth using anymore.

title: Required to get “free trial”
body: I’d had this app for a little over a year and recently I reinstalled it. When I went to sign in it would not give me an option to decline the free trial at all. Was a great app once but now you can’t even access it without a subscription. Another thing to note is when it claims you “fall asleep” is inaccurate.

title: Pay to sleep
body: Even the most basic features are now locked behind a $40/year paywall.

title: New Version Not working
body: I’ve used this app for about 7yrs and since last update it stopped tracking accurately rendering it useless.

title: Sleep Stages Graph Not Working Correctly
body:
I have been using the Sleep Cycle app (free) for several years. Yesterday, 6/23/25, the sleep stages graph did NOT show sleep stages correctly: shows spikes of awake and flat line of something, but not dreaming or deep sleep.
Please fix this.

title: Oh yeah
body: Meesa sleepy sleepy 😴💤🛏️🤑

title: Cash Grab
body: I’ve used this app for years, and even paid for it at one point. Now, they just keep removing features and putting them behind this expensive subscription. In the latest update it no longer shows the sleep stages like it always has. I think my watch does this anyway, so maybe it’s time to let this app go. The alarm is nice, but it’s really all it’s worth at this point without a subscription.

title: Useless
body: I’ve used this app for years, for at least a decade. Slowly certain things became inaccessible over the years, but not so much that I would quit this app. Today I wake up to find that I can no longer view my full sleep analysis as a free user, which is really the only reason to use this app in the first place. I refuse to pay a subscription when I would never use the majority of the features, and you’d think after a decade of loyal nightly use there would be exemptions for people like me. My husband was grandfathered into full features without having to pay a subscription bc he started using it before they even had a subscription model. This last update is the last straw, I will no longer be using this app. Congratulations, you guys have made your app inaccessible & useless.

title: Extremely Disappointed
body: I have been a paid owner of this app for years. Occasionally they would add additional features for an additional price. After this last update, they have actually removed the features that I PAID for and have put them behind a new pay wall. That is underhanded business and extremely disappointing. Cannot recommend this app anymore.

title: Uninstall
body: They no longer give free features as the sleep graph. You litteraly don’t need a subscription to use a timer, do not waste your hard earned money here. Used to be a great app and now it was ruined by greed.

title: What’s happening?
body: I’ve had this app for 10 years and have loved it. But lately it’s glitching. I’ll set my alarm and go to bed. When I wake up in the morning - it’s not set. It’s driving me crazy. Would love for this to be addressed and fixed.

title: Too expensive!
body: $39.99 after 7 day trial

title: Inaccurate
body:
I’ve utilized a couple apps, this one came with MyFitnessPal for a discount. This particular app is so inaccurate compared to others. 

For example:
Last night I got about 7.5 hours of sleep but the app says I was in bed for 8h 10m but only slept 6h 14m. I don’t wake up in the  middle of the night at all.

This also doesn’t really allow you to see your sleep pattern very well compared to others. If I hadn’t forgotten to cancel after my trial I would no longer be using this tracker. So just be aware of that you’re getting with this one — also, this doesn’t allow for an edit in the error like other apps do. This app could use a major uplift.

title: Inaccurate Readings
body: I have used this app nightly for years but over the past few months, the readings have become completely unreliable. For some reason it’s saying when I initiate the app that I’m up for up to 2 hours after that, which usually I’m asleep within 15 minutes. I hate to switch to another app, but this isn’t worth using if it’s going to be this unreliable.

title: Great sleep and sound tracking
body:
Great tracking of metrics movement, various sounds, heart rate, ambient noise distinction, weather, comparisons of other countries.
I only wish I could distinguish my partners sound from mine without her having the app, I can’t get her to turn on her app at night 🙄

title: Helpful and Easy to Use
body:
Sleep is less efficient as you age. Using Sleep Cycle you can see the effect of diet, alcohol consumption, bedtime etc. 

SC encourages good sleep hygiene. 

The analysis is excellent.

title: Was accurate but not now
body: I’ve been using this app for years. I upgraded to premium a couple of years ago for more accuracy. I was very satisfied until recently. When I go to bed, it usually only takes me a few minutes to fall asleep. I have always been that way. Lately, I have been getting reports that say I am awake an hour and a half to two hours before I fall asleep. This is not true at all. I am going to look for another app when my subscription expires.

title: Solid but lots of storage
body: I love the app: alarm works great, recording settings are great, sleep metrics are insightful and helpful. I wish there was an option to store audio for somewhere more than one day and less than 20, because 20 days of audio takes up so much storage. Strongly recommend. Maybe we will see that option in a future update…? Here’s hoping!

title: STOP. SHOWING. ADS.
body: Bought this years ago. Still showing ads.

title: Great sleep tracking app!
body: I’ve used this app for about 8+ years now, every night! Especially with the recent upgrades, it’s a great app. It tracks the sound of your movement with your phone sitting beside your bed, so you don’t have to wear a watch to track your sleep data. One thing that is a bit of a bummer, but not sure there’s a solution, is that if you play one of their brown noise options when you fall asleep, it can’t track your movements (obviously) through any sound you would make, so it logs that as deep sleep when that’s not always the case….so that makes some of it a bit inaccurate. But that’s okay with me! It’s nice to see your sleep trends over time. Worth checking out!!

title: Best sleep app
body: I tried many sleep apps years ago and this is the one I landed on. title: Disappointed with the New Update
body:
I would give 5 stars for previous versions! I used sleep cycle paid version for several years and always appreciated its clean design and intuitive features—but the latest update has been a major letdown for me.
	1.	UI Design Causes Anxiety: The complete redesign of the interface is visually overwhelming. The stark contrast between the pitch-black background and bright white text is extremely harsh on the eyes, especially compared to the softer, more calming look of the previous version.
	2.	Unintended Touches While Scrolling: Now when I try to scroll down through the app, I often end up accidentally tapping buttons that take me to new windows or features I didn’t mean to open. It disrupts the experience and feels frustrating.
	3.	Missing Audio Recordings: One of my favorite features used to be the snore recordings. Even though the app might say my snoring increased by a certain percentage, I never took the data too seriously because I could always listen back and realize the recordings weren’t always of loud snores—and that made it kind of fun. Now, with the redesigned interface, I can’t find the recordings anywhere, and that makes me question the accuracy of the data.

Please consider bringing back the previous design’s simplicity and usability. This update has taken away a lot of the app’s charm.

This app, with it’s algorithms trained to look for movement or sound (your choice) does a pretty good job, I’d say about 90% of the time it’s accurate in the analysis - I wake up from a dream and see it’s saying I’ve dreamt. I have a deep sleep and it notices. But there are times where I wake up and it doesn’t notice, despite me moving about. But it gets better all the time. 

As someone prone to nodding off here and there, I love that it uses my watch to track the nap - that’s really neat. 

I don’t use the sleep aids, but I can say with certainty that most days when I wake up using this alarm, I wake up more refreshed and less groggy than with others. 

The only problem I have is sometimes - The alarm doesn’t go off, I sleep right through and that can be a problem. I could also see an issue if you sleep with someone else, but they’ve got a clever solution to that…

I’d say this app is a must - I wouldn’t be without it and I’m extremely happy with my purchase.

title: Used to be brilliant, but now nothing special unless you pay for premium
body:
I first downloaded this app many many years ago, and it was brilliant. It tracks your sleeps, supposedly waking you in up at the optimal time. One of my favourite features was the soft alarm, and the way it slowly builds in volume. But I also really enjoyed the recording feature that was built in, where you can listen to yourself snoring or sleep-talking. 

Unfortunately, they introduced a premium feature many years back, which introduced some new features to put behind the paywall, but also moved some of the existing features (such as monthly and weekly roundups of your sleep stats) behind this paywall, restricting the users who do not pay but have already gotten used to these features. 

Since then, it has only gotten worse, with more and more features being moved behind the paywall. Now, free users are left with all the alarm features, but they wake up each morning to a whole wall of blurred out information about their nights sleep. Things that used to be available like info on the sleep stages you went through and when, how much deep sleep you got, the cough radar that was available for free for about a month,  and the sleep recording feature. The app now only functions as an alarm, when it used to be so much more. The loss of the stages and the recording playback might be my final straw to look for something else. 

I understand wanting to make money, but taking away features from people who have been using the app for so long just feels greedy and inconsiderate. Adding new features is fine, just don’t take away existing features that people have gotten used to having!

title: Paywall forcing subscription - avoid
body:

title: New paywall ruined everything

title: Lazy

title: Love this app

title: Not going to use anymore
body:
I’ve been using sleep cycle for about 10 years now and I won’t use it anymore. 

First you’ve taken away the functionalities I had already paid for when I purchased the app and locked things behind subscriptions. Then you’ve started to bully us into paying for subscriptions by showing increasingly annoying pop-ups in the app. Now you’ve started to use iPhone notifications for subscription ads.

title: Good app though too restrictive payment wise.

title: Great app but I prefer the previous graph
body:

body:

First off, it woke me with my usual 5:30am alarm when I’d set it for 8:30.

Following from this, I set the alarm for 8:30am and went to sleep again. The app breaks these two sleeps into separate sessions and only uses one to aggregate into your sleep statistics, this is just lazy/poor programming… All your sleep should contribute to statistics, and it should at least try and combine two sleeps or let the user do this manually…

title: Not that accurate

title: Inaccurate time

I don’t know if it’s different if you wear your watch however it’s uncomfortable for me to sleep with my watch every night. As well as this, I wish you could change how it looks to a more black and white modern less childish look of that app going more into the simplistic and sleek way Apple works.

title: Please provide features to help people with sleep disorders
body:
Pros:

I like this app more than other alarm apps because it has quality alarm tones and a lot of useful features. It seems like it’d be useful for people who have or suspect apneas due to the recorded snippets of snoring etc. 

Cons:

I don’t feel this app is particularly useful for anyone with narcolepsy or hypersomnia – unfortunately I haven’t yet found a sleep app that is and it’s a massive missed opportunity because people like me with these conditions or other sleep disorders would gladly pay to have help if only it existed. So many apps just seem to cater for people who already have healthy sleep and want to excel at sleeping even better, and don’t bother to add features for people with sleep disorders who need help far more – I just can’t understand why this is!

Suggested improvements:

I suggest these as features that would massively help people with sleep disorders such as narcolepsy and hypersomnia. I desperately hope the developers will consider incorporating these features because a lot of them would be very easy for them to do since they often expand on existing features. Not only would it help people, this would be the only app to do it so is a huge marketing opportunity!:

1.  Longer wake up window options: 45mins, 1hr, 1hr 15mins, 1hr 30mins. It definitely needs to be at least an hour as those with narcolepsy hypersomnia can be in an extremely sound sleep for a long time and 30mins isn’t enough.

2.  Option to set the alarm so the time tapers down ie. 20min gaps to 15 to 10 to 5 to 2 to 1 minute. For those with narcolepsy and hypersomnia, your body can get so used to the rhythm of an alarm going off after the same amount of time that you just fall back asleep – I can do this in between 5min alarms for 2hrs. 

3.  Option to alternate between a few different alarm tones of your choosing would be useful too – again so you don’t get too used to one and fall back asleep again. With narcolepsy and hypersomnia, you can be in such a sound sleep and it’s horrible to have to resort to loud, offensive alarm sounds to wake you because its such an assault on the senses. For me it works better if I can use soft alarm tones but unless I can ensure I don’t get used to the alarm tone or the gap in between snoozes etc then I’ll just be pulled back into sleep.

4.  Lastly, a general suggestion is that it would be useful to be able to  programme the app to start your alarm at a certain time. I sometimes forget to set it before I go to sleep and so end up starting it a few hours earlier to ensure I remember, but then your phone battery is depleted and you’re recording all sorts of things that are nothing to do with sleep.

title: Great app!
body:
Simple, intuitive, great app!

Has all the features you want in a contraction timer.

Simple to start, simple to end, and simple to see log of past intervals.

I love the simplicity of the app, where it doesn’t bother you with a bunch of useless questions or ask for money or get in my way. I have a job to do and this app helps me do it without distracting me.

The Graphs section is great — very similar to the log shown to midwives/doctors to monitor contraction intervals.

Critical suggestions:

Might be good to note on setup that it’s important to distinguish how you time contractions (which can be configured in settings but which I missed at first).

It would be nice if the “graphs” section remembered my settings instead of starting fresh each time I click back to see the graph view.

I downloaded RoboKiller with the impression that I would be notified before the free trial ended, giving me the chance to decide whether or not to continue. That promise was never honored—without a single alert, I was charged $130.

The most frustrating part is that the app itself barely functions as advertised. Numerous spam and junk calls still slipped through without being filtered, making the subscription essentially worthless. What makes matters worse is that the app’s effectiveness seems to depend heavily on your iOS version and carrier, creating an inconsistent and unreliable experience.

I reached out for support and have received no response whatsoever, which only underscores how little accountability this company shows its customers. At best, this app is ineffective. At worst, it feels like a deliberate scam—charging a premium fee while delivering a subpar product and ignoring customer concerns.

If you value your money and peace of mind, I strongly urge you to avoid this app.

body:
It’s great to have it sync with family and Google Home.

But my primary use case is shared lists, and Keep has horrible accessibility.

On iOS, there is a three second timeout after which keyboard focus leaves a list item, finalizing the list item with whatever text was input. If you are a slow typer or use alternate input means - or even if you just need a few seconds to form your thoughts - google keep interrupts you.

You end up with empty list items because you didn’t type fast enough. You end up making multiple list items instead of one. You end up cut off with half written list items.

Unless you are a fast typer who always has fully formed thoughts ready to input without pause, this app is nearly unusable.

This no doubt demonstrates the limitations of a formulaic user testing process. I have a hunch that the Keep QA team has list entry items ready to go, and quickly runs through tests, rather than testing real world use cases - especially with a variety of accessibility considerations.

There is a lot to love about this app but it is missing a few key functions that make habit tracking more successful. In addition to “check ins” (positive score) there ought to be a way to record “missed check -ins” (negative score) and just also a way to log days where you missed your habit but it was intentional (neutral/no penalty score). The metrics of only seeing your number of check ins is a useless metric without also seeing those days you dropped the ball. 

It’s also be great to see two habits side by side so you can see if your “early to bed” habit has a correlation to “deep work” the following day—another reason why showing “missed” days would be useful. 

I like how you can schedule a habit that has a once/week (or whatever) frequency but I’d love to see a countdown on that habit so you know, “3 more days left in week to accomplish habit”

The ability to add in widgets is amazing! Design is beautiful ... Just wish some of the basic habit-tracking functionality was more useful.

As long as you keep your phone with you, you will never forget an important task again. With the app you can set daily or weekly reminders that will notify you to do any chore at anytime of the day, and if you need to complete a task several times a day you can set it up to remind you multiple times a day. The app has beautiful backgrounds and a lovely font. Among other things, I use the app to make sure I drink enough water and stretch at particular times during the day, and water my plants when they need to be watered, since my memory isn’t what it used to be. The app is easy to use! And there is an easy to understand video tutorial that comes with it. Apparently, there are other things the app can do, but I haven’t gotten around to exploring them yet. Use the basic version for free or pay a small fee once for the upgrade. The app will back up your data in case you need to reinstall it, but this feature is probably only available with the upgrade. It was recommended by a teacher, and I am glad I tried it. Now it’s an essential part of my life.

Edit:

title: Alarm & Timer
body:
Apple's default clock app and the way their alarms work has annoyed me since its inception. I have ADHD and I really struggle with time blindness, so I use alarms on my phone set every ten minutes to keep myself on time when getting ready for work in the morning to remind me of how much time has passed and prompt me to move on to the next task, when to leave the house, etc. Apple's clock app has always been so clunky and inconvenient to use in the ways I need to use it. This app allows the perfect customization I need and works even better than I expected!! 

features I especially love about this app:

- you can put alarms in folders and turn all alarms in those folders on/off at once without effecting any of your other alarms!

- you can turn on a feature that displays ONE button to turn on/off ALL alarms at once without having to go in and click each one on/off individually!

- once you create one alarm, it remembers those settings when creating your next series of alarms so you don't have to tediously set the same settings over and over!

- there is a button on each alarm that allows you to skip that alarm for just the next time it is set to go off! which is perfect for my ADHD brain, which is prone to forgetting to turn that alarm back on again if I had to turn it off just for one day.

- you can create a schedule and set alarms to go off at a specific date and time! great for reminding me about bills and such each month.

- when the alarm goes off, a banner notification appears that actually reads the time! I watch YouTube when getting ready for work, and this is so helpful to tell me the time without exiting the YT app. Apple's just says "Alarm Clock" without the time, it's so annoying. 

- there is a setting you can turn on that sends a notification every time you leave the app to make sure you turn off silent mode so you don't accidentally not hear your alarms, which is great for my forgetful ADHD brain. (alarms don't sound on silent mode)

Stuff I wish the app had (but is not a necessity for it to still be great):

- It would be cool if when the alarm goes off, there was an option to have the time read aloud.

title: Brain.fm: Focus & Sleep Music
body:
I’m 23 weeks in using this app and it is my most important tool. I came to brain.fm for the variety and I stayed because I found I can actually focus. 

I’ve tried several things to calm my monkey mind and give it something to occupy itself with while I work, read or plan. I’ve had a waterfall on my desk physically and monitor virtually , I’ve listened to classical music (thank you Mozart), I’ve listened to white noise, tried brown noise, and I even bought an album with nothing but the sounds of a coffee shop (a favorite by the way) I’ve listened to more audiobooks than I can count(for the more repetitive tasks).  I’ve even tried working on my computer in VR to shut out distractions (how much battery do I have left?)

I tried brain.fm because the coffee shop was getting old but I’ve found that (coupled with noise canceling headphones or even regular earbuds), I can sit at the kitchen table in the middle of life happening and still focus on what I’m doing.  Where my wife walking by used to throw me off, now I barely notice.  It’s almost like VR. I’ve also been attacking my distractibility from other angles but, I was using brain.fm before that. 

As I’ve used it I gradually added in or took away certain sounds. I’ve liked what I liked and thumb downed what I didn’t (the evil drone didn’t work for me) I’ve done the meditation, I tried sleep but it pulled a Pink Floyd Dark Side of the Moon and scared me awake after lulling me off, easily fixable with a thumb down. 

Thank you guys for a great app and the work you’ve put into it. If the science is just a scam don’t tell me about it because it’s been working great for me.  I suspect there has to be something to the science though because every now and then I stop and realize “I’ve been working on this for 2 hours?”

title: Brain.fm: Focus & Sleep Music
body:
I have ADHD and suffer from severe difficulty focusing on a frequent basis. I’m also musically inclined so listening to normal music in the background is usually more distracting than helpful. I had heard trusted influencers recommend Brain.fm but I was skeptical at first because I already pay for music subscriptions and macOS and iOS come with native sounds of nature you can play on repeat so it seemed like I should be able to get by without spending more money, especially when it’s a significant amount. I tried looking up the research to see if it was legit studies proving the music actually helps someone focus and my attempts were inconclusive.

Nevertheless, I tried the trial and noticed an immediate difference in my ability to focus. The music is not distracting but just fades into the background. I was also afraid it wouldn’t have enough diversity of music or genres to choose from but they actually have a ton of diversity and are continuously coming out with new tracks. I try new stuff all the time and haven’t yet heard it all. I also expanded to the other types of music, for meditation and for sleeping, when needed. Sometimes I get a little craving for real music in the background but I still want the cognitive effects of brain.fm so I will layer it by playing it from the brain.fm website a little softer volume than my Apple Music while I’m working and this works well.

There of course is no magic bullet for ADHD but I have been using it for 30 straight weeks now and I believe it is an indispensable tool in my arsenal for treating ADHD without medication.

title: Daylio Journal - Daily Diary
body: Daylio reinvents journaling for the time-strapped, offering a minimalist interface to log moods and activities with quick taps and customizable icons. Its strength lies in simplicity—no typing required—making daily entries effortless and consistent. The app excels at visualizing mood trends and habit patterns over weeks or months, ideal for mental health awareness or routine tracking. Free features are generous, but the premium upgrade unlocks deeper insights (goals, unlimited activities) and removes ads, though the one-time purchase option is a welcome reprieve from subscription fatigue. However, the lack of text-based prompts or rich formatting limits its appeal for reflective writers, and repetitive logging can feel robotic over time. Occasional syncing hiccups and a clunky backup system also nag. Perfect for **casual users seeking a low-effort mood diary**, but those craving narrative depth may pair it with traditional journaling apps. A polished, accessible tool that prioritizes convenience over complexity.

I used to be very disciplined, so I am hoping this app will help me get back on track and I can honestly say that it already has in a short amount of time. 

Some of the things I love: the app will choose simple habits for you (like drink water first thing in the morning, stretch for 1 minute every day). When you’re depressed, it can be hard to think of and create these goals for yourself, so I love that they choose them for you. I also love the daily coaching and how they seamlessly integrate it in to your routine. The lessons are helpful and I have learned a lot about my behaviors. 

Some of the things I don’t love: there is A LOT going on in this app. The first time I opened it, I immediately thought to myself, “there is no way I will be using this for more than a day” because it was wildly overwhelming and confusing. I decided to push through, and I have a general idea of where things are now, but I still don’t understand the flow of the app. This needs a lot of work. There is also a ton of advertising for there other apps, which needs to be toned down.

Overall, I do think this app is helpful, but it needs to be decluttered and the flow needs to be improved.

title: Oak - Meditation & Breathing
body:
I have over a decade of experience meditating but have fell out of practice for a while. So I wanted to try an app to help me get back into having a consistent practice again. I tried some of the other well known apps (that also cost money), and didn’t like them. I did a search for free meditation apps & Oak was on the list.

I have to say I love this app. It is no frills while also being so well-designed. Oftentimes free apps are hideous & dated, have bad UI, and functionality issues. Not Oak! It’s minimal design gets out of the way, looks gorgeous, and functions so well. There are no ads either, which is also rare for a free app.

The options for guided & unguided meditation are superior compared to others I’ve seen. The guided meditation instructors give cues while also knowing when to shut up & let you do the actual practice. Can’t stand it when a guided meditation instructor doesn’t stop talking - it gets in the way of the practice & becomes distracting rather than helpful. But Oak’s guided meditations strike a good balance & I really like them. 

The unguided option is great too. I like that they have the option to add or remove chimes at whatever interval you choose (5, 10, 20 mins, etc). It helps keep you focused & also helps if you start wondering how long you have left. And you can set whatever length of time you want for your session - it uses the scrolling time feature that the timer uses on your iPhone. Like if for whatever reason you wanted to do some odd number that’s not a real interval, like 23 minutes, you could. LoL.

There’s also guided courses you can take around a specific theme. The one I’m doing is a 10 day mantra class with each session being about 15-25 minutes. Love it.

title: HabitMinder • Habit Tracker
body:
This app is exactly what you need. Believe me.
It helps you think the way you should be thinking.
One of the good things about this app is that you can use it in whatever way you see fit.
I will share with you the way I use the app (I might be one of the only ones to use it like this, but it’s awesome).
One of the problems I’ve always had when trying to take on a new habit was that, once I missed my “streak”, it was hard to get back to it. For instance, let’s say I start going to the gym, boom, two months in, haven’t missed a day, you feel AWESOME. But then, the day comes where you just can’t go, now what? Now you missed your streak, you broke your word, what’s even the point of going tomorrow, you’re a failure.
Well, not so fast.
With habit minder, the DEBT is still there, if you had a goal to read 30 pages a day, and the day comes where you can’t do it, nothing stops you from reading 60 pages the following day. If you want to go to the gym five times a week (monday through friday) and you missed a day, there is nothing stopping you from going on saturday and finishing that workout you were supposed to do on wednesday. I mean, wow.
It is also really visual and it helps you see the habits you are not following through, it helps you see the things you are avoiding, and that is an amazing insight into your personality, it shows what you are running away from. Why are you so scared, go and do it (literally talking to myself rn)!
So yeah, amazing app, like Jordan Peterson says, you will not get where you wanna get by accident, you have to have it written down, and go for it consciously, and at the end of the day, if you WRITE DOWN YOUR GOALS, and you don’t forget about them (which is what this app ensures), you will be a more successful person in a year, even if you only hit them 50% of the time (A LOT BETTER THAN 0), if you have 70% completion rate, out of 20 habits or so? Wow, you’re on the right path, and you can always strive for more next month, my current goal is 80% completion rate out of all my 22 habits (currently at 79%), and a 60% minimum in any given habit (which is really hard cause some of them are tough lol).
Oh well, what can I say, thank you guys for developing this amazing tool, and I feel like I’m stealing from you guys with the 9.99$ a year (like really, are you kidding me guys? why not subscribe??) BEST 10$ INVESTMENT I EVER MADE
BY THE WAY, don’t listen to the people who are telling you guys to remove the option to change previous days (like yesterday) are you crazy?? that’s the whole point of the app for me. Pleasee don’t change that you guys, people like me, who get unmotivated when we lose our “streak” need the ability to go back and get on track, do NOT REMOVE THIS FEATURE!!!!! (people who don’t like it can just not use it)

body: A very effective Safari extension that blocks most all ads & trackers without any user input? Yep. Ability to make your own blocking rules as you go? Yep. Tap to block unwanted elements on any webpage? Yep. Several more features to list but you’ll figure them out. Suffice to say it’s still a little obtuse in some regards. You have to discover some of its features on your own. For instance if you’re trying to block YouTube ads it won’t always work. You’ll get YouTube’s terms of service warning page instead. Unless you pull to refresh the content you want to watch multiple times then it’ll load up without the ads. This little tip isn’t listed in the apps rules or on the developer website & probably for good reason (though I suppose I’ve let the cat out of the bag now myself if it was meant to be a hush hush pro-tip… Oops). It doesn’t always work due to YouTube’s constant battle trying to circumvent ad blockers. But when it does it’s magic just like the name implies. body:
I hate the Recurring Mode so much (in locked mode).    If you set this for a future time, it automatically locks you out of all your websites and apps right away.   It doesn’t even wait for your scheduled time.    This is such a disaster.   

The 24 Hour ALL Day option on locked mode is an even bigger disaster.    This basically runs on a loop.  It doesn’t even give you an option to schedule days or weeks in advance.   It just does a 24 Hour never-ending loop.   

I also had to call the Help Desk several times this week because the app keeps double booking the same active session.  That means if you have it on Locked mode, you have to waste your one-time a week  cancellation just to get rid of the active session that you posted on accident.   

And even when your recurring session is over, they still have the recurring session actiivated again in the background when it should be cancelled.   

This can easily be fixed by letting us schedule the Locked mode in days instead of just hours on a never-ending loop.   This lets us reset our schedule when  our days are over.  

This app has the potential for 5 stars if you fix all these issues.     I will change my rating to 5 stars if you fix the recurring mode, allow us to set the timer in days, and stop the double booking and stop the recurring mode from running again after it has already ended.

And it’s very carefully thought out. The teachings and meditations build on each other. It doesn’t have the scattershot feeling that seems to be common in meditation apps. Also, I don’t know which Tibetan teacher or teachers the creators of the app studied with, but their training comes across as deep. Really, using this app feels like belonging to a sangha with a great teacher. I hope the app store features this more prominently in U.S. searches for meditation apps. title: Brightmind Meditation
body:
Well, you have a large number of high ratings, which encourage me to try Brightmind. So, I tried the intro meditation, explaining to me why we learn mindfulness.
So far, so good. I have, shall we say, experienced meditations of many types, with an emphasis on mindfulness. 
The first problem, and I didn’t blame your app personally, is the price of membership. I am rated 100% disabled by the VA, due to my time in the armed forces, which means I’m unable to work. Again, not your fault, but as people you get than me like to say…” just sayin’”.
The other comment that bothered me is the first topic you addressed in your version of FAQs is that you do not use nature sounds in the background of any meditation. Your reasoning is something I cannot agree with.
I guess I’m one of “those people” that like nature. Mindfulness, as you correctly described, is training your self to be aware of subtle things , feelings, sounds, sensations, developing the “ mental muscle” to improve your cognitive ability to maleate your awareness, basically your life. I was attracted to Brightmind because it claimed to help you “ find happiness”. I’m thinking, He’ll yeah! Who doesn’t want to be happy?
I wanted you to know that this is meant to be a comment letter, not a hateful flame mail.
I also wish to point out that, because of the high level of work related stress in Japan, they developed a strategy which became a social trend, called” Forest Bathing”. Dr Sanjay Gupta, a neurosurgeon who sometimes appears on CNN, Fox, and runs a podcast, while still performing surgeries, went to visit Tokyo, Osaka, and other cities and provinces that I don’t recall the names. He was researching the area around the “Blue Zones”, which are areas on the planet where people tend to live past 100 years. Okinawa is on the list along with the Italian islands, and a few others. In Japan, people meet in a park in one of the Northern Perfectures of the main island of Japan. They test their cortisol level with strips of indicator paper, which folks can get in drug stores. They take notes of the reading. Then they take a hike through a heavily forested park in the mountains for 20-30 minutes. They return and retest their cortisol level. It dropped over twenty units( either mg or micrograms, I need to watch the documentary again.) since cortisol is a stress hormone that secretes into the body during chronic stress, it’s always good to keep it low.
Okay, I am finished, I just wanted to mention that maybe you might consider adding an option for people who like nature sounds. My mental faculties always seem sharper after my wife and I walk in our park. But, I realize there are people who might prefer silence.
I like both and have meditated both ways.
Be well, you do have good information on here and I’m sorry I couldn’t join you on the journey. Blessings.

title: Brightmind Meditation
body:
I have been meditating for 7ish years and have tried Headspace and 10% Happier in addition to Brightmind. I think all three apps are good for people who want to start a meditation practice. 

That said, for me Brightmind is far and away the most helpful because it is a coherent curriculum that provides a structured progression while also giving a wide variety of options. I had hit a plateau with my meditation practice and was on the verge of giving up. Shinzen Young’s “Unified Mindfulness”, which is the conceptual framework that underlies the app, provides tools that helped me find concentration, clarity, and equanimity in a far more powerful yet flexible way. 

Other apps, books, and methods seem to repeat the same (to me, stale) advice: “just return to your breath” with a haphazard mixture of voices and guidance saying mostly the exact same thing. 

Brightmind and Unified Mindfulness guided me through a series of very diverse approaches, allowing me to experiment and find a technique that works FAR better for me than watching my breath. I’m re-energized and committed in a transformed way.

title: TimeFinder: Time Blocking
body:
The beauty of TmeFinder is in its simplicity and ease of use.

UPDATE 11/01/24:  How can the best app keep getting better? I’m not sure, but it happens with every update!

📅 This app allows you to take control of your schedule. Other apps may boast of this, but in my experience, none are as simple or as user-friendly as this one.

🧠 What most impresses me about this app is its ability to manage my mind.  (Am I the only one who can relate to that meme about my mind being like an internet browser with 19 tabs open, 3 that are frozen, and no idea where the music is coming from?)

Thanks to TimeFinder, I can make quick work of scheduling my day (I have a list of routines saved for frequent tasks: get ready for work, commute, work, lunch break) while also making sure my To-Do lists get gone. The widget and Apple Watch notifications keep my on track throughout the day.

You know that awful feeling when you’re trying to go to sleep, but get flooded with a long list of things you need to do?  I even have a specific list dedicated to that. It’s not in a random place to be forgotten about, but it’s in TimeFinder where I can easily drag and drop it to my schedule as time allows and then mark it done— and I don’t mean figuratively.  A feature within TimeFinder allows you to mark tasks as done from within a list and as you complete it on the schedule. 

One word of caution: Because this app is so intuitive, you may think it a waste of time to view the video tutorial in the settings. You can easily navigate the app and get great benefit from it even if you don’t, but if you do watch it, you’ll get the scoop on some other great time-saving features that will maximize the overall benefit of the app.

If you really want to save yourself some time, you’ll stop reading reviews and download it to see for yourself!

title: TimeFinder: Time Blocking
body:
To begin,  customer support is great! I had trouble getting the app to sync between devices and Luke responded within a few hours that very evening (a Sunday evening at that).

If you have ADD and are tired of feeling guilty for frequently missing deadlines or important tasks due to lack of time because you’ve spiraled down a trail of hyper focusing on (mostly) trivial aspects of some other thing, this app is for you. Segmenting the day into manageable chunks that I can visually see has given me breathing room because I can know that I do have to time to accomplish these things. 

I thought the price seemed a bit steep at first, but having it sync between all devices is worth it, as it is so much easier to keep up with. But, while this is a great tool, it is still just a tool. honestly i hate this. i may be biased as my parents used this to control my screen time and what i do on my phone— but i feel like there are way better options out there.
 
i’ll start by mentioning i do like a few parts of the app.  there’s a feature that lets u see ur child’s location, which may weird me out, but i definitely understand the need for it. i also like how it lets parents monitor their kids screen time, although i personally feel it takes it too far.
first of all, it shows every website and app you use or download to your guardian. this gives you rly little privacy, which is pretty frustrating especially for a child or teenager. in my experience, this feature scared me a lot as well; i was terrified my parents would use it to either belittle me for my interests or force me to get rid of games and such that i enjoyed. it also lets your parents specifically block you from viewing certain things, which prevented me from playing a mobile game made for children 9+ (as i said, i’m definitely biased, tho i do think i have some valid points!).
this is getting long, so i’ll end off by saying how this app and others like it can ruin the trust between children and parents. again, i’ll be speaking from my experience — my parents were always trying to control what i did both online and in person, which led to me having very little trust in them, and them using this app did not benefit that poor relationship. i feel like there are ways to monitor ur children and make sure they don’t view anything bad or inappropriate online without installing apps such as this.

tldr, although the app works as intended, i would not recommend it to others because it gives ur child little privacy and prevents you from building a trusting relationship w them.

title: everyday - Habit Tracker
body:
I’ve tried a lot of habit trackers, but there is almost always TOO much to fill in that it made me not want to use them. The process of filling everything in felt like it needed to be a habit in itself. 

My ADHD brain gets too distracted; I desperately wanted simplicity. After years, I’ve developed some great habits simply by using timers and reading Atomic Habits, which this app draws some concepts from. Now, I want to visualize this in a simple, easy-understand-visual for novice data folks like my wife or friends. So I turned to this app, (shout out r/dataisbeautiful). This app does just that. With intention and time, I’m excited to see what my visual will look like. Literally 3 click options:

-Did you do it? Tap.
-Did you do some of it? Tap.  Tap.
-Didn’t do it? Tap. Tap. Tap.

Obviously, there are things to fill out. But compared to others, IMO, set up is simple. Reminder options are available. There is even an option for breaking habits! 

Free to use, so I’ve testing with 3 habits and I’m very happy so far. It’s only 1/2, but so far, so good. 

Some improvements for this app, for me, would just be customizable user preferences. Specifically, visuals with fonts. I have unique reading needs so the ability to alter these helps a ton! This would help keep the app accessible for all. TY for your great app.

title: Portal - Escape Into Nature
body:
I really love this app; I'm a studen in University and I can now be taken back to a class I was studying for by hearing one of these soundscapes, which is a really interesting experience to say the least. What I really use Portal for, however, is to sleep. 
After listening to a podcast about the Amazon rainforest, I now go to sleep listening to "Twilight rainforest" in St. Lucia. 
When I read fiction, I always put on that "Spring Barley Field" and it takes me straight into fairytale land. 
When I want white noise like sound for sleep or focus, why not do it in beautiful "Ama Dablam" in Nepal, or my all time favorite "Highlands Snow" in Scotland (seriously this one is just perfect).
I've woken up to "Fingle Woods" birds chirping so much that I once was kind of confused where I was when I woke up.
And then, there's Stuart Chan at Portal, who's the goat. They hooked me up with the beta for Mac so I could try it early and "help out" by using it and find bugs (little do they know they were the ones helping me hehe). Speaking of, any bugs I did find Stuart instantly responded to and it was fixed so quickly.

Yes, it's expensive, and I'll be sad when my year subscription ends come november - because I'm in my final year of university and I need all the spare change I can get. But as soon as I'm able, I plan on putting my money where my mouth is, and I suggest you do too (on your mouth that is, I don't want your money on my mouth).

Here's to portals to better worlds; or has it been our beautiful world all along?

title: Portal - Escape Into Nature
body:
Portal is that rare app that's worthy of your time and attention because that's precicely what it gives you in return—time and attention. It's. so. zen.

I've used Portal on my iPhone for a couple of years, projecting it to my Homepod for pleasant morning birdsong and water lapping on the shores of Lake Bled, or Triglav thunderstorms for a soothing night's sleep; I've even taken the birds of Fingle Woods with me on my walks while I simultaneously listen to a podcast or audiobook.

But the desktop app brings a whole new dimension to the experience. I'm mesmerized by the beauty of the video taking over my desktop background in its gentle, near-seamless loop. It's a window into the outside world—any outside world that you want right now. Is it a river? A waterfall? A beach? A field? A rainy forest? Portal has brought my mind to a whole new place of focus and productivity I hadn't felt for some time. I adore it. This is a uniquely poignant and important productivity tool, the true missing piece in the remote worker's arsenal. You might try mixing it with music, too—I always love a good afternoon Lo-Fi listen—and see where your focus takes you.

I've been in contact with the team behind Portal, and they're a pleasure to talk with. They take feedback sincerely and their craft seriously. I can't wait to see what they bring to Portal next!

title: Habit — Daily Tracker
body:
I downloaded the app after reading these exact words on the product page:

”Why more than 900,000 users choose Daily Habit Tracker?

1. Unlimited amount of habits. You don’t need to pay a penny to start building as many habits as you need.
2. Ad-free. We hate ads & don’t want to bother our users”

Here’s how that went: 
- Opened the app
- Greeted with a prompt to pay for premium. 
- Dismissed the prompt. 
- Premium prompt pops up again.
(“Hmm.. that’s kind of annoying..”)
- Dismissed the prompt again.
- Started creating my first habit.
- Tried to change the color.
- Premium prompt pops up again.
- Dismissed a third time.
- Finished creating habit (minor complaint here; you can’t set the frequency to more than once a day, e.g. twice a day).
- Created two more habits.
- Tried to create a fourth.
- Premium prompt pops up again.
- Dismissed a fourth time.
(“Surely that’s a mistake..? I was promised unlimited habits, for not even a penny.”)
- Tried to create a fourth habit.
- Premium prompt pops up again.
- Dismissed a fifth and final time.
- Uninstalled.

To be fair, the interface is pretty nice and polished. Please correct me if I’m stupid and missing something obvious, but why can’t I create more than 3 habits? I thought this app could help me structure my day and hold me accountable with reaching my goals. I don’t need an app to remind me of a maximum of 3 things. 

The premium pop-ups are a minor annoyance, and I understand that the creators need to make money. I just found their incredible frequency ironic after they touted, “We hate ads & don’t want to bother our users.” They’re a bit bothersome to be honest.

title: Focus Plant: Forest phone lock
body:
This app is literally SO amazing! Let’s start with how it actually helps you stay away from your phone and focus. My phone is almost always on a focus session, and my screen time overall has shown a decrease. 

Another thing that makes the app stand out is how it’s an adorable game as well! I love to play it a lot, and it’s not addicting (I try my best to avoid addicting games)! Planting and taking care of all of your super cute plants is just an awesome experience. I really enjoy expanding my gardens, opening chests to reveal more gardeners, and getting to join a group. The app in general is just so cute and you can get two things at once: a great game and less screen time. 

One thing I would really like, though, would probably be a chat feature in the groups. It would be really fun to get to chat to the other members in the group, and we could feel closer to each other and help out.

But other than that, this app is TOTALLY worth trying out! I will definitely recommend it to my friends! I’ve already told my dad about it and he loved the idea. Thank you so much! 💕

title: Focus Tomato - Let's focus now
body:
I rarely write reviews for apps. But, I’ll make an exception for this one. To put things in short, this timer is different from others visually, has simple interface, and it’s ads-free!
For the visual, I find it very pleasing as it’s not minimalistic and plain boring. The art is very aesthetically pleasing and I can tell efforts were put into this.
For the interface, beginners can instantly pick up where they need to start. The timer allows you to set however long you want your work session to be. You can also set your rest time to however you want. Compare to Focus Keeper, I think it’s overrated because you have to pay just to change the intervals of timers.
In addition, while you are working, the app gives you a variety of options to play ambient sounds in the background; Works even if you exit the app! There are also no ads in for this background noise!
Which brings me to my last point, that this is all free and has no ads in them! I believe that putting ads would ruins the whole atmosphere this app is intended to created.
Bonus: You have an option to upgrade to Tomato King permanently for $2! Just $2. Even though I may not use the data feature a lot, I’ll buy it to support the creator of this app for their creativity and the vast utility this app has to offer. 🌞

body: I'm in the healthcare profession and spend time helping people with stress reduction. I have tried nearly all of the meditation apps so I can recommend.
