The results are tangible. The details and timing carefully thought out. The lessons are invaluable for anyone genuinely wanting to evolve and (re)train that wild monkey of a brain and not just cover up the difficult stuff with rainbows and unicorns. (That has its place too, for sure.)The interview on the home page is a helpful deep introduction and overview and (refreshingly)not a sales pitch.

title: FitMind: Mental Fitness
body:
I have been mediating off and on for my mental health issues for roughly 10 years. I have used multiple apps. Even gone through therapy that involve Metta (loving kindness). This is the first app that I have used that I can genuinely say is making a difference in my life.

Other apps offer up a smorgasbord of topics of mediation which can be overwhelming. Their approach, from my experience is not focused at all on the science of the mind, but the experience of meditation. 

FitMind gives you the researched back science up front and then teaches you how to use it. It’s truly a system to rewire your brain. It’s not a question of will this work for me, it’s a statement that this does in fact work you just need to be open and committed. For me any level of progress inspires me to learn more. To be eager for more, hungry for more and that has made all the difference in the world.

Liam your dedication to this system, the level of research you have done, how you have presented it. the commitment you have made is absolutely outstanding. I’m 10 days in and I’m blown away by how much I been able to reframe my thoughts. Years of negative thinking patterns and behaviors that I have struggled for so long to overcome are actually being recoded. This is insane.

So if you are on the fence let me tell you that you have nothing to lose and so much to gain.

Chris, Lancaster PA

title: Avocation - Habit Tracker
body:
I’m definitely one of those people that need to write a list every day of things to accomplish or I’ll end up sitting on the couch all day. I often times made lists that were lengthy and unorganized which resulted in me feeling overwhelmed or discouraged when I didn’t finish everything. So I went on the hunt for an app to help motivate me and this app is exactly what I’ve been looking for!

Not only is this app super cute, it’s so easy to use! I love the simplicity of it and how customizable it is to fit everyone’s unique tasks, goals or habits as they came them in the app. I tried a few other apps and in comparison I found that Avocation really motivated me to stay on track and organize my daily habits so I can accomplish them easily. Plus, the cute characters make it fun! My favorite thing about the app is the creative freedom they give by letting you customize your habit entirely with your own title, color, days of the week and time of day.

I would highly recommend! You can download the app for free to try it out and see how you like it. It limits how much you can do in the free experience but honesty, it’s worth the $10 (one time purchase for lifetime benefits) to not only get all the features of this beautiful app but also support the creators who clearly are making this app to help others. A one time payment for all the benefits of the app?? It’s very affordable and generous of the creators! Most apps I tried will charge you monthly or yearly!

One suggestion I’d like to make: It would be awesome if the habits were organizable! I love that they are separated by morning, afternoon and evening but currently the habits in each section stay in order by creation. So it would be nice to have a filter option to sort them by specific time, type of habit or importance or to be able to drag the habit bubbles to be in a custom desired order.

title: Tiimo: AI Planner & To-do
body:
I don’t need a fresh new glow up, or a new icon. I don’t need AI task management. 
I DO NEED the app to load when I open it on the first try. And I really need those features that made this app so awesome that I decided to purchase a lifetime membership. The routines, the ability to set a duration of time and then set the end time and the app would automatically set the start time. THAT is precisely what my neurodivergent brain NEEDS and that is exactly what I paid for. But it was taken away I keep waiting for them to bring it back but instead they keep adding things that I don’t need. I don’t need to see HIGH, MEDIUM, and LOW on the To-Do list. Or at least give the ability to turn those off, it’s very distracting. 
Ohhh, and I doesn’t sync across devices, you have to load each calendar for each device. 
The only thing I use is the Focus Timer so I can visually see how much time I have left (mostly getting ready to go somewhere) and this only works if I’ve done the math correctly to begin with because that’s one of the features that were taken away. Ohhh how I wish I could get my money back!!! 

My previous review Aug 10, 2025:
DON’T WASTE YOUR MONEY!!! 

It’s been a little over three months since I wrote my original review and nothing has improved. I am beyond frustrated because this app no longer has the features that made me decide to fork over $59! I don’t need or want AI, I want to be able to plan my day with routines (no longer a feature) and to reverse plan my day (also no longer available). They say they’re “committed to supporting executive functioning and daily planning in the best possible way” but all I see them committed to is taking people’s money. And yes, there is a weekly/monthly overview on the web planner but it only shows events that are directly in your iCal or Google calendar, and if you are subscribed to other calendars, they don’t show up on the web planner. So the web planner is basically useless. Bottom line; DON’T WASTE YOUR MONEY!!!

My previous review May 6, 2025:
Used to be perfect, now it’s just a mess.

Well, close to perfect. I paid the lifetime fee for this app and I wasted my money! I used to be able to do reverse scheduling; my appointment is at 1:15, I like to give myself 15 minutes arrival time to park and get inside so I would set the task for 15 min duration and the end time for 1:25 and the app would automatically set the start time. Same for travel time, 40 minutes to get there, set duration then the end time and app would set the start time. I’d plan my whole day this way. BUT now this feature is no longer there. I have to do the time math myself and if I’m wrong I could be late. I love the visual timer but it’s useless to me if I’m not on time. The main reason I purchased this VERY EXPENSIVE app was for the task duration and ability to plan my day backwards. 

There are many more features that would improve this app like the ability to glance at the week, or drag/drop multiple tasks when an appointment gets rescheduled, the ability to leave a comment (not a note) in the task, but I could (and did) live without these things. HOWEVER, I NEED the task duration returned!!!!

I don’t understand WHY features that were there when we PAID for the app would be removed.

title: Tiimo: AI Planner & To-do
body:
I’ve been using Tiimo for over a year now, and I have to say the updates since my last review have been really great. A lot of the things I mentioned before actually feel like they were taken into consideration.

What I love most is that the app keeps its simplicity, but still allows for creativity. I can customize my layout to fit my style without feeling overwhelmed by too many options. The built-in color schemes are vibrant without being “too much,” which makes it fun and motivating to use.

I especially appreciate how the day is divided into morning, day, and evening sections, which keeps things from feeling cluttered. The drop-down lists are another favorite—being able to expand or shorten them makes my schedule feel manageable.

One of the biggest highlights for me has been the new AI integration. I actually suggested this in my original review, so seeing it added was amazing! It’s still new and could be expanded, but it’s already a great feature that makes planning easier.

Since these updates, I’ve been using Tiimo more consistently, and I can honestly say it helps me stay on track throughout the day.

A few things I’d love to see in the future:
	•	More adaptations to the AI features.
	•	A true home screen view—being able to see tasks and check them off directly from my home screen without fully opening the app would be so helpful.
	•	A way to schedule travel time between activities, so that “empty space” actually reflects the time I spend driving or transitioning, not just free time.

Overall, Tiimo is still my favorite ADHD/autism-friendly planner. It’s colorful, simple, and motivating, and I can see it only getting better from here.

title: Tiimo: AI Planner & To-do
body:
I didn’t think that any productivity app could help put me on a path that would lead to my dreams coming true. Yet the techniques and lessons I learned from using Tiimo have helped me to build the skills in such a way that I now do most thing out of habit and need the app less and less. 

That right there is pure magic and should be the point of all apps that are focused on helping people become more organized and especially when they are designed as thoughtfully as Tiimo; with the neurodivergent community in mind. Don’t miss out on the videos and how to tools in the app as they can really teach you things you thought you knew but really could benefit from learning more about. 

I found myself more successful in using Tiimo due to some of the quality of life perks such as the ability to utilize colors and emojis in interface that make it easier for my brain to sort and process the information it is seeing.

It’s essential features like this that help set Tiimo apart from the rest. I also very much appreciate the ability to have multiple profiles. As someone with multiple disabilities and varying needs in my day to day life, I value being able to switch profiles so that I can access different sets of daily tasks.

Not every productivity or organizational app is for everyone, but the flexibility provided by Tiimo means that I’m confident you’ll find something beneficial from giving it a download and trial run. Good luck and enjoy your Adventures in the Apple App Store!

title: Joon: Kids ADHD Chore Tracker
body:
1. Heads up: unless you are going to assign 7 or fewer tasks per day, don't bother downloading this. The app strings you along and lets you believe you'll be able to use its basics for free. It DOES pester you nonstop to upgrade/subscribe, but you can opt out initially. You get this all set up, the kid's game app installed, and your kid invested in using it, and THEN after the 7th completed task, it hits you with the subscription requirement to keep using it. Very aggravated at the old bait and switch tactics and will be uninstalling. 
2. Additionally: For an app that is supposed to help keep a kid on track, why on earth are there a myriad of extra coin-earning tasks built in that keep the kid indefinitely on the app doing random things instead of helping them focus on executing the tasks assigned by the parent? Talk about a backfire.

title: Joon: Kids ADHD Chore Tracker
body:
If you’re a parent looking for a fun, engaging, and productive way to help your child stay on top of daily tasks and build better habits, the Joon Kid App is a must-try. This app turns to-do lists into an interactive game where kids take care of a virtual pet called a “Doter,” and every real-world task they complete helps their pet grow and thrive.

What I loved:
	•	Gamified Motivation: The game-like approach makes chores and routines exciting. My child actually looks forward to brushing teeth or doing homework just to earn rewards in the app.
	•	Parental Controls: The parent dashboard is easy to use and allows me to assign tasks, monitor progress, and approve completed activities.
	•	Positive Reinforcement: Instead of constant reminders, my child now feels ownership over their daily responsibilities. The app rewards consistency, effort, and good habits.
	•	Educational Angle: It subtly encourages time management, independence, and goal-setting skills.

What could improve:
	•	Some customization options are limited (e.g., not all tasks are editable in detail).
	•	It’s more effective for younger kids (around ages 5-7); older children might find it less appealing.
	•	There’s a subscription cost, which may not work for every family’s budget—but there is a free trial to test it out.

Overall Rating: 4.9/5

Joon isn’t just another kids’ app—it’s a clever way to turn parenting into teamwork. If you’ve struggled to get your child to stick to routines, this might be the help you’ve been looking for.

title: Purity - Porn Block Browser
body:
I have long said “If only there was a text-only browser for mobile!” Well, here it is. It gives you a black- and white-list option, as well as the option to add the email of an accountability partner, and a 4-digit pin to lock the settings. It does not take screenshots of your phone, but analyzes the text of your search words and of the web pages for risky/dangerous behavior.

And it works. Sometimes a little too well- for example, it will block some Intuit pages because they include the phrase “yandex”. But by and large I can get done what I need done. Thankful to these folks for enabling me to have access to the internet for research and work, without the temptation of porn, or even of reading sensual stories. 

To Purity - thank you. Please don’t cave to the inevitable pressure of users who say “this would be perfect, if only we could also do X, Y, or Z”. The world needs a barebones text-based browser just like Purity is now. I get that some changes might be good, but you have a simple app that works. More complexity lends itself to more bugs and issues. 

To other users - this app works really well in tandem with the Screen Time restrictions on iPhones, if you want to really dial in safety on your phone. Set your safety settings in Purity and Screen Time, then have a trusted friend/accountability partner set the 4-digit pins for both Purity and Screen Time.

3 cheers to helping make the internet a safer place.

The positives sadly stop there. This browser is slow and very clunky, taking a considerable amount of time to load web pages even on a newer phone with great connection. The main issue though, is that if you have a specific URL blacklisted, it will block that URL even if it is a back link somewhere on the page. For example, if I have Twitter blocked, it will load a web page until it realizes there is a link for a company’s Twitter account somewhere on the page, then it will send an alert and stop loading the page. This app and its blocking algorithm does not take into account URLs that are linked to a web page, it just sees them and automatically blocks the page. You can imagine how frustrating it is to try and load a web page but it is blocked because the author has a link to their social media at the bottom of the page.

Although this app will help you fight temptation and that is the ultimate goal, it is slow, filled with errors like the example given above, and poorly optimized. I am actively looking for a replacement because of these issues.

title: Purity - Porn Block Browser
body:
No content blocker is perfect— there’s almost always a workaround. We tend to find what we’re after if we look hard enough. Chances are, if you’ve been in the fight for years or decades now, you know plenty of terms and websites that may let you sneak past security. That being said, Purity does a great job at putting up tough borders. The option to whitelist/blacklist terms and sites is so welcome; having an accountability partner option is also welcome; being able to report pages, block pages as you come across them, block images and videos entirely, and more, make this an incredibly useful app for protecting your heart. So I can say pretty confidently that I would recommend this app.

I also want to say to anyone reading this review that fighting temptation is an arduous process, and frequent victory over it may take a lot longer than you expected. You may find, as I have, that the issue goes deep, and you might have to cut out other things from your life beside just porn— other apps, websites, games, shows, movies, books... Things that may seem innocent enough, or innocuous, but tempt you to make the wrong choice.

In the Bible, in Matthew 5:30, Jesus says that if your right hand causes you to sin you should cut it off. He doesn’t mean literally (or Christians all across the world would be distinguishable by how maimed they are!) but he’s using a very extreme kind of imagery and language to describe the severity of action needed to overcome a sinful lifestyle. He’s saying, “If that show you like leads you to desire porn, stop watching it. Get rid of it. Rip it up from the root. If that app or game makes you lust, delete it, prevent yourself from even having access to it. Whatever tempts you, cut it out like its a cancerous mass or it will eventually kill you.”

This app will help you do that. It will help you be proactive in the fight, not just reactive. It is a handy tool in the task of uprooting bad habits in your life. And for those burdened by the guilt and shame that come with the struggle with porn, I say, “Lay that burden down at the cross of Jesus.” If we own our sin and admit our guilt, God will consistently and reliably forgive us of that sin and work in our hearts to purge those habits from our lives. (1 John 1:9) And He does that with joy, because Jesus paid the price for our guilt when he sacrificed himself in our place. God sees the finished work of Jesus— the atoning blood spilled to pay our debt and the blameless righteousness of the perfect Son— and He delights to take away your shame because you’ve been justified. To use this app is to lean into the change that God is already working in your heart, and will see to it’s end; it is to be that much more in step with living a guilt-free life.

title: Awesome Habits: Habit Tracker
body: You can set up any number of daily, weekly or monthly habits to track, and can also put them into custom–named categories. I like that the main screen with the habits being tracked also displays a percentage of completion, which can count either your daily tasks, or all tasks via one of the settings. For example, if a habit needs a count of seven to complete and you have only performed it four times, you get credit for that. Nice. title: Awesome Habits: Habit Tracker
body:
The app works really well! Enjoying it. 

Would love the following features:

1. All me to make a goal out of any Apple health metric, I don't think you need to build them all in, but rather just a section within the "custom habit" to pick a health stat so that it can automatically connect to that health data. 
2. An "On or Off Track" status indicator for the habits that are weekly or monthly as well as one for the daily status. In other words if my status is weekly, but it's tracking sugar intake, I really have no idea if I'm on track with my goal or not which forces me to to some math in my head "ok we're halfway through the week and it looks like I'm less than halfway done so I should work on this today" rather than seeing the gap between where I should be and where I am, or inverse, the fact that I can ignore that habit today because I'm already ahead. title: Awesome Habits: Habit Tracker

Another aspect that I liked about the app is that when checking the history of a habit the app is designed in a way that it doesn’t allow to accidentally modify past days, if you want to change something in the history you have to be intentional, there’s not risk of changing the history by error with the finger like in other apps. The only feature I would add is the ability to choose how many days in a week I want to track an app by quantity and not only by choosing selected weekdays like “Monday, Tuesday, etc”. title: Awesome Habits: Habit Tracker
body:
A lot of thought went into this app and it shows. So easy to use and a pleasant experience to mark goals complete. Tap the widget, tap the goal, and done. Or use Siri Shortcuts. This is perfect.

I was wondering if you have a roadmap anywhere on what improvements might be coming down the pipe. Some apps have an entire week view with little colored or uncolered squares showing if a goal was completed. It’s a cool way to pack a lot of data, like 10 goals over a week, and view it all at once.

Another cool feature would be multi level goals to track workouts, like the habit could be bench press, the # of reps would another dimension, and the weight would be the 3rd level dimension. Getting data in for weight and reps would mean you completed the goal of bench press, but would be cool to track weight and reps in a way that could be displayed on graphs. So not just using the notes feature for this.

Lastly, for the hardcore nerds among us, csv export of all the data in case we want to juxtapose our goals alongside data from other apps that we are tracking. Like overlaying our goals data on a graph from our smart scale app that shows our weight/ muscle mass/etc. exporting the data makes this possible and allows for the potential to make some amazing insights on how our habits can correlate to other things that we are tracking.

This app should become the solution to track everything else. We have Apple Watch and smart scales to track so many things, overlaying that data on top of anything else we want to track should make this a must have app.

title: AppBlock: Block Apps & Website
body:
Is the app good? Absolutely — 100%.
I’ve been using this app for over two years, and it’s been such a valuable tool that I’ve recommended it to my family as well. It’s genuinely helped me stay focused, and I’ve always felt it was worth paying for.

That said, I’ve noticed some recent changes that feel a bit disappointing. For example, we used to have access to strict mode for an entire day, and unlimited app blocking, which was incredibly helpful. Now, strict mode is capped at 12 hours, and the block sessions are limited to 4 hours, which feels restrictive — especially for those of us who rely on the app for long, focused periods.

I completely understand that you need to monetize — no offense at all — but I do wish the app would return to the features that originally made it feel generous and user-focused. These changes feel like a step backward in terms of flexibility.

Still, I truly believe the app is a great investment. I just hope the team can find a balance between revenue and retaining the features that long-time users loved.

title: AppBlock: Block Apps & Website
body:
The free version wasn’t as strict as I would’ve like it to be, so I ended up going premium for $15 for the first year (still in that first year). 

 While creating different schedules are nice, I’ve learned that there’s only one “strict block” option— the schedules block— that really works. While it’s been helpful to keep me off my phone endlessly in the morning and at night, I created another limit to control how much time I’m allowed on an app (ex: “I want to spend 30 minutes on Instagram max.”), but it won’t allow me to put that schedule in strict mode. So it’s practically useless, since I can pause it at any time. 

 Additionally, say I was to go into one of my schedules I’ve made and add a new app. If I add it to the list of apps within the schedule, if I go to save my changes, I’m given a notification that says, “changes can’t be made, or apps would be blocked indefinitely.” So just by adding a new app— which, for premium should be unlimited addition of apps— my schedule won’t let me change anything. 
 I’m sure I could loophole it by deleting the schedule entirely and creating it again with the new app, but it shouldn’t have to be that difficult. 

 They created a “hide the pause” button, in hopes for you to be unable to keep hitting “pause for 15 minutes” for hours (guilty), but there’s nothing keeping you from simply going to setting and clicking “show pause button.” So, even in that update, it’s not helpful. 

 They asked once for feedback, and I happily gave it— not out of frustration but truly wanting to give the developer honest feedback— but there’s no space to leave your feedback in the app unless it’s asked for. So, reviews were the only way to go. 

 I would love to see this app succeed, but I’m struggling to stay without any updates.

title: MyRoutine: Routine Habit Goal
body: Life changing! I originally downloaded this app to build habits. Checking each habit I’ve completed feels so satisfying. It’s that small sense of pride that keeps you going. No matter how small that change seems, when you incorporate into your everyday life, it makes a difference. This app gives me an excuse to not skip out on small tasks from flossing to getting ahead of my assignments. The functions could be a bit smoother and the emoji keyboard has a small scrolling back-and-forth bug, but this app still does its job and completes its purpose well. The thing I love most about this app is how you can build a series of routines and have a timer for each of them. If you take too long, then the timer will turn red and begin to count your overtime. That has shown me when I surprisingly take too long on something that I didn’t think was a problem. Best of all, you have the option to make habits repeat between certain weekdays or a number of times a week, and if you do finish something that was a goal, you can mark it off forever. For example, when I got my braces off today, I could mark my habit of wearing elastics as forever completed. :) Something this app could change is seeing progress as “last 7 days” or “last 30 days” instead of “this week” or “this month”. Because when you just started a month, there’s not much to see with “this month,” and that forces me to scroll back to see my progress from last month, which is less efficient.

I’ve tried more than a few routine-building apps and this is by far the one closest to what I’ve always wanted in one of these. First of all— NO TIMER (or at least the option to turn it off.) Timers have always been a source of stress in my routines because I can’t always stick to whatever I’ve assigned a habit. Secondly— the LOOK! I’m a spreadsheet girl, plain and simple as that. The customization is always fun too. And finally— the routines themselves! I love that I can easily make weekly and daily habits and toggle between having them on specific days or just up to a certain # of times in a given time range.
My only gripe is that the app doesn’t keep my appearance preference (dark mode) when I access the app via a widget. I’m sure it’ll get addressed soon enough.
Anyway, this is well worth my money :) (written about a week into using it)

title: Focused Work - Pomodoro Timer
body:
This app checks several of the boxes I’m looking for in a pomodoro system. Though, I can’t bring myself to use this app or pay for the subscription as it’s incredibly ugly. It needs a substantial UI upgrade. Very off-putting colors, constrained menus, odd layouts, etc. The entire experience needs to be more minimal while maintaining functionality. What’s worse, is there isn’t a single setting to alter any part of the app’s appearance, which is a very odd decision on the developers part. 

For instance, the green and orange glowing icons on the session structure screen. Yikes. That along with the ugly, bold purple core app color is just terrible. I also don’t understand why integrations is mentioned on this screen, it’s already in settings. There’s also a glitchy Siri thing at the bottom that is spazzing out. It’s unfortunate because having a session view screen like this that breaks down and labels each section of the pomodoro system isn’t available in other apps that I’m aware of. And it’s a bit ruined by the ugliness of it all. 

Also the tiny icons above the pomodoro timer wrapped in a bold red line. Why?? This is so weird. The entire top of the app is so cluttered and strange. And the bold red, uneditable color of the timer is not cool. And again, why is integrations on a tiny system menu icon that’s just cluttering up the limited space available? Integrations should be in settings and left alone. Makes absolutely no sense to keep pushing integrations. If someone wanted to use the functionality, they will… in settings. 

You also can’t remove the dumb tomato icon in front of pomodoro. Some of your users are over 12 and don’t want to use emojis. Weird thing to hardcode.

Under appearance settings, where you’re weirdly only able to edit the font thickness (seriously), it even shows a purple timer color and yet the only available color on the actual main screen is VERY red. 

We also don’t need the “ready to focus?” text. Yes, we’re ready to focus, that’s why we downloaded a focus app. 

This isn’t to say that other pomodoro apps are much better, though some apps with limited functionality have a much better UI.

This app has a lot going for it, but as a person who shys away from ugly apps, I just can’t bring myself to use it. But I do see a lot of potential here, so I’ll check back to see if UI improvements are made.

title: Focused Work - Pomodoro Timer
body:
As productivity tools go—especially for those who use Toggl and want to integrate time-tracking—Focused Work is probably the strongest. Add to that the ability to integrate Shortcuts and it becomes a powerful tool with a lot of flexibility and potential. 

However, although it boasts many strengths, it does still have one (admittedly, superficial/minor) flaw: The emojis are non-negotiable. For all its flexibility, not having the option to opt out of using emojis—especially when they’re displayed so prominently—is incredibly distracting, and incentivizes me to hide what is otherwise a clean interface with crisp Live Activities. 

That’s not suggesting adding an alternative like SF Symbols; just that I wish the emojis themselves were optional, so I’m not required to use them or forced to decide which garish emoji best fits the custom focus session I want to create.  PLEASE make these optional.

title: Focused Work - Pomodoro Timer

I spent a lot of time searching for an app with a flexible Pomodoro timer that includes a count-up clock and tracks my sessions. I love that Focused Work offers a Flowmodoro option, a flexible timer, and the traditional Pomodoro. The Toggl integration is also very convenient. This app has really boosted my productivity.

I knocked off one star because there are some features that I find extremely annoying. So much so that every now and then, I stop using the app, try to find something similar, but never find it, so I come back. The main issue is the notifications. I didn’t like them, so I turned them off. Now I get reminders to turn on notifications so that I can get reminders! It really makes no sense. Then there are the reminders to rate and review, which I guess worked. I also wish we could complete the session without having to pause it and that it had better sync between iPhone and MacBook

title: Inflow - Manage your ADHD
body:
STAY AWAY 

I don’t usually write reviews. But this app inspired. 

You be assaulted by an endless stream of quizzes, that are very hard to focus through, and added, time consuming pointless graphics splash screens and glossy nothingness. Users are completely captive to this endless process, and it is extremely stressful for my adhd.  I devoted close to an hour trying to get into this app and became so frustrated I submitted a support request and detailed, fair and respectful feedback for them to approve. 

They didn’t reply to my message content, then they charged me $200, one week after downloading for a trial, and trying my best to communicate with the developers about my situation and asking for help. 

Stay away from this app. It was developed by developers, for developers, without an understanding of what adhd users will actually think and feel. This app will profit off us, inappropriately, because adhders are particularly susceptible to bait and switch predatory pricing tactics. We already had an adhd tax, we don’t need Trojan horse solutions making the situation worse. 

STAY AWAY

body:
Real person, I promise, and if you read some of my other reviews I can be highly critical and sound like a Karen quite honestly. I wasn’t even looking for an app like this mental health wise or gaming wise. The types of videos I watch about having better mental health just kinda popped the ad for this app onto my screen.

I’ve always enjoyed guided meditation along with choose your own adventure games. This app is the best of both worlds! It has peaceful music with therapeutic storyline and prompts or times where you can respond with your own entry. The “narrator” doesn’t speak so the voice that your mind comes up with to read their lines in is all up to your interpretation.

Now, I did get bummed at first upon realizing that there is a tiered payment system after the first 3 levels, however, do not let this run you away! It is only a one time payment! This is in order to help the company grow and it is not at all a money grab like most of the other apps out there! There are 3 different payments you can choose from to continue your journey and all of them are only a one time payment that unlocks everything at that tier permanently, the lowest of which I believe was $13.99 if I remember correctly. So they really do try to make it as affordable as possible. This is just a very small company that needs help in order to grow, so every penny helps.

There is such a creative and kind team behind the Betwixt App. As a player, you can tell that a lot of time and effort went into putting the resources together and creating the story mode adventure. Really great app and just what I never knew I needed!

title: ScreenZen- Screen Time Control
body:
I’ve tried my fair share of screen time apps, and most of them left me frustrated—either because of expensive subscriptions or because they weren’t effective enough. ScreenZen, however, has completely changed my perspective.

What makes it stand out to me is the thoughtful design. Instead of simply blocking apps, it gives you a customizable pop-up that asks if you really want to use one of your daily “passes.” That pause, that question, makes me think twice—and it works. On top of that, the app has a strict cut-off option for when I need firmer boundaries, which I appreciate.

But what impressed me most is their approach to cost. ScreenZen doesn’t demand a subscription. It’s available freely, with the option to support the developers through donations. For people like me who can’t afford to subscribe to dozens of apps (because of medical expenses, in my case), this is an absolute gift. And despite being donation-based, the service is excellent—better than many paid alternatives I’ve tried.

In short, ScreenZen is simple, powerful, and accessible. If you’re looking for a screen time app that respects both your focus and your budget, I highly recommend it.

title: Hush Nag Blocker
body: ### How Hush Works Hush is a content blocker for Safari that focuses on blocking nag screens, such as cookie consent banners and privacy-intrusive tracking scripts. It does this by using a set of rules that target specific scripts and elements on web pages without interacting directly with the site itself. ### Why It Might Be Less Effective Now 1. **Lack of Updates**: The Hush app and its GitHub project have not seen significant updates recently, which might mean it's not keeping up with new tracking techniques and ad implementations. 2. **Advanced Obfuscation**: Some websites employ advanced methods to bypass blockers, which Hush may not be updated to counter. 3. **Evolving Web Standards**: The web is constantly evolving, and without regular updates, any blocker may fall behind in its effectiveness. Checkout the developers GitHub page (found on the website) to see that it’s been inactive 4 years. Thank you Hush for the great service you provided, and I hope to see you again. But now we must find another.

title: Migiri: Porn Blocker & More

I first got Migiri and I was a little skeptical. I had tried other blockers and things, but the fact that Migiri focused or seemed to want to focus on MORE than just blocking, drew me to it.

Before I get on to talking about why I love the app, I will say that I wasn't pleased about not getting notifications from the app or my chosen companion getting emails to celebrate / cheer me on. 

I emailed the Migiri team about the issue and they responded quickly and a few days later, the issue was resolved. It means a lot to be that I, as a user, was treated respectfully, in a timely manner, and heard.

Now, going back to what i've enjoyed from Migiri... I loved that there were some lessons to help me contemplate my addiction and behaviors. I love that one of the lessons helped focus on accepting a relapse and doubling down on the commitment to quit.

I can't say for anyone else, but that lesson really helped me get to understand who I am, what I need, and why I relapse.

So yes, I would suggest this app to anyone who's trying to quit porn. A blocker isn't good enough because there is always a way to circumvent it if you look hard and long.

However, a blocker that also helps you change and grow so that you can some day not need a blocker so well worth the price.

As for all of y'all on this journey, you got this and keep at it. You're not alone and you do matter. I would suggest y'all get this app and also try groups, therapy, blockers, church, and friends.

Every positive relationship is another strand in the net to keep you from falling.

title: Focus Traveller - Flow Timer
body:
I recently switched to FocusTraveller from the Flora app, which I had used for years. It had become virtually unusable because of its glitches. 

I love the intuitive interface of the app, and the graphics are gorgeous. The prompt to take deep breaths are helpful. I love the ability to take breaks and choose your traveler. 

It would be great to see a few valuable features I enjoyed from other productivity apps. 

1. Adding a sense of progression to keep it engaging. In other apps, I liked how spending more time on the app allowed you to unlock new features, like growing new plant species or exploring new areas. It made the experience more rewarding and less monotonous. Introducing a similar gamification element here would be a fantastic addition and help keep users motivated- maybe adding different maps to explore or customization for your traveler (like clothes/accessories or a pet that travels with you). 

1.5: Special badges- the Flora app not only allowed users to unlock new plant species to grow as they spent more time focusing; they also gifted a badge for every plant that was grown either with a friend or through a paid session (putting money on the line). Seeing those badges was very rewarding, so even when I ran out of plants to unlock, I focused on earning both badges for every plant I had. Visual reinforcement for progression is KEY to keeping users interested in coming back to the app. 

2. Allowing users to put money on the line. Flora allowed users to choose a value (between $5-$100) to be charged if they took a break or left the app. This is useful for those who need an extra push to stay focused on their task- it helped me a LOT during finals season.

3. The ability to block distracting apps during the focus session. This adds an extra barrier to simply scrolling on social media while the session is running. I benefitted a LOT from this feature, as I sometimes open distracting apps without even thinking when I get bored. 

4. The ability to add friends without Game Center. I very, very frequently studied with friends through the Flora app. It provides an extra layer of accountability. Providing a QR code or a username to add friends through would be convenient. 

I have diagnosed ADHD, but these features kept me coming back to the Flora app for a little less than four years. I really love FocusTraveller and would love to see the aforementioned updates. I think they would enhance the experience and keep distracted users engaged and coming back for more. 

I hope these suggestions were helpful. Thanks for reading my review!

body:
Приложение, в целом, неплохое. Из бесплатного контента очень нравятся медитации из раздела «экстренная помощь» - когда нужно проработать тревогу, страх, печаль. Такие 5-минутки очень эффективны, а голос актеров позволяет полностью сконцентрироваться на смысле. Нравится содержание уведомлений и то, что можно управлять их регулярностью. 
Абсолютно раздражает то, что ежедневно приходят уведомления с текстом «медитация: такая-то, доступно только сегодня». Я захожу в приложение и в итоге мне по-прежнему недоступна эта медитация. Во-первых, чувствуешь себя обманутым, а во-вторых, это тоже мое время: я обращаю внимание на приложение и захожу проверить, действительно ли сегодня открылось что-то новое. Каждый раз разочарование. 
Также я недовольна тем, что нет полного бесплатного курса. Было бы классно, если бы уроки курса по запросу (самооценка, спокойствие, сон и тд) открывались ежедневно, чтобы сформировалась какая-то привычка слушать медитации не только вообще, но и в вашем приложении. 
Такие вот мысли.
Прошу обратить внимание на абзац, начинающийся с «абсолютно раздражает», потому что именно ощущение намеренного ввода в заблуждение заставило меня оставить этот отзыв. 🙄🫠

The app lets you create typographical lists of app shortcuts on your home screen. However, adding apps is a hassle because the search results often show irrelevant apps or give "No results found" if you scroll too fast.

But this shortcut is their to launch another shortcut already in your library. So when you finally have it setup and tap one of these shortcuts on your home screen, you’re taken to your Shortcuts library where it launches that actual shortcut.

Ive had clearspace a long time, and the change was not immediate. I have a 189 day streak right now and i only noticed a change like two weeks ago. The screen time is the smaller part of why I like this app though; what I really like is the pushup challenge. I used to do cross country but quit a long time ago, and when i started doing the pushup challenge, it was the first time in about two years i saw an improvement in my body and not a steady decline in my physical condition. I did 1 pushup per 3 minutes for a 31 day challenge, and at the end i noticed it was much easier to do pushups, so I started a 100 day challenge with 1 pushup per 1 minute. I’m a week and a half in and I suddenly realized that over the last month my body has gotten visibly more strong, especially my chest. I can also see my abs more clearly. This little improvement and the fact that I was doing around 50 pushups to 70 pushups a day inspired me, and I finally started working out for the sake of working out again. I lift weights, do pushups, and do core sometimes. It’s not something I spend a huge amount of time on, but im seeing a gradual improvement in my physical condition and willingness to improve my habits. I highly recommend downloading this app.

P.S.
There are a few things wrong with the app; i wish i could put limits on more than one app for free, i uninstalled youtube to keep myself off shorts as an alternative to reels; however, this isnt a huge problem cause there isnt much to do on my phone anyway. 
I also notice that the app has a very hard time realizing if im doing pushups unless im looking straight at the camera and going slow; this hasnt bothered me too much, but sometimes I’ll do like twenty pushups for ten minutes. Usually it works a lil better when im in short sleeves or when i turn on a bunch of lights.
That’s all! Amazing app.

title: Ochi: Block Websites & Apps
body:
I have been looking for a blocker for both apps and websites while I am at work. After quite some research, I settled on Ochi, which is really easy to set up and works on both macOS and iOS. Ochi has all the modern perks of a native Apple app, supporting Shortcuts and iCloud syncing among other things. The developer is very responsive to support questions. The free version is beyond generous, offering a single filter that can be configured to block an unlimited number of apps and websites together. 

The only major limitation on macOS so far is that website blocking does not work on Firefox (for which I use LeechBlock, an open-source extension). Web blocking works very well on Safari and Chrome-based browsers. On iOS there are more system limitations, but Ochi has managed to accomplish a lot within these limits. It is particularly clever to use the Focus mode for macOS control of Ochi filters across Apple devices.

title: Ochi: Block Websites & Apps
body: As a longtime Freedom user I've been dissapointed with that app's lack of new features, especially the lack of support for Shortcuts, so I was really intrigued when I read about this app on 9to5Mac. Unfortunately, it just reallly doesn't feel ready for primetime yet. In my experience so far on an M1 Mac, the app has been pretty much unusable, with lots of beach wheels and complete unresponsiveness. Even worse, when I tried to set up a filter with specific apps blocked, it ended up blocking apps I had NOT selected, ones that were CRUCIAL to my workflow. It was a huge waste of time and really frustrating. I had to force quit it with the activity monitor, and I'll be putting it away for now until these bugs get addressed.

body:
I am 15 and my mom used this app for me instead of the built in screen time. It was personally embarrassing for any of my peers to see that not only did I have screen time as a high schooler but I had an app called Ohana. The app made it so my mom could see everything on my phone, and would look at everything on it which made me feel like I had no privacy in anything. Because not only could she track me but she could control and see everything on it. She would constantly question me on websites I was on which led to many misunderstandings and fights that could have been avoided. This also made me feel like I had no control over anything which crushed my self esteem, and would make me feel constantly angry with her and her need to control my life. It’s stupid to center your life around a phone, but to my generation we need a little freedom and a phone is a big step of freedom and having that taken away feels terrible.
So not only did this app lead to many fights that could have been avoided it made me have a sense of no freedom and caused me to get made fun of by my friends. If you get this app please don’t use it as my parents have.

title: ADHD Lifehacks For Adults Pro
body:
Unlike Neurotypical folks, I need to see/read/hear something MANY times before it becomes a ‘ Go To’ or becomes an Action to develop a Habit around. I ‘BELIEVE’ that by saving info in an ADHD File I my Cloud, Printing out a copy & pining it to my “L👀K Center” or even flagging a page in a book will cause me to “Re•Visit” these GREAT IDEAS when I’m ready to write them in my Habit Tracker section of my BuJo…. WRONG…..

THIS APP is the ONLY WAY THAT WORKS! It is almost Gamified in that it ‘Pops Up’ each day all fresh & new! However, I’ve now developed a routine with a digital list & the “Latest” hack as an entry…. I then review this list at the end of the month and add on to my Habit-Tracker for the next month.

THIS APP HAS CHANGED MY LIFE! More than ADDitude Website/Magazine App or any other Specialized App for Neurodivergent folks like me!

I’d also like to add that I’m 57 years old…. You CAN teach an old dog NEW TRICKS!!!  

THANK YOU SO MUCH FOR THIS APP!!!!

title: BePresent: Screen Time Control
body: I have a very strong mindfulness meditation practice, but I still find myself occasionally scrolling for too long on Instagram and using my phone as a distraction. This app seemed like a wonderful idea and I love the name and concept, so I thought I'd give it a try. Like some others have stated, it offers you a free trial followed by a year long subscription, and if you don't accept that it will offer you 60% off. The catch is if you take the discount, you don't get a free trial and they charge you right away. And I very quickly realized that the app doesn't work for me. It has too many features and things I don't need and I actually find it a little bit overwhelming and excessive. That said, I do think it could be helpful for a lot of people. I find that downtime is a suitable option for me and basically just a simplified version of what this app is. But if you like having a streak and a bunch of different options to connect with people, track progress, receive gifts and reminders, and if phrases like "please I'm begging you open instagram" deters you from opening it, you might love this app. I'd personally rather work on my mindfulness practice and addiction to distraction as a whole which also helps lower screen time. Apple denied my two requests for a refund, they deny 95% of my requests which is very frustrating because they are all authentic and valid requests, but I reached out to the company and they were very friendly and did offer me a one time refund after I explained what happened. And I appreciate that they responded and offered this refund which most companies don't. I don't think it's a scam, but I did tell them that I felt like I was sort of tricked into buying a subscription and for an app that is meant to improve your well-being, to push so hard for someone to make a purchase just doesn't feel very aligned with their purpose. However, I do understand that everyone needs to make a living and if this app does help people use their phone less then that is wonderful.

title: Unpluq: Reduce Screen Time
body:
Get  premium. Get the RFID tag. If you’re serious about reducing your screen time, this is the app you’ve been looking for.

Just set your anti-distraction schedule, then leave the RFID tag that lets you break that schedule in a hard-to-reach area. title: Unpluq: Reduce Screen Time
body:
I like the idea of this app and even bought the tag to help me further break some bad habits. I’m continuing to use the app and tag but have noticed several bugs or defects while I’ve used it. On occasions when I have temporarily disabled a couple of my schedules but not all of them, the schedules that I have disabled continue to run, restricting access to my apps. For example, I have a schedule that restricts apps from 8 AM - 5PM, M-F and another that blocks shopping apps 24/7 while I was on an no-spending challenge. I disabled the 8-5/M-F schedule because I was on vacation but wanted to keep the shopping apps blocked and the app continued to block my other apps that were in the 8-5/M-F schedule. I ended up having to also disable my shopping 24/7 schedule to get access to the apps in my 8-5/M-F schedule. 

Today at 7:15 AM, I needed to disable my 8-5/M-F just for today so clicked on the prompt “Disable for Today” when I was asked and all of the apps listed in that schedule became blocked. First off, I just disabled it and second off, it wasn’t even 8 AM so even if it wasn’t disabled they shouldn’t have been blocked.

These inconsistencies, bugs/defects are annoying and frustrating especially because I have the tag and can’t just unblock my apps without either scanning it (which is annoying because I but the tag in the garage on a high shelf to add friction) or use emergency mode. I’d like to eventually shut off emergency mode so I can’t use that loophole but can’t do that with the issues that I’m having.

Again, love the idea and if you don’t have to make changes to your set schedules then it’s awesome. I’ve found that I’m more present and focused at work and during time with my family but those glitches are pretty annoying. Had I not bought the tag, I’d probably be deleting and trying a different app but I’m going to stick with this one for a while longer in hopes of improvement.

title: Unpluq: Reduce Screen Time
body:
This is one of the only blocking apps that allows you to scan a QR code to unlock. I have one stuck to the fridge so that if I want to use a distracting app I have to go physically to the fridge, which works quite well. Unfortunately, it doesn’t allow you to lock it to a specific QR code, so I can bypass it by scanning any random QR code, eg I can scan any pass/ticket in Wallet on my watch. Since I wear my watch to bed this somewhat negates the barrier to midnight doomscrolling of having to trek downstairs to the kitchen. I’m mostly successful with pretending I didn’t discover that, but it does require a bit more willpower.

(To the devs: the alarm clock app Alarmy allows you to lock it to a specific QR code, if you want inspiration! It seems to work by just storing the text it read from the code. This allows me to generate different codes and specify for example that I have to go to my exercise bike to shut the alarm up some mornings, and just the kitchen other mornings. Similarly it might be useful to be able to block some apps with a QR code I put on a keyring and other apps with a QR code that stays at home for example.)

I figure it’s possibly intentional if they’re trying to funnel me towards buying the actual unpluq device, but I’m happy enough paying monthly, I shouldn’t have to also buy a fairly pointless object to make the app work better.

If they ever implement specific QR codes I’ll increase to 5 stars.

Finally I think this is more of a limitation from iOS than Unpluq, but it would seem you have to use only Safari if you want website blocking to work. Ideally I’d still be able to use Chrome and only block eg news websites and Reddit.

title: BetterSleep: Relax and Sleep
body:
BetterSleep was my primary sleep app from 2014 to 2025: unfortunately, the app has changed to try to capitalize on other sleep app markets in ways that have made the app hard to use.

As a soundscape app, the ratio of free-to-upcharged noise options has drifted with updates over the years. The most recent app update reduced access to sounds to the single digits: insult to injury, mixes that are user made and have been in use for years are still stored but inaccessible. Someone new to the app wouldn't be able to build mixes they like and get to know the value of the sound library, and the change leaves a sour taste for a long time free user familiar with the library.

There's been a rapid pivot to serve as a sleep hygiene management app, but it unfortunately also doesn't have features that are competitive. BetterSleep does not offer wide ranging integration with sleep tracker devices, which would be the biggest draw that could tip the scales towards investing in a membership on top of my fitness tracker app's membership.

I'd really love to see BetterSleep refind its footing as a competitive free soundscape app and (sleep tracker-friendly!) sleep management features for an additional cost.

The Bad:

title: Relax Meditation: Guided Mind
body: So I got this app around maybe two(ish) years ago and loved it. I suffered from extreme anxiety, agoraphobia and had panic attacks almost every other day. Life was pretty excruciating. After trying the sample meditations I started to notice that my attacks were coming a bit less often. I went ahead and bought the full app (that’s right, bought, not rented, not subscribed, bought, for a one time price) as well as talked my wife into trying one of their sleep/clock apps. Everything was great. Over time after meditating around the same time every day, my anxiety almost disappeared. I eventually did most of the meditations multiple times and with my anxiety not quite gone but better than it had been in years, I sat it down for a while while I waited for some new meditations. I’m not gonna lie, I didn’t use the app for a long time after that, maybe 6 months or more but it never left my home screen, I never uninstalled it or anything. Eventually my anxiety started bothering me again back around Christmas so I pulled out my handy dandy anxiety busting meditation app only to find that the app that I BOUGHT for just a couple of dollars had been taken back from me and that I could now rent it BACK from them for a ridiculous amount of money a month. My progress is all still there, I’m just locked out of it. I understand the devs have a right to make money and to charge whatever they see fit. I just don’t think it’s right to sell someone something only to take it back away from them and try to rent it back out to them again for thousands of more dollars. If it was to be changed I feel like the changes (a monthly subscription fee) should have only applied to people who downloaded/installed the app AFTER the decision to change it from a flat price to a subscription fee had been made and not forced upon those who had already paid for the full version. I was originally gonna leave a review around Christmas when I discovered what had happened but was just blown away and I guess hurt. I didn’t want to talk or even think of it. Smh

title: Breathing Zone
body:
I’ve been using this app for a week after comparing and test driving a few others.  I really appreciate the way you can start at a number of breaths and then the app progressively adjusts to the desired number of breaths.  

However, it could be better.  While I like how you  can set your target number of breaths, the app is missing the ability to control how long it takes for you to get to that desired number of breaths.  For example, if you’re doing a 20 minute session it would be nice to be able to set to have it slow down over the first 5 minutes... or 10... or whatever your preference is.  As it is, I know it goes slower but I have no idea how long it takes, nor is it possible to see how many breaths you’re doing at any particular time, which beings me to...

While the session screen is moderately cool with the pulsing orb thing, it’s kind of useless.  More helpful would be an option for an easy to see (always on while using the app) display of how much time is left in your current session as well as the current breaths per minute.  I’d like to be able to glance briefly at the screen and see how I’m doing and if I’m at my desired breath rate.  

Another minor complaint is that the app pauses very easily - by just touching the screen - which I’ve unintentionally done many times while in a session.  A more deliberately styled pause button would be better.  

Not a bad app but these adjustments would make the app perfect for me and one that I would use much more personally and be able to recommend much more highly to others.

Hi, Pro subscriber here. I sent a message on August 23rd through the app about an issue I'm having but I still haven't received a response as of yet, so I'm following up with this review.

After recently updating my phone to iOS 18.6, the Timer+ app hasn't been working properly. The issue involves the widget or live update not showing the remaining time on the Lock Screen.

I have a 20-minute countdown timer that I use for time blocking purposes, which works fine if I don't add or subtract time from the 20-minute default. However, once I add time, the Lock Screen shows the initial time that the countdown started with, frozen at that time. This also happens with the quick timer feature.

I want to be able to lock my screen and not have the app open in order to see the remaining time, as it helps save battery. Otherwise, I can't really use the app since it requires too many steps to check the time, which would be disappointing. This has been my go-to productivity app for the past 3 years.

What's the point of paying for a Pro subscription if there's no support to help with issues? I'm frustrated that despite reaching out nearly two weeks ago, I haven't heard anything back.

*UPDATED REVIEW 9-6-2025*

As soon as I posted this review the App Store refreshed and allow me to update the app which is now better than ever. This app is 5 stars ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

title: Strong Workout Tracker Gym Log
body: I’ve been using this app for 5 or 6 years and have really enjoyed it. The recent update, however, has removed some of the most useful features. I used to be able to sort my templates alphabetically. I used a numbering system in the template names to make them sort in the order I wanted, placing the newest ones on top. Can’t do that anymore. When adding an exercise to a template, the app will use the same weights & reps as the last time you performed that exercise, which is handy. If I modified a weight or rep count, it used to roll that change down to all the subsequent sets. It no longer does that - I have to update every single set by hand. It’s a pain when coach programs 10x3 with +10 lbs from the last week. Those 2 changes have made the app significantly less useful to me. It’s still nice to have all my history in one app though.

body:
I love this app and have been a subscriber for nearly a decade. I recommend it every chance I get, and typically meditate daily as a part of my mental health routine. From courses to help with specific challenges, to sleep sounds and music; content for adults as well as for kids - this app covers a lot of ground without making meditation feel like a chore.

There are a few other reviews talking about needing new content. Content has been added, but it’s been in very particular areas. There have been some new courses added for work life balance in recent years, new sleep sounds get added semi-regularly, and they’ve added the Therapy and AI features recently. While these options are great, they don’t quite align with my needs. My daughter uses the Sesame Street bedtime stories to help her fall asleep, but there haven’t been any new ones added in ages (nor has there been any unbranded children’s stories added to cover the gap)

It would also help if there was more content around temper and outbursts/triggers (and the SOS content is really limited here)

It would also be great if there were reminders to do stress and anxiety check-ins when they open - and it would also be great if those check-ins also reported data back to the Apple Health app.

body:
I don’t want to sound dramatic but it actually did save my life.

To summarize myself, let me just say that I’m a nontraditional premedical student, meaning that I started college late and suddenly decided to become a doctor of all things.

I applied during the 2018/19 cycle and had one interview at UC Davis and was rejected. I was 29 yrs old at the time and it was just heart-wrenching to believe that everything that worked towards didn’t lead to an acceptance. I didn’t know what to do with my life anymore. It was so stressed and depressed and plus, I had used up so much of my money saved for this entire process that I was near broke.

I needed to inject some urgency and accountability back into my life. That’s when I decided to actively look for an app that would hold me accountable for the 24hrs in a day.

Long story short, I started to prepare for the MCAT again. With this app, I took the MCAT 2 more times. I did all of this studying while having a high pressure position at a fertility clinic. On February 25th of 2020, I got my score for my 4th MCAT and I got a very competitive score.

What does this mean? Well, now I have a shot at any US medical programs across the country and most importantly, I can take one step closer to reaching my dream of becoming a doctor.

It all started from using this app to measure literally EVERYTHING in my life: sleep, shower/washing up, socializing, study, eating, working, running errands, driving, gym etc... the list goes on. I wish there is a way to upload a pic of my schedule because it’s humanly impossible to have done what I did WITHOUT this app.

Yes, I accounted for literally every single minute of my life for about 1yr straight. Funny thing is that I’m certain that I will continue to use this app for the rest of my life.

ATracker, thank you so much for this app. Your app got me here. So many times, I wanted to give up. I lost count on how many times I thought about ending my life as well. I just keep at it and believed in my process. Today, my world looks so different. What time to be alive. 

Thank you.

body:
ATracker Pro has enough features that if you log your time diligently and with intelligently chosen categories, you really will have charts and graphs showing you exactly where your time goes. The ability to categorize specific tasks into larger baskets, and then view your time expenditure in categories rather than tasks, is a particularly cool feature. The pie chart of time can show you for today, this week, this month, or a selected range of dates; I find this very handy. You can also see bar graphs of time spent in specific tasks by period of time. 

I’ve been using this for three months now. As a result I have quit social media, quit Netflix and Hulu, subscribed to the New York Times and the New Yorker, almost finished writing a book I had abandoned, and finally established a truly daily exercise routine (just walking for 40 minutes right now but I plan to upgrade to biking when I feel it is time). Knowing specifically how you are wasting your time, minute by minute, makes it no chore to start spending that time better. It’s a pleasure to choose the “Categories” feature on my pie chart and see almost none of that pie chart showing “Wasted Time.”

body: I have a 2 year old (almost 3) and we had issues with transitions. We used to set Alexa timer but he would get upset when that was done. Now we use this and it’s a world of difference. We set the timer and show him how much time he has and every so often show him how much time he has left during activity. When it gets close to being done I ask if he wants to want it explode. He understands when timer is done he is done with activity (usually playing for a few extra minutes) and is actually happy to go on with his routine. We have not had as much whining after timer is done and when we have it’s been minimal. I think being able to SEE how much time he has left is great and he is able to understand that much more then being told he has 5 minutes.

I really like this alo moves app.  I have been doing Yoga for 6 years and I guess over time I have become a bit particular.  I like my instructors to know what they are doing, and I want my yoga classes to be a relaxing and unwinding end of my day.  The Alo moves Yoga instructors are top notch. 

 But the second piece of what I am looking for in a class is relaxing atmosphere, which is where the music comes in.  The music should help me to relax and unwind.  Most of the music on the app is great, but some classes have music that includes lyrics.  Here is the problem.  When there are lyrics in the song, and the instructor is also speaking… that means there are two voices at the same time. Maybe it’s me, but my brain absolutely cannot make sense of two voices speaking/singing simultaneously.  It may sound weird but it gives me some sort of anxiety because my brain can’t choose what to listen to…which is the opposite of what I want in a yoga class.  I want to relax. 

Please take out songs with lyrics for yoga classes, or give us the ability to choose our style of music.  I will then give a 5 star rating, as I really do like this app.  Thanks!!

title: BB - Screen Time & App Blocker
body:
I almost never write reviews but this app is fantastic. There are plenty of apps that offer similar services, but this one offers the most for free, and the premium option is far more accessible as well as it’s a one-time purchase of a very reasonable $5. It also offer more privacy since you don’t make an account, everything is just stored locally on your device. The schemas are pretty straightforward to set up, and are definitely effective (especially with strict mode enabled). It’s also great that it works on iPads as well, exactly the same as on your phone, which I found was not the case with comparable (much more expensive!) apps.

I have just a couple of suggestions:
1. The ability to pause schemas for a set amount of time, e.g. “Pause for 30 minutes” or “Pause for 2 days.” Things like that. Or also pause until certain times like “Pause until 11:00” etc.
2. I don’t know how possible this is in terms of maintaining privacy, but it would be useful to have an in-app screen time tracking feature, where you could see how much time you spent in total, but also see apps marked as productive vs unproductive (either automatically marked by BB or manually selected by the user) to see how much productive vs unproductive screen time you had for that day/week, etc. 

I know it’s just one person building this app on the side, so I completely understand if these recommendations aren’t possible for such a small operation, or if they’d require functions the app simply can’t access due to iOS limitations, but they are just some ideas I had.

Overall, this app is amazing, especially considering its price (or lack thereof), and I highly recommend it to anyone looking to cut back on their screen usage. :)

The app can go further with the power of Shortcuts. I mostly use this app to block apps while a focus is turned on, since most of my focus settings have scheduled times anyway. The BEST thing that I use this app for isn’t even an advertised feature. I call it my panic button. In shortcuts you can make a fake app cover (tutorials on how to do this are online), and mine functions as an app I can press that instantly hides certain app groups. All in all, this app has saved me literally more times than I can count and I would recommend it to any kid with insanely restrictive parents

title: Roots: Screen Time Control
body: I have a pretty bad phone addiction, and I got Roots to support me by offering the time limits for apps and also blocked off time. I paid for the subscription so I could have monk mode and the most access to Roots’ offerings. I had to stop using app specific time limits because I would find myself locked out of apps that I needed after only being awake for three minutes. It would tell me that I timed out of my four hours of time limit for a work necessary app at 6:03 AM when I hadn’t even opened that app. the screen would have the accurate time for my screen usage, but the time limit would be locked anyways. And here I am sitting on my lunch, hoping to have 15 minutes of downtime before heading back into my stressful workday to find that my apps are locked once again when I have no active time limit, and no active blocked out time running. I paid around $30 to find my phone bricked more often than not and while it has significantly reduced my phone time, I also want to be able to use my phone when I find it appropriate. I really hope that these issues can be fixed, and I will be seeking some sort of refund or at least some amount of cheat days added to my account because I should not have to use an entire cheat day that I earned by following my goals because I want to be on my phone for 15 minutes and I’m finding myself locked out. It does not seem fair to the user and I am very dissatisfied with that.

title: Grit: Daily Habit Tracker
body:
I’ve been using Grit for a short time, and it has quickly become one of my favorite productivity tools. The app’s design is sleek, intuitive, and highly customizable, making it easy to track habits and stay on top of my goals. I especially love the ability to set specific goals and track progress over time—it’s a game-changer for habit-building.

However, the one area where Grit falls just short of perfection is the lack of support for non-repeatable, one-time tasks. While the app excels at habit tracking, it would be incredibly useful to have the ability to add one-off tasks that don’t factor into the overall habit metrics. This functionality would consolidate all my to-do items into one app and eliminate the need for other tools like Apple’s Notes.

This minor shortcoming is the only thing keeping Grit from being a perfect five-star, daily-use application for me. With the addition of non-repeatable tasks, this app would truly be unbeatable.

Despite this, I can’t recommend Grit enough—it’s a fantastic tool for anyone looking to take control of their habits and achieve their goals. Here’s hoping this already great app continues to get even better!

body: I wanted to like this but it’s just not helpful for me. I did the one week free trial.  I tried to play this daily for the past 6 days, I think I got 4 days in, but I just don’t think it’s beneficial for me.  While I’m playing I feel anxious and agitated. I also hold my breath. The pace is so fast, the angle of the phone is not good for my neck or wrists and as I do better it speeds up so I never feel successful. The repetitive sounds may be designed to be a purposeful distraction, but I find them so irritating. There’s the ‘oh crud’ when you miss your target (but it’s strange b/c I am hitting the thumb button but it is almost off the screen and  but not quite but still registers as having missed it) and there’s the loud command not to miss the power zones &  “you’re slowing down!!!” After missing only one. At the pace it goes and with multitasking happening of course I’m going to miss one or two, I don’t need that startling distracting reminder which will only make me miss more. The game is repetitive and it continuously has me targeting blue creatures—don’t know if that’s by design because on the rare occasion I’d need to target a red or a yellow creature I often forgot and went for blue by mistake b/c I was so used to it. There’s also all these extraneous bells and whistles with the points, purchasing different characters and uniforms and a farm but I don’t know what any of that is or how it would benefit me from the standpoint of treating adhd. It actually seems more like a gratuitous dopamine fix that I’m not interested in. The stats that are shared on my progress mean very little to me because they aren’t explained in detail. Overall I don’t see this as having any value for me personally and certainly not at 149 dollars a year.

This is a very useful app and could even be a money/life saver if someone gets a hold of your cell phone and has an idea of your passwords (or can get them out of you, somehow). After using it for a couple of months now, I will gladly rate it a 4 1/2 as it is, but it has a potentially dangerous flaw and two programming, nuisances, to wit:

- It should offer the option of disguising the app icon AND NAME to something innocuous, both in picture and name. There is another “App Lock“ offered in the App Store, that allows for this possibility, i.e. changing the app's icon to something like a calculator, for example, but, strangely enough, does not allow the user to change the app's name. Even though the app's icon (and name) can be hidden from view in your cell phone main screen, the app is readily available via a search of your installed apps, where it shows the icon and name (and it even starts with an “A” so…). I installed this app, and use it constantly, because my son (who is a programmer) recommended it to me, and I thought that I had achieved almost total security from this standpoint. However, a few days ago, talking to an Uber driver, regarding the cases in which people have had their bank accounts cleaned out via the app installed in their cell phones, he mentioned to me that I could install an app that would hide, the icons, the conclusion to this being that, if an Uber driver knows about this type of app, undoubtedly crooks would also be aware of these applications and would search for them in the cell phone and, if they also have you, they can beat the pulp out of you until you tell them the PIN and, once they have it, they can deactivate the “Hide“ feature of the app, and then proceeded to get from you the various passwords and PINs needed to transfer money out of your accounts (some of which will even be, no doubt, set up for facial recognition). The app should allow the user to completely disguise it, BOTH THE ICON AND THE NAME, so that it could not be easily found and deactivated, thust increasing security considerably.  Much easier to "explain" that you do not have any financial apps installed "because of the dangers involved...".

Now, for the programming flaws:

- The PIN used to lock/unlock apps is the same used to access the app itself. They should be allowed to be different, i.e. have one “master pin“ to activate/deactivate the various features in the app and other pin(s) to block/unblock block apps.

- Finally, when when one is selecting apps to be blocked, or hidden, the program has a rather disconcerting tendency to return to the main app categories screen when one has already chosen a category and began to choose individual apps to be blocked or hidden, and you have to start all over again.

It would be fantastic if the developers could fix at least the main problem (i.e. disguising the app itself so that it would not provide any clue as to its true identity and purpose)

title: Llama Life ADHD Routine & Task
body:
I love this. I can set up a morning routine and then it counts down each step of events and how long I expect it to take. Seeing a list with an active count down timer really helps me visualize what I need to do and how much time I have to do it, rather than getting sidetracked.

That said, I really wish this app had some other features (because now I have to use other apps in supplement to this one, which sometimes makes it a bit inconvenient). 
— I wish the in app sound would offer more than just relaxing nature noises but rather a clock/timer tick sound or a water droplet sound that CONTINUES to play even if you exit the app/start playing music. 
— This is one of the biggest things- the timer should be able to show and continue running in the Lock Screen or at least create an interactive widget feature. If I close out of the app and I play music or something, the notification simply says “timer will keep running” rather than a current count down of your task / and the ability to mark as complete/etc. This is the biggest inconvenience of the app compared to other promodoro or task management apps. 
IF the second feature was available, this would genuinely be an app I could not live without and would be such an immense game changer.

For example, if I need to do my morning tasks I know it’s a total of 1.5hrs, but I know I have to leave the house in 1hr- then I can adjust the list of tasks and move the tool to show the exact time ie. 8:43AM that it would take to complete all the morning tasks.

I love knowing how long it will take to complete a group of tasks and when that group would be complete. I have over 20+ tasks in a given day. Llama Life is the only way I get these things done!
