title: Llama Life ADHD Routine & Task
body:
This is time-boxing for time-boxing-challenged people!! I have tried for years to time box (after other productivity hacks also failed) only to get off track and wind up overwhelmed and discouraged. I actually quit even trying because I knew I would just waste time replanning and re-replanning if the time slipped. And here is the thing Llama Life taught me. Time sometimes does slip. And it’s not a reflection on me. Sometimes a task just takes longer or an interruption happens. And the day isn’t a failure. 

Llama Life has just enough flexibility to adapt to the day’s situation. But not so much that you could go down a rabbit hole playing around in the app instead of moving through the day’s to-do’s. 

I am a paper planner person and have been looking for which one to buy for the new year. I’m so glad I found LL before I purchased my annual planner because I won’t need a day planner at all, just a simple place for my goals and projects. I trust Llama Life to help me keep my days focused and productive. And even fun!!

title: Llama Life ADHD Routine & Task
body:
For years, there has been a 30/30-shaped hole in my heart, and I have bounced from app to app searching for a worthy replacement. I found the Llama Life website a few weeks ago and was disappointed to see that it was via Internet only, but then I was almost immediately thrilled to read that an iOS app was to release within the month. Talk about perfect timing! 

Words cannot convey how much this app means to me. As an ADHD woman whose sense of time is vestigial at best, finding a app that works with my brain is like birthday and Christmas rolled into one. 30/30 worked for me, and then it just… went away. 😭 I mourned that app the way other people might mourn lost family members. There is no telling how much time and money I’ve wasted searching for a replacement, but the search is finally over! HUZZAH. (That’s what the kids say nowadays, right??)

To the developers of Llama Life, thank you thank you THANK YOU for all of your hard work. All of the features, the colors, emoji, the ability to break tasks down, to save routines, to easily enter times, the end time estimate, the planned vs. actual time, the divider bar… This app feels like it was designed especially for me. I cannot wait to see where you take it, and I’ll be a subscriber all the way!

title: Propel: ADHD Games for Adults
body:
After downloading and playing this game for ~ 45 minutes, I came across several claims that caused me to question the integrity of the developers. 

1) upon opening the game, one of the first screens claims something to the effect of, “#1 downloaded ADHD app/game.” Given that Propel currently has <600 reviews and the App Store doesn’t indicate # of downloads, it seems safe to say that statement is misleading. (I understand that such statements have become more normalized, but that doesn’t make the en any less deceitful.)

2) After answering the demographic and “let’s create your plan” questions, I was faced with the option to sign up for a “3-day free trial” followed by a $49.99 annual subscription fee. I clicked “see other plans” and was surprised to find the annual plan offered for $39.99 “(no free trial)”. Charging subscribers that opt to use the trial $10 more than those that subscribe sans the trial does not equal “free”; rather, it equals $10/3 days, or $3.33/day.

3) Finally, I played almost every game at least twice.  I’m apparently quite good compared to all the other users because I scored better than 93-95% players on EVERY game I played…including the game that I quit four times (number sort with the moving tiles). Quitting the game resulted in a ZERO score every time, and I STILL scored higher than 93% AND 94% of other players! According to this game, I’m decently bright (it is the #1 downloaded ADHD game 😉) but I can’t figure out how I could improve my standing -within minutes! - with the lowest possible score.    Assuming that the lowest possible score is ZERO (were negative scores possible, I would have received one based on how many moves I made before quitting), it’s not statistically possible for someone who scores 0 (the lowest possible score) to have outperformed 93% of users, because no one can score worse than 0. 
This statistical & coding oversight led me to conclude that the ego-boosting performance stats at the end of games are in place only to keep players playing. Presenting users with a sense of achievement is valuable…especially to the developer. 

If the developer is truly interested in helping those with ADHD (or anyone), they need to attend to the studies that indicate that honest, direct feedback is far more beneficial than sugar-coated or insincere. Instead of spitting out false numbers, consider offering tips on how to improve their gameplay. You ask for and benefit from in-app feedback so you can improve your game; extend the same courtesy to your users.

I used to be a very productive powerhouse back in the day before a child and all of the daily urgent responsibilities that have now inundated my life.  I am barely able to keep up now and the last two years have been very miserable for me.  I looked into getting a life coach to help me feel motivated and tap into my passion but also to help me stay organized and on track however after being quoted between 6000 and $7000 I realize that that was not a path that I could pursue. I know that I really need personalized help somebody to be interested and ask me what’s going on and ask follow-up questions and pitch ideas on how to move forward and so I looked at AI assisted task managers and after testing about four different ones I landed on this one.  It is really really amazing and I haven’t used all of the features yet, but I’m really impressed. Of course there are some bugs and kinks that need to be ironed out because I think this app is relatively new, but I really believe in their approach and I wanted to leave this review to thank them and make sure that I can contribute to helping the team and the product to continue growing and providing such valuable support. Maybe I didn't use the app long enough to discover more functions, but it seems as though the only other useful functions the app provides are the ability to select an accountability partner, access to daily tips (see next comment), and a self-evaluation function.

If you’re thinking about trying this app, just be careful — and set a calendar reminder to cancel. You won’t get one from them.

title: Productivity - Daily Planner
body:
This truly is the very best application to plan and manage your life. I upgraded to the Pro version after only a week of using it.

I have been using this app for about a year now, and this latest update is very beautiful!

There are still a few tweaks/implementations that need to be addressed:
- Remove the login screen whenever we load the app.
- Morning Routines, Daily Checkin, and Reflection reminders do not work properly. I set the time to be different than the default time, but it kept on reminding me at the app's default set time.
- Routines that are tied to a Major Goal do not automatically go away after the goal has been achieved; it remained as a weekly routine indefinitely.
*** Adjusting the routines' time and days of the week does not sync up with the Calendar app; we have to manually edit those times and days on the Calendar app as well if whenever we make adjustment to the routine. I must say that this lack of sync function had irritated me the most, as making minor changes and adjustments to our routines are important to making progress toward our goals. The end-goal should be fixed, but the routines to get there should be flexible.

Even with all the weak points mentioned above (which could be improved in future updates), I still would rate this app as a 5 Stars app. It is definitely one of the most important apps on my iPhone.

I highly recommend anyone that is serious in personal development to purchase the Pro version of this app. It will definitely produce positive changes to your life, if you make a daily habit of using it!

title: AdBlock
body:
Pros: it works. Well. Very few ads slip through, it even blocks them on apps which can turn some freeware games into actually enjoyable games when you don’t get bombarded with ads every few seconds. It’s also very set it and forget it, only once in a couple of months will i go in and toggle or change something.
The meh:
Adding exceptions is a nice feature but can be finnicky at times. I don’t blame the app for this i don’t think there’s a better way to do this on mobile. 
Youtube’s app has the ads baked in so much that you will still get ads even with this adblocker (you can block the ads with exceptions but the videos will stop loading too) BUT the adblocker WORKS on the browser version of youtube so i just stopped using the app altogether and use the ad-free broswer version.
The cons(?): if i understand how this adblocker works, it redirects ALL your phone’s data requests through their servers where it blocks certain url’s from sending data back to your phone. That does mean that theoretically the app makers see ALL your data. Depending on how you feel about this it’s either a dealbreaker or an afterthought. I am already in too far so i just trust them at this point not to misuse my personal info.

title: Flat Tomato (Time Management)
body:
Solid little app. Birds chirping at break times is a nice touch. 

I am adding new info to this review, of the paid version. 

I feel I am more productive and focused as a result of using this app. I have integrated it with my calendar (it required an email to the developer to figure out how to do so), and it is nice to see my Pomodoro's appear on my calendar as a sign of work well done. 

In my previous review (see below), I said that I did not use this often. I am using it more now. And getting more things done. 

A couple of items that are puzzling to me: the awards and feedback and are you cons of stars and moons are not clear to me. 

Also, sometimes the sound cuts out, or the select task option (below the clock on main screen) disappears. Those are minor cosmetic issues that don't stop the app from working very well, but do detract from the final polish of the app. 

Finally, this app asks me to review it. So I finally did… And find that I DID review it earlier. Ah well.

OLD COMMENTS ABOUT OLD VERSION: I don't use it daily, or even nearly daily, but do use it as a mental reboot aid at times when I've been too distracted. It's excellent to help me get on task/stay on task. Also good for getting started on or working through imposing tasks or things I am mentally resisting. 

I upgraded for the calendar tracking list of tasks.

Brainbuddy was exactly what I needed when I first began the fight against porn addiction. In the early stages, the app gave me structure, daily check-ins, and encouragement that helped build the discipline I didn’t yet have on my own. It tracked my streaks, gave insightful content, and helped me reflect on my urges without shame.

What I appreciate most is that Brainbuddy doesn’t just focus on stopping porn — it helps you understand yourself better, build healthier habits, and improve your mindset.

Over time, my journey became more spiritual and personal. I started turning to prayer, reading books, and speaking to God in sujood instead of relying on numbers. But that’s a sign the app worked — it helped me graduate from external motivation to internal strength.

If you’re starting your journey, this app is a powerful ally. Use it, reflect, grow — and when you’re ready to walk without it, do so with gratitude. That’s what I’m doing now.

title: Mindfulness Coach
body:
I’ve read many books, watched many videos and have taught an Eckhart Tolle group of over 200 k people online daily for 4-5 years. This app, hands down is the best tool to step into mindfulness with, beginners or advanced. If Tolle, Donald Walsh etc and nonduality is not getting you anywhere or even if it has, try this. This app is FREE. The people who made this app didn’t make it to monetize off of. They’ve made it to be effective and it is exactly that, effective. You just might be really pleasantly surprised.

The only thing that I would like to see fixed is the counter that keeps track of how many days in a row you use the app. It doesn’t work a lot of times, maybe it is to do with change of month and new year. 

I have used this app every day for almost 4 months and the counter keeps resetting. 

Other than this very minor issue it is hands down the very best mindfulness app that I’ve used over the years. There are also links in the app to get more free exercises that are really awesome as well from iRest. Do yourself a favor and try this app. 

Just because it’s free doesn’t mean it’s poorly designed or that it doesn’t work as well as other mindfulness apps. I have several apps including Wake Up and this one is just as good and effective as that expensive app. 

One other thing that I would love to see covered by this app is “non-striving and non-doing”. If these are understood mindfulness is a cake walk. It is also the same as Wu Wei non-striving and non-doing. Everything that we need is right here in this moment, anything else is a desire and is mind-made suffering because we struggle to achieve a goal in the hopes that when we get to that goal we’ll be happy or when “I retire” I’ll be happy or when “I hit the lotto, I’ll be happy”. 

All those goals that we rely on to make us happy in a future moment is like having a stick with a carrot dangling out in front of us, and we constantly try to catch it or get to, not realizing that the chasing after it, is what creates a LOT of suffering AND takes us away from this moment. 

If we can see this and intentionally just Stop chasing a future moment and be Here Now, we can have peace, joy and contentment. It really is that simple. 

Thank you so much to the developers and VA for making this free and available to everyone, veteran or civilian. 🙏🏼🙏🏼❤️

title: Forest: Focus for Productivity
body:
I’ve had this app since 2017 and used it on and off through college and my working life. It’s one of the best apps on my phone, and I don’t regret paying for it back then. 

Pros: the tree variety is great, especially within the past year with the new monthly challenge plant varieties. The ambient sounds are good. The graphs are great if you use tags and unobtrusive if you don’t. It has a lot of small quality of life features that are really great, like the ability to keep the screen on so you can see the timer running, the ability to run a whitelist of apps in case you need to consult something on your phone quickly without your plant dying, and the fact that you can set the app to keep counting time length. The achievement system helps newbies quickly diversify tree species available to them. The new daily challenges award a small amount of the paid currency so with patience you can unlock previous time limited trees. It’s also significantly spread up collecting gold, which is nice for a casual like me. Most of the tree species have stages of growth depending on how long you plant them, so even with only a few trees to start with you can get some visual interest going. I like planting a variety of the more realistic trees so my little monthly forest is biodiverse, but I appreciate there’s also weird and whimsical trees. There really is a tree or two for everyone.

Cons: The company behind this app has decided to monetize it more, in the form of a paid subscription model instead of a one-time purchase. I understand why they’re doing this, and I think it’s going to be good for the app, but on principle I won’t be using it as I dislike subscription models for productivity apps. Hopefully the free version won’t be too inaccessible. Also, the daily challenge prize collection glitches sometimes, and it’s not actually clear on the screen where to tap to collect it and move on.

Wishlist: Like another commenter, I’d really like the ability to set a little chime when a planting is done that makes it through silent mode. I always have my phone on silent though so maybe this is on me! Other than that, some more water based plants would be nice. I’d love the ability to put a little pond on my forest. The app also has some integration with the Apple Watch but I’d also love something like a quick replant button on the watch that starts the same tree and timer combo again.

title: Influenster: Try & Review
body:
I used to enjoy this app a lot before a lot of the changes have been made, which I feel was unwarranted for. I used to love see the badges for products I reviewed - now that’s gone. Right now, they focus on claim nows mostly, and while I’ve been able to snag some, I feel that they keep offering me things that don’t align with my interests. I’ve been working hard in putting out authentic reviews and reviewing things I’ve personally purchased and it’s not helping with anything any more. 

Like some others have said - if you don’t fit into their mold, you won’t get anything. They’re extremely biased in who they give things to, and I’ve noticed if you’re a POC, you won’t get as much offers as opposed to if you were white. I usually see on Reddit and Instagram of people who get multiple claims daily or weekly, and its always a very similar group of people. What’s worse is that sometimes they give reviews like “I can’t wait to try this!” like hello? You were sent the product to test it? Some of these reviews come off really fake. But who cares if Influenster doesn’t care, am I right?

I never get notifications for claim now nor does the app bother to offer me anything new. I also see some people getting really big ticket items and always wondered if I would get a chance. I have been on the app for over 3 years now, and I’m in mid to late 20s, so I don’t know what I’m doing wrong. I’ve settled that Influenster would never offer me these things given my demographics, and have put less effort into this app compared to what I’ve done in the past. 

I’ve also seen some disturbing posts of people selling ozempic through comments and the fact Influenster is doing nothing to remove these accounts gets concerning. 

Last but not least, I used to get my items within a week of claim. Now I’m lucky if I even get them within the month.

body: This app has a number of good things going for it. It has a clean look and interface, the dashboard and tracking is very useful, and it doesn’t feel as gimmicky as other platforms. However, there are some simple key features missing. First, the heart rate tracking is either too difficult to use or just doesn’t work. Given the number of heart rate trackers on the market now, heart rate data via a smartwatch or other device is way overdue. Second, the timer feature only lets you use either their preselected sounds (which interrupt your meditation by cutting in and out to buffer) and your music library. For those who use Spotify, you are out of luck. Third, also in the timer feature, when the timer ends, the sound abruptly cuts out. It is very jarring to go from your relaxing meditative sound to an abrupt silence. Even if you use a bell to mark the end of the mediation, the ending is abrupt and disturbs some of the mindfulness you were just building. Simply allowing the sounds to continue after the bell (even at a reduced volume) would greatly improve the experience. Overall, good app, but needs improvements before it can be considered the best choice.

title: Parental Control App - OurPact
body:
…but it just didn’t do what I needed it to do. I wanted to give my son an hour of screen time each day, and I wanted it automated through OurPact so I didn’t have to be the bad guy and on top of it constantly. Specifically, wanted him to be able to listen to an hour of music or podcasts. Unfortunately, OurPact’s shut-off mechanism doesn’t work for audio: if a user turns on music with their time allotment, but turns off the screen, the time they spend listening doesn’t count against the allowance. After just a couple days I realized my son was on his headphones longer than an hour (and he sure wasn’t going to point it out to me!). I got in touch with the company to ask for help, and this was their response:

“This particular issue is a bit of a challenge for us since it's related to Apple product functionality and how iOS devices report applications to our software. We hope to have a fix for this in a future update... 
 
In the meantime, we suggest you send a manual 'Grant' to your child's device, then after a few minutes send a manual 'Block'. 
 
This should shut them out of Spotify or whatever app they were trying to access. They may try again, but from our experience, usually, they give up pretty quickly and decide just to call it quits.”

I had suspected it was an Apple thing, not an Out Pact thing, but I had hope. Here’s how I responded:

“In response to your suggestion: "we suggest you send a manual 'Grant' to your child's device, then after a few minutes send a manual 'Block'." This is exactly why we got OurPact in the first place: to do away with the need for "granting" anything. As a parent trying to keep my kids safe online, I am making myself insane trying to give my kids an hour of screen time *OR* listening time each day. When it is me who is getting asked for time, and me who is setting a timer for an hour, and me who is disabling the kids' devices when an hour is up, I take on a part-time job as a police officer. I don't know about you, but as a parent I have to be the bad guy plenty enough already. If, on the other hand, the device was set up automatically to give an hour of screen/listening time when the child wants it, to count down and shut off automatically, it would offer me peace of mind *AND* not require my engagement. Win-win! 

So....if that's not something OurPact can do, then I'd like my money back. Because that's definitely how you promoted it.”

After that, I’ve pinged OurPact twice but they haven’t responded, and I haven’t received a refund. I’m especially unhappy about this because setting the app up on my son’s phone was outrageously invasive and time-consuming. 

I don’t know that there’s any real solution to this problem out there yet. Not OurPact’s fault, but they need to be clear on the limitations in their advertising.

body:
I tried several other timer apps only to be left disappointed. This app however, I paid for the pro version because I believe this app is very promising and the best experience I’ve had so far.

What I love so far from this app: 
1. love that I can set the “ALERT auto repeat” to constantly repeat itself. This is helpful in times when I have to setup away from my phones and alarm goes off repeatedly and when I get back I am reminded that time’s up. Unlike another timer I downloaded prior to this, it only ring once and if I am away from my phone then I just missed the reminder and lose track of time as that timer then goes into another continuous loop.
2. Love that I can set the “TIMER” to auto repeat. Ie. I set my reminder to drink my water every hour without having to reset or do anything!
3. Love the user interface and the ability to see everything all on one screen without having to scroll through to find what I want. It’s like the screen adjust itself to accommodate for all my different timers I keep adding - all on one screen! 
4. love the ability to have different timers running at different intervals. Ie. If I am working on something that should take 1 hour, but need to break it down then I can set different timers for that and run it all at the same time (Ie. 5 min, 15 min, 7 min, etc…) 

What I would love to see:
1. The ability for the app to act like an alarm even if the phone volume is turned off. I don’t always like to have my phone on for a reason or sometimes forget to turn my phone volume back on in the morning, but then I would miss the reminders on this app. Of course there would need to be a way for people to turn on/off this function because it may not work for everyone. 
2. Wish that there’s a way to still see the timer from my phone while the screen is turned off. 
3. Ringer does not work when using EarPods. 

I see great potential for this app as long as developers continue to work on improving and making it better. So far I am really loving this app and no need to look further.

Improvements:

Currently, the stopwatch starts when you press a button. Then it pauses if you hit it again. Finally, it resets the third time you hit the button
Personally, I wish there was an option to customize this sequence. I wish I could just hit the button to start, and hit it a 2nd time to reset it. I don’t really care what time it measures because I’ll be analyzing it later.

title: Happier Meditation
body:
This app started out great. I still use it every day and have for years, but I really thought about not renewing this February when my annual subscription came due. But I saw that it had rebranded as “Happier“ so I decided to give it a chance. 

I didn’t realize that founder and creative force Dan Harris left over creative differences. I don’t know if that’s why I dislike the new stuff on the app so much, but it doesn’t seem to actually understand mindfulness anymore. And some of the content is squishy and would never have been allowed by Dan. There are these video shorts of people getting interrupted in their daily life and then explaining how they try to be mindful in that moment, and they just don’t work.

I miss Dan’s podcast episodes. I found the new video course almost unwatchable. Because I’ve still got nine more months., I will keep an eye on the app to see if it improves. But I suspect I will be sticking with the Waking Up app and the Plum Village app and dumping this one. There doesn’t seem to be a vision anymore. I’m no longer learning or growing by interacting with this.

body: A key tenet of Buddhism is learning to sit with things that are unpleasant and let them go. That is now my experience with this app. Gone is the serendipity of finding a daily meditation that you didn’t know was exactly what you needed. Instead I get an AI curated list of meditations like “dealing with rage” and “a depressed day”. Those are not issues I’m dealing with so if they had come up as generic options for everyone I would have just moved along. But now those are the options chosen FOR ME specifically. I realize it’s just a machine and not a person accusing me of rage issues, but it still is unpleasant. Maybe they’re trying to give me rage issues!! :) It used to be nice to read the weekly wisdom. That is gone. The fact that the developer says it’s available on the website is useless to me when I’m meditating on my phone. It turns out I was wrong. You CAN set the widget to dark mode in Settings but it is a bit complicated. On the “HomeScreen” page, you have to click on whichever list you want to use (or are already using) for your widget - Small List, Today, Medium List, or Large List. When you click on the list you’ve chosen, a new screen with Options pops up. From the first page of the Options menu, you need to hit “Next” to get to the page where you can change the setting to Dark Mode, although make sure that you have a Source List selected otherwise you won’t be able to move forward to the next screen. On the next screen, there are 3 different ways to set the widget to dark mode. You can toggle the “Auto Dark Mode” button, select“Dark Mode Setting” or select any color for the background and text. Maybe my review should have said, “It would be nice if setting the widget to dark mode were simpler or if could be done from the iPhone Home screen.” If I had gone through the app to add the widget to my Home screen, I might have seen this option at the beginning but since I added the app directly from my Home screen, I didn’t encounter these options in the process of setting it up. body:
*** Update*** I keep losing health and such when I check off tasks instead of gaining it. Its really annoying and just killed me in the app.

title: Habitica: Gamified Taskmanager
body: I adore this app, I use it for every little thing of my day to day life!!! I like the multiple ways you can use it between making habits, having dailies, and the task list. Which I’ll even use for little things like did I pet my cat today, just to boost my motivation a bit. And it’s helped like no other app! Only not possitive thing I’ve experienced is that the interface can be confusing to navigate. Like it’ll take me a few tries before I found the customization screen, or where the pets were. Otherwise I LOVE this app!

title: Habitica: Gamified Taskmanager
body: Habitica is good for staying organized and I like the take they took on this app by making it sort of like a game. I have yet to connect with friends so maybe when I do it will serve as a stronger incentive to stay motivated and get things done. However if there was one thing I can add to this it would be a sort of calendar and or tracking device atleast to see what you have done so far in your past days. For example if I have a habits list that I want to complete for the day I want to be able to look back and see my progression from getting only some done to getting all of them done consistently. I think it would help to see what I have accomplished so far and same things with the habits section so I can see what days I was working more on developing habits and or doing the habits I am not fond of.

title: Habitica: Gamified Taskmanager

title: Habitica: Gamified Taskmanager
body:
Excellent app, I enjoy using it all the time. It color codes your habits and daily tasks to let you know which are no being done. The gamification is a unique feature but it lacks incentives to want you to complete your habits. If there were benefits of having certain pets and mounts it would have been cool. Also there is a lack of quests and rewards. 

The biggest issue for me is the speed of the app, so many times I will complete a task it will lag and not complete. Even after refreshing it and closing the app, it only after a while the app will finally accept the input. The same goes for quest completion and starting, it’s super slow, not sure why that is but it’s super annoying. 

Overall this app has great potential and I still use it all the time. However, it can be far better.

title: Habitica: Gamified Taskmanager
body: As an rpg nerd, There’s nothing like this app to help motivate me and trick me into building better habits and accomplishing my tasks to help me achieve my goal. When it works, I love it. The problem is that the app (and website) are completely reliant on having an online connection to function. So when habitica servers are down, the app is rendered useless. If the company could figure out a way to make the app available regardless of your internet access, I’d give it 5 stars. But till then, this is the best rating o can give to due to constant server interruptions.

title: Habitica: Gamified Taskmanager
body: I have tried almost every todo list, planner, calendar app on the App Store and even Android. This one is my favorite. The gamification is very good, and keeps you coming back. Other apps I get bored with, and few work to keep motivation so they dissolve quickly. The best part of the app to me is Task Value color coding. Just because I do something I need to do daily/weekly once doesn’t make me successful. I like that as I improve (example write recap email daily) the color goes up. If I start skipping or slacking in this area of work/life it goes red. This has helped me improve areas of my work, keeping my from having hard conversations later. I would like to see an Apple Watch app added would be nice. Also a calendar, and some statistics built into the app vs the Data Tool would make this perfect. Please add a calendar, stats, and notes (journaling). Even if you made this part of your subscription plan to access. Would pay for those features. Thanks for a good app.
